move-in.note: to start living in a new home
move-in.tip: move in 后面不直接跟地点；要说搬进哪里用 move into：move into a new flat。搬走是 move out。
move-in.example: We're moving in next Saturday, so the flat is full of boxes.
move-in.en: So, I moved in three weeks ago, and I'm still getting used to the new flat.
move-in.szh: 我是三周前搬进来的，到现在还在适应新家。

more.en: It's their first visit since I moved in.
more.szh: 这是我搬进来以后他们第一次来。

more.en: When I moved in, Mr Patel was the first neighbour to learn my name.
more.szh: 我刚搬来那会儿，街坊里头一个记住我名字的，就是 Patel 先生。

more.en: I've done it every morning since I moved in.
more.szh: 从搬进来那天起，我每天早上都这么干。

more.en: When I moved in with Tom, I had no idea he came from a place like this.
more.szh: 刚搬去跟 Tom 合租的时候，我完全不知道他是从这样一个地方来的。

get-used-to.note: to become familiar with something new so that it no longer feels strange
get-used-to.tip: to 是介词，后面接名词或 doing：get used to living alone，不说 get used to live。
get-used-to.example: It took me a month to get used to working from home.
get-used-to.en: So, I moved in three weeks ago, and I'm still getting used to the new flat.
get-used-to.szh: 我是三周前搬进来的，到现在还在适应新家。

more.en: And after that, you always had it ready, so I just got used to it.
more.szh: 后来你每次都给我提前做好，我也就这么喝惯了。

more.en: It took her a whole year to get used to it.
more.szh: 她花了整整一年才用顺手。

more.en: Anyway, you'll get used to things like that.
more.szh: 反正这种事你慢慢就习惯了。

fall-asleep.tip: fall asleep 说的是「睡着」这一下的变化；go to bed 只是「上床」。过去式 fell asleep。
fall-asleep.example: I fell asleep on the sofa in the middle of the film.
fall-asleep.en: I usually go to bed at eleven and fall asleep in minutes.
fall-asleep.szh: 我一般十一点上床，几分钟就睡着了。

more.en: At one point, I nearly fell asleep.
more.szh: 有那么一会儿，我差点睡着了。

more.en: She was reading her book when the man next to her fell asleep on her shoulder — and started snoring.
more.szh: 她正看着书，旁边的男人靠在她肩上睡着了——还打起了呼噜。

more.en: My interview's at ten, and I can't fall asleep.
more.szh: 我明天十点面试，可怎么都睡不着。

make-sense.note: to have a clear meaning that is easy to understand
make-sense.tip: 「我看不懂」可以说 It doesn't make sense to me，用 to 不用 for；make sense of sth 是「弄懂某事」。
make-sense.example: Your plan makes sense, but it will take a lot of time.
make-sense.szh: 说真的，我完全摸不着头脑。

more.en: It didn't make sense — she never missed a day.
more.szh: 这太奇怪了——她可是一天都没落下过。

more.en: In a small flat, it just doesn't make sense.
more.szh: 房子这么小，做鱼根本不现实。

more.en: I hope this all makes sense.
more.szh: 希望我说清楚了。

w-fast-asleep.note: 这里的 fast 不是「快」，而是「牢牢地」；同样意思还可以说 sound asleep。
w-fast-asleep.en: At two in the morning, I'm always fast asleep.
w-fast-asleep.szh: 凌晨两点，我早就睡得死死的了。

on-purpose.note: because you want to, not by accident
on-purpose.tip: 反义说法是 by accident / by mistake（无意中）；放在句末最自然。
on-purpose.example: Sorry, I didn't delete your file on purpose.
on-purpose.en: So I went downstairs and said, "I'm really sorry, but whatever it is, I'm not doing it on purpose."
on-purpose.szh: 于是我下楼跟她说：「真的很抱歉，可不管是什么动静，我都不是故意的。」

more.en: I didn't do it on purpose — it was just habit.
more.szh: 我不是故意的——纯粹是习惯了。

w-hum.note: 机器、冰箱、蜜蜂发出的低沉而持续的声音；也能当动词：The fridge is humming.
w-hum.en: At exactly two o'clock, I heard a soft hum in the living room.
w-hum.szh: 两点整，客厅里传来一阵轻轻的嗡嗡声。

turn-out.note: to happen in a way you did not expect, or to be discovered to be true
turn-out.tip: 两种常见用法：It turned out (that) + 句子；sth turned out to be + 名词或形容词。
turn-out.example: The meeting turned out to be much shorter than I expected.
turn-out.en: I walked in really slowly, and it turned out to be my new robot vacuum.
turn-out.szh: 我轻手轻脚地走进去，结果发现是我新买的扫地机器人。

more.en: But the real star turned out to be Mr Harris.
more.szh: 不过，真正的明星原来是 Harris 先生。

more.en: It turned out I'd spent an hour complaining to the birthday girl.
more.szh: 原来，我对着寿星本人吐槽了整整一个小时。

more.en: It turned out we had a lot in common.
more.szh: 结果发现我们俩还挺合得来。

more.en: It turned out we'd all thought someone else was going to send it.
more.szh: 原来，我们每个人都以为会有别人发。

more.en: It'll probably turn out to be something small.
more.szh: 多半最后是个小问题。

more.en: "And to my surprise, my house turned out to be an old sweet shop."
more.szh: 「结果没想到，我家以前居然是一家糖果店。」

w-vacuum.note: vacuum cleaner 的简称，robot vacuum 就是扫地机器人；当动词是「用吸尘器吸」：vacuum the floor。
w-vacuum.en: I walked in really slowly, and it turned out to be my new robot vacuum.
w-vacuum.szh: 我轻手轻脚地走进去，结果发现是我新买的扫地机器人。

w-bump.note: bump into sth 撞到东西；bump into sb 还可以表示「碰巧遇见某人」。
w-bump.en: There it was, bumping into the sofa in the dark and cleaning a floor that was already clean.
w-bump.szh: 它就在那儿，黑灯瞎火地一下下撞着沙发，扫着本来就干干净净的地板。

leave-a-note.note: to write a short message and put it somewhere for someone to find
leave-a-note.tip: leave 的过去式是 left；「给某人留言」也可以说 leave sb a note。
leave-a-note.example: If I'm not home, just leave a note under the door.
leave-a-note.en: The next day, I changed the time and left a box of biscuits outside Mrs Wang's door, with a note.
leave-a-note.szh: 第二天，我改好了时间，在王太太门口放了一盒饼干，还留了张字条。

more.en: On Tuesday, I left a note in the lift: "Free bananas — help yourself!"
more.szh: 周二，我在电梯里贴了张字条：「免费香蕉——随便拿！」

more.en: Then I left a note on the ticket for Rachel: "Done. Sorry about the wait."
more.szh: 然后我在工单上给 Rachel 留了句话：「做完了。让你久等了。」

w-shift.note: night shift 夜班，day shift 白班；work shifts 倒班工作。
w-shift.szh: 「我的扫地机器人上的是夜班。」

more.en: She snacks on biscuits all through her night shifts.
more.szh: 她上夜班的时候，饼干一直没离过嘴。

more.en: After a twelve-hour shift, a hot shower is part of a balanced diet.
more.szh: 干完十二个小时的班，洗个热水澡就是均衡饮食的一部分。

w-snore.note: 名词也是 snore；snore loudly 呼噜打得很响。

w-regular.note: 做形容词是「规律的、经常的」：a regular customer；当名词直接说 a regular，是咖啡馆、酒吧的常用说法。
w-regular.en: I run a little café near the station, and most of my customers are regulars.
w-regular.szh: 我在车站附近开了家小咖啡馆，来的大多是熟客。

w-grey.note: 英式拼写是 grey，美式是 gray。in a grey coat 用 in 表示「穿着」：the man in the black jacket。
w-grey.en: There was this woman in a grey coat.
w-grey.szh: 有这么一位女士，总穿一件灰大衣。

in-a-hurry.note: doing something quickly because you do not have much time
in-a-hurry.tip: 中间的 a 不能省：in a hurry，不说 in hurry。「不着急，慢慢来」说 There's no hurry。
in-a-hurry.example: I left the house in a hurry and forgot my laptop charger.
in-a-hurry.en: For two years, she came in at 7:45 every morning, always in a hurry.
in-a-hurry.szh: 整整两年，她每天早上七点四十五分进门，每次都急匆匆的。

more.en: Lesson one: never cook in a hurry.
more.szh: 教训一：做饭千万别急。

more.en: I finished writing my three-line update in a hurry and joined the call at 9:29.
more.szh: 我手忙脚乱地写完三行进度，九点二十九进了视频会议。

w-flat-white.zh: 澳白（一种奶咖，也叫馥芮白）
w-flat-white.note: 浓缩咖啡加一层薄薄的热牛奶，比拿铁奶少、咖啡味浓；点单时说 a flat white, please。
w-flat-white.en: The first time, she ordered a flat white.
w-flat-white.szh: 她第一次来，点了一杯澳白。

w-queue.note: 英式常用词，也能当名词：a long queue；美式多说 line / wait in line。
w-queue.en: After a week, I started making one as soon as I saw her at the door, and she never had to queue.
w-queue.szh: 过了一个星期，我一看见她出现在门口就开始做，她从来不用排队。

pick-up.note: to lift something, or to collect something that is waiting for you
pick-up.tip: 代词要放中间：pick it up，不说 pick up it。开车去「接人」也用它：pick sb up at the airport。
pick-up.example: Can you pick up my parcel from reception on your way in?
pick-up.en: She just smiled, paid, picked it up and ran for her train.
pick-up.szh: 她就笑一笑，付了钱，拿起咖啡就跑去赶火车。

more.en: And when I finally picked up?
more.szh: 等我终于接起来，你猜是谁？

more.en: Then I'm going to pick them up from the airport at three.
more.szh: 然后三点去机场接他们。

more.en: Then she said she'd follow up with the client herself, and picked up the phone.
more.szh: 然后她说她亲自去跟客户沟通，说完就拿起了电话。

more.en: He picks up his phone, just to check the weather.
more.szh: 他拿起手机，说是只看一眼天气。

w-miss.note: miss a day 是「缺一天」；没赶上车是 miss the train。还有「想念」的意思：I miss you。
w-miss.en: It didn't make sense — she never missed a day.
w-miss.szh: 这太奇怪了——她可是一天都没落下过。

w-habit.note: it was just habit = 纯属习惯；也常说 out of habit（出于习惯）。
w-habit.en: I didn't do it on purpose — it was just habit.
w-habit.szh: 我不是故意的——纯粹是习惯了。

find-out.note: to get information about something, often by asking someone or by chance
find-out.tip: find 是「找到（东西）」：find my keys；find out 是「得知消息、弄清真相」：find out why / find out that …。过去式 found out。
find-out.example: I only found out about the meeting from a colleague.
find-out.en: That afternoon, I found out from another regular that she was on holiday in Spain.
find-out.szh: 那天下午，我听另一位熟客说，她去西班牙度假了。

more.en: I think she wants to find out how I really live.
more.szh: 我看她是想摸清楚我平时到底怎么过的。

more.en: Three of our reporters have just found out, and the answer has surprised us all.
more.szh: 我们的三位记者刚刚找到了答案，结果让我们都大吃一惊。

more.en: OK. I'll find out by Friday.
more.szh: 好。周五之前我查出来。

more.en: "Don't bother trying to find out. I spent three weeks trying."
more.szh: 「别费劲去查了。我查了三个星期。」

more.en: Instead, each girl was given a street, and she had to find out about one building on it.
more.szh: 她给每个女孩分一条街，让她去调查街上的一栋房子。

w-tanned.note: 名词是 tan：get a tan 晒出健康的肤色；晒伤是 sunburnt。
w-tanned.en: The next Monday, she was back, and very tanned.
w-tanned.szh: 下个星期一，她回来了，晒得黑黑的。

w-counter.note: 商店、咖啡馆的收银台或取餐台；at the counter 在柜台前。
w-counter.en: Her flat white was waiting on the counter, but this time she didn't pick it up.
w-counter.szh: 她的澳白已经摆在柜台上了，可这回她没去拿。

take-a-deep-breath.zh: 深吸一口气（给自己壮胆、让自己镇定）
take-a-deep-breath.note: to breathe in a lot of air, especially to calm yourself before something difficult
take-a-deep-breath.tip: breath 是名词，读 /breθ/；breathe 是动词，读 /briːð/。take a deep breath = breathe deeply。
take-a-deep-breath.example: I took a deep breath and clicked "Send".

more.en: Tom, my flatmate, was working a double shift, so I took a deep breath and called a locksmith.
more.szh: 室友 Tom 那天连上两个班，我只好深吸一口气，打电话叫开锁师傅。

more.en: So I took a deep breath.
more.szh: 于是我深吸了一口气。

more.en: Take a deep breath, Mia.
more.szh: 深呼吸，Mia。

to-be-honest.note: used before you say what you really think, especially something the listener may not like
to-be-honest.tip: 放在句首，后面加逗号；常用来引出对方可能不爱听的真话，比 Actually 更坦白。
to-be-honest.example: To be honest, I don't think we can finish this by Friday.
to-be-honest.en: "OK, to be honest, I don't really like flat whites," she said.
to-be-honest.szh: 「好吧，说实话，我其实不太喜欢喝澳白，」她说。

more.en: To be honest, I'm a bit nervous.
more.szh: 说实话，我有点紧张。

more.en: To be honest, I still don't feel completely at home.
more.szh: 说实话，我还没完全找到家的感觉。

more.en: Well, she's right, to be honest.
more.szh: 嗯，说实话，她说得没错。

more.en: To be honest, I'm not much better myself.
more.szh: 说实话，我自己也好不到哪去。

more.en: But to be honest, this is the best handover we've ever had.
more.szh: 不过说实话，这是我们有过的最好的一次交接。

more.en: To be honest, I was nervous about joining them.
more.szh: 说实话，跟他们一起参赛我有点紧张。

more.en: To be honest, I paid more attention to the trains than to my bag.
more.szh: 说实话，我光顾着看火车了，没怎么留意包。

more.en: To be honest, my standards went down a bit when I moved in with Tom.
more.szh: 说实话，跟 Tom 合租以后，我的标准是降了点。

more.en: To be honest, you're my only caller tonight.
more.szh: 说实话，今晚就你一个人打进来。

more.en: To be honest, the first week dragged on.
more.szh: 说实话，第一个星期特别难熬。

by-mistake.note: without intending to, because of an error
by-mistake.tip: 反义说法是第 1 课的 on purpose（故意）。by mistake 一般放在动作后面：delete it by mistake。
by-mistake.example: I sent the email to the whole team by mistake.
by-mistake.en: "That first day, I was in such a hurry that I ordered one by mistake.
by-mistake.szh: 「第一次来那天，我太赶了，点错了。

more.en: On Sunday night, I was ordering food online, half asleep, and I typed 50 instead of 5 by mistake.
more.szh: 周日晚上，我迷迷糊糊地在网上买菜，一不小心把 5 打成了 50。

more.en: Sorry, I think you've sent this to me by mistake.
more.szh: 不好意思，你好像发错人了。

more.en: I tested it three times, because I was sure I'd broken something by mistake.
more.szh: 我测了三遍，因为我总觉得自己不小心弄坏了什么。

for-a-change.note: in order to do something different from what you usually do
for-a-change.tip: 常放句末，说「跟平时不一样一回」。别和 change（找的零钱）弄混：Here's your change. 是「找您的零钱」。
for-a-change.example: Let's have the meeting outside for a change.
for-a-change.en: "So... could I have a tea, for a change?"

more.en: Last Sunday, for a change, I asked the questions.
more.szh: 上周日换了个样，轮到我来问她了。

w-lift.note: 英式说 lift，美式说 elevator；电梯坏了常说 isn't working 或 is out of order。
w-lift.en: It was raining, and the lift wasn't working — again.
w-lift.szh: 那天下着雨，电梯偏偏又坏了。

w-slam.note: slam the door 用力把门摔上；过去式双写 m：slammed。
w-slam.en: While I was looking for it in my pocket, the wind slammed my door shut.
w-slam.szh: 我正在兜里摸手机，一阵风「砰」地把门关上了。

w-handle.note: 作动词是「处理」：handle a problem；这里是名词，door handle 门把手。
w-handle.en: I didn't even try the handle.
w-handle.szh: 我连门把手都没试一下。

more.en: And if the handle hadn't been so thick, the clay would have dried evenly.
more.szh: 还有，把手要是没那么厚，泥也会干得均匀些。

w-flatmate.note: 英式说 flatmate，美式说 roommate；在英国 roommate 多指同住一个房间的人。
w-flatmate.en: Tom, my flatmate, was working a double shift, so I took a deep breath and called a locksmith.
w-flatmate.szh: 室友 Tom 那天连上两个班，我只好深吸一口气，打电话叫开锁师傅。

w-locksmith.note: lock（锁）+ smith（工匠），同类的词还有 blacksmith 铁匠。
w-locksmith.en: Tom, my flatmate, was working a double shift, so I took a deep breath and called a locksmith.
w-locksmith.szh: 室友 Tom 那天连上两个班，我只好深吸一口气，打电话叫开锁师傅。

call-back.note: to phone someone again, or to phone someone who called you earlier
call-back.tip: 人称代词放中间：call me back / call you back。「我晚点回你电话」常说 I'll call you back later。
call-back.example: I'm in a meeting — can I call you back in ten minutes?
call-back.en: He was busy, but he promised to call me back.
call-back.szh: 师傅说他正忙，答应一会儿给我回电话。

more.en: There was always a queue, and if the line was engaged, you had to call back later."
more.szh: 那儿老排着队，要是占线，就只能过会儿再打。」

lock-yourself-out.note: to shut a door that locks by accident, with your keys still inside
lock-yourself-out.tip: yourself 跟着主语变：I locked myself out / she locked herself out。「把自己反锁在里面」是 lock yourself in。
lock-yourself-out.example: I locked myself out of the office last night and had to call security.
lock-yourself-out.en: "Did you lock yourself out?" he asked.

more.en: I've locked myself out once — well, sort of.
more.szh: 我还把自己锁在门外过一次——嗯，算是吧。

it-takes-sb-to-do.text: It takes sb + 时间 + to do
it-takes-sb-to-do.note: used to say how much time someone needs to do something
it-takes-sb-to-do.tip: 主语用 It：It took me an hour to …。想用人做主语就换成 sb spent + 时间 + doing，不说 spent … to do。
it-takes-sb-to-do.example: It takes me forty minutes to get to the office.
it-takes-sb-to-do.en: It took him ten minutes to find a ladder, and then it only reached his mum's window.
it-takes-sb-to-do.szh: 他花了十分钟找来一架梯子，结果梯子只够得着他妈妈家的窗户。

more.en: It took Ana twenty minutes to save dinner.
more.szh: Ana 只花了二十分钟就把这顿饭救回来了。

more.en: After all, it only takes ten seconds.
more.szh: 反正也就十秒钟的事。

w-ladder.note: climb a ladder 爬梯子；楼里的「楼梯」是 stairs，别混。
w-ladder.en: It took him ten minutes to find a ladder, and then it only reached his mum's window.
w-ladder.szh: 他花了十分钟找来一架梯子，结果梯子只够得着他妈妈家的窗户。

give-up.note: to stop trying to do something because it is too difficult
give-up.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：give up smoking，不说 give up to smoke；代词放中间：give it up。
give-up.example: Don't give up on the bug yet — let's look at the logs together.
give-up.en: I nearly gave up and went to a hotel, but my wallet was inside too.
give-up.szh: 我差点就放弃了，想去住酒店，可钱包也在屋里。

more.en: And I've given up cooking fish.
more.szh: 还有，我已经不在家做鱼了。

more.en: And don't give up if they ask a hard question.
more.szh: 碰上难题也别轻易放弃。

more.en: It's so slow that I've almost given up.
more.szh: 慢得我都快放弃了。

more.en: But as Rachel says, "Nobody's given up, and nobody's let the client down."
more.szh: 不过就像 Rachel 说的：「没人放弃，也没人让客户失望。」

have-no-choice-but-to.note: to be forced to do something because there is nothing else you can do
have-no-choice-but-to.tip: but to 后面接动词原形：had no choice but to wait。比 have to 更强调「实在没别的办法」。
have-no-choice-but-to.example: The server was down, so we had no choice but to delay the release.
have-no-choice-but-to.en: So I had no choice but to sit on the stairs and wait.
have-no-choice-but-to.szh: 所以我只能坐在楼梯上干等。

more.en: Then I suppose we have no choice but to buy some real ones.
more.szh: 那看来我们只能去买几盆真的了。

in-the-end.note: after a long time, or after a lot of problems
in-the-end.tip: in the end 是「经过一番周折，最后」；at the end of … 是「在……的末尾」：at the end of the meeting。
in-the-end.example: We argued about the design for weeks, but in the end we kept the old one.
in-the-end.en: In the end, the locksmith turned up at five, while I was opening my second packet of biscuits.
in-the-end.szh: 最后，开锁师傅五点才到，那会儿我正在拆第二包饼干。

more.en: In the end, she learned to send voice messages — dozens a day.
more.szh: 后来她学会了发语音——一天几十条。

more.en: In the end, I explained in front of everyone: the "someone special" was an eye specialist.
more.szh: 最后，我当着所有人的面讲清楚了：那个「特别的人」，其实是眼科医生。

more.en: The radio took all morning, but in the end he was able to fix that too.
more.szh: 收音机花了一整个上午，不过最后也修好了。

more.en: So, did you make up with Tom in the end?
more.szh: 对了，你最后跟 Tom 和好了吗？

more.en: In the end, he gets up, goes into the kitchen and picks up his phone — to search "how to stop a clock ticking".
more.szh: 最后，他爬起来走进厨房，拿起手机——搜「怎么让钟不嘀嗒响」。

turn-up.note: to arrive, often late or when people are not sure you will come
turn-up.tip: 口语里常说人「来了、露面了」，常带点「来晚了、没想到会来」的意思；正式一点用 arrive。
turn-up.example: Only three people turned up for the Friday meeting.
turn-up.en: In the end, the locksmith turned up at five, while I was opening my second packet of biscuits.
turn-up.szh: 最后，开锁师傅五点才到，那会儿我正在拆第二包饼干。

more.en: 7:00 p.m. The first guests have turned up — on time, of course.
more.szh: 七点。头一批客人到了——当然是准时到的。

more.en: She was running late for a meeting, and she finally turned up at ten past nine.
more.szh: 她开会眼看要迟到，最后九点十分才赶到。

more.en: Nobody else has turned up yet.
more.szh: 其他人还一个都没到呢。

more.en: Just turn up with whatever's broken.
more.szh: 东西坏了，直接拿过来就行。

more.en: Every Saturday morning, she opened the empty lab and spent three hours answering questions from anyone who turned up.
more.szh: 每个星期六上午，她都会打开空荡荡的机房，谁来了就给谁答疑，一答就是三个小时。

more.en: On average, about twenty people turn up, even in the rain.
more.szh: 平均每次来二十个人左右，下雨也照来不误。

more.en: What pays off isn't the shoes, it's turning up.
more.szh: 真正有回报的不是鞋，而是每次都到场。

more.en: The number 73 finally turned up, and as I stepped on board, the sole split in two.
more.szh: 73 路总算来了，我一脚迈上车，鞋底裂成了两半。

w-packet.note: 英式常说 a packet of biscuits / crisps，美式多说 a package / a bag of …；biscuit 在英式里就是饼干。
w-packet.en: In the end, the locksmith turned up at five, while I was opening my second packet of biscuits.
w-packet.szh: 最后，开锁师傅五点才到，那会儿我正在拆第二包饼干。

by-heart.note: from memory, without needing to read it
by-heart.tip: 常和 know、learn 连用：know sth by heart 背得出，learn sth by heart 把……背下来。
by-heart.example: After a year on the project, I know the release checklist by heart.
by-heart.en: "Well," she said, "I used to know twenty phone numbers by heart.
by-heart.szh: 「嗯，」她说，「那时候我能背出二十个电话号码。

more.en: I know the map by heart now.
more.szh: 线路图我现在都背下来了。

more.en: And he knows everyone's shopping list by heart.
more.szh: 谁家平时买什么，他都记得清清楚楚。

keep-in-touch.note: to continue to talk or write to someone
keep-in-touch.tip: 跟谁保持联系用 with：keep in touch with old colleagues；告别时常说 Let's keep in touch!；get in touch 是「联系上」，是一次性的动作。
keep-in-touch.example: We still keep in touch, even though she left the company last year.
keep-in-touch.en: Her sister lived in Shanghai, and back then, letters were the cheapest way to keep in touch.
keep-in-touch.szh: 她妹妹住在上海，那时候写信是姐妹俩保持联系最省钱的办法。

more.en: Families who've moved away still keep in touch.
more.szh: 搬走的人家，到现在还跟他有联系。

more.en: "I just want people to keep in touch."
more.szh: 「我只是希望大家别断了联系。」

look-forward-to.note: to feel happy about something that is going to happen
look-forward-to.tip: to 是介词，后面接名词或 -ing：look forward to seeing you，不说 look forward to see you。
look-forward-to.example: I'm really looking forward to the team dinner on Friday.
look-forward-to.en: "I used to look forward to the post every morning," she told me.
look-forward-to.szh: 「那时候我每天早上都盼着来信，」她跟我说。

more.en: He always looks forward to their postcards.
more.szh: 他总盼着他们寄来的明信片。

more.en: For two weeks, our app had a bug that nobody was looking forward to fixing.
more.szh: 有两个星期，我们 App 里有个 bug，谁都不想去修。

w-post.note: 英式说 the post，指每天送来的信件，也指邮政：send it by post；美式多说 the mail。
w-post.en: "I used to look forward to the post every morning," she told me.
w-post.szh: 「那时候我每天早上都盼着来信，」她跟我说。

more.en: The post has been piling up by the door since I arrived.
more.szh: 我来了以后，门口的信就越堆越多。

for-ages.tip: 口语说法，正式场合用 for a long time；也常说 take ages：The download took ages.
for-ages.example: I waited for ages for the build to finish.
for-ages.en: "Sometimes I waited for ages for one envelope with her handwriting on it."
for-ages.szh: 「有时候等上好久，才等来一封她亲笔写的信。」

more.en: The smell stays for ages.
more.szh: 那股味儿好久都散不掉。

w-envelope.note: 重音在第一个音节：/ˈenvələʊp/；寄信时信封上要贴 stamp（邮票）。
w-envelope.en: "Sometimes I waited for ages for one envelope with her handwriting on it."
w-envelope.szh: 「有时候等上好久，才等来一封她亲笔写的信。」

more.en: There, a bag of old envelopes costs less than a coffee.
more.szh: 在那儿，一袋旧信封比一杯咖啡还便宜。

more.en: Dad took notes on the back of an envelope lying on the table.
more.szh: 爸爸拿起桌上的一个信封，在背面记笔记。

w-handwriting.note: 不可数名词：Her handwriting is beautiful.；by hand 是「手写地」。
w-handwriting.en: "Sometimes I waited for ages for one envelope with her handwriting on it."
w-handwriting.szh: 「有时候等上好久，才等来一封她亲笔写的信。」

w-tin.note: 英式说法：a biscuit tin 饼干盒，a tin of beans 一罐豆子；美式多说 can。
w-tin.en: She still keeps all those letters in an old biscuit tin.
w-tin.szh: 那些信她到现在还收在一个旧饼干铁盒里。

w-film.note: 常见意思是「电影」；这里指老式相机用的胶卷，作不可数名词。
w-film.en: "Film was expensive," she said, "and it took two weeks to get your pictures back."
w-film.szh: 「胶卷贵啊，」她说，「而且洗一次照片得等两个星期。」

w-dozens.note: a dozen 是「一打、十二个」；dozens of … 泛指「几十个、好多」：dozens of emails。
w-dozens.en: In the end, she learned to send voice messages — dozens a day.
w-dozens.szh: 后来她学会了发语音——一天几十条。

these-days.tip: 和 in those days（那时候）相对；后面常用一般现在时或现在进行时。
these-days.example: These days most of our meetings are online.
these-days.en: "These days I'm in three group chats, and I can't help checking them.
these-days.szh: 「我现在加了三个群，老忍不住要点开看。

more.en: These days, Mum asks me dozens of questions on the phone.
more.szh: 最近我妈一打电话就问我一大堆问题。

can-t-help-doing.note: to be unable to stop yourself doing something
can-t-help-doing.tip: 这里的 help 是「忍住」，不是「帮助」；后面接 -ing：can't help laughing，不说 can't help to laugh。过去式是 couldn't help doing。
can-t-help-doing.example: I can't help checking my work email at the weekend.
can-t-help-doing.en: "These days I'm in three group chats, and I can't help checking them.
can-t-help-doing.szh: 「我现在加了三个群，老忍不住要点开看。

more.en: So yeah, I can't help worrying.
more.szh: 所以啊，我就是忍不住担心。

w-yoga.note: 读 /ˈjəʊɡə/；do yoga 练瑜伽，a yoga class 一节瑜伽课。
w-yoga.en: My online yoga class is starting."
w-yoga.szh: 我的网上瑜伽课要开始了。」

tidy-up.note: to make a place clean and neat by putting things where they belong
tidy-up.tip: 可以说 tidy up the room，也可以说 tidy the room up；代词放中间：tidy it up。英式常用，美式多说 clean up。
tidy-up.example: I need to tidy up my desk before the client visit.
tidy-up.en: OK. In the morning, I'm going to tidy up the living room and sort out the kitchen.
tidy-up.szh: 嗯，明天上午我打算先把客厅收拾一下，再把厨房整理好。

more.en: Then you could tidy up the kitchen together.
more.szh: 然后一起把厨房收拾一下。

more.en: And after every session, everyone had to tidy up.
more.szh: 每次课后，所有人都得把桌面收拾干净。

more.en: Yeah, and I also used to have a mum who tidied up after me every single day.
more.szh: 是啊，那时候我还有个妈天天跟在后面帮我收拾呢。

sort-out.note: to organise something that is untidy, or to deal with a problem
sort-out.tip: 两个意思：整理（sort out the cupboard）和解决（sort out a problem）；代词放中间：sort it out。英式口语 It's sorted. 就是「搞定了」。
sort-out.example: Can we sort out the login bug before the demo?
sort-out.en: OK. In the morning, I'm going to tidy up the living room and sort out the kitchen.
sort-out.szh: 嗯，明天上午我打算先把客厅收拾一下，再把厨房整理好。

more.en: And Mrs Wang's coming over tonight to help me sort out the food.
more.szh: 还有，王太太今晚过来，帮我把吃的弄好。

more.en: Why don't you two sort out a cleaning plan?
more.szh: 要不你们俩排个打扫计划？

more.en: Can you sort it out before the tests finish?
more.szh: 你能在测试跑完之前搞定吗？

more.en: The repair shop took two days and 300 yuan to sort it out.
more.szh: 修理店花了两天、收了 300 块才弄好。

w-bake.note: 烤蛋糕、面包、饼干用 bake；烤肉多用 roast，烧烤是 barbecue。
w-bake.en: I'll vacuum the living room — oh, and I'll bake a cake for your mum!
w-bake.szh: 客厅的地我来吸——哦对了，我再给你妈烤个蛋糕！

w-inspection.note: 动词是 inspect；正式用词，多用于官方检查：a safety inspection。
w-inspection.en: It's a visit, not an inspection.
w-inspection.szh: 她是来看你的，又不是来检查的。

w-cupboard.note: 读 /ˈkʌbəd/，p 不发音。英式常用，美式厨房的柜子多说 cabinet。
w-cupboard.en: When I was a kid, she used to open every cupboard in my room.
w-cupboard.szh: 我小时候，她总要把我房间的柜子挨个打开看一遍。

at-least.note: used to say that a bad situation has one good point; not less than
at-least.tip: 放句首是「好在」：At least nobody was hurt.；放数字前是「至少」：at least ten people。别和 at last（终于）混。
at-least.example: The demo crashed, but at least the client laughed.
at-least.en: Well, at least the plants are still alive.
at-least.szh: 嗯，好歹那几盆植物还活着。

more.en: So, for a short commute, cycling saves time and money — at least when it isn't raining.
more.szh: 所以，路程不远的话，骑车省时又省钱——至少不下雨的时候是这样。

more.en: Well, at least Mum looked thrilled.
more.szh: 好吧，至少妈乐坏了。

more.en: Add a "please", at least.
more.szh: 起码加个 please 吧。

more.en: At least pretend to think about it for a while.
more.szh: 至少也要装模作样想一会儿。

w-plastic.note: 也能当名词：made of plastic；plastic bag 塑料袋。

w-buzz.note: 手机调成振动时「嗡嗡」响就用 buzz；铃声响用 ring。

more.en: Oh, your phone's buzzing.
more.szh: 哎，你手机在震。

be-running-late.note: to be later than you planned
be-running-late.tip: 一般只用进行时：I'm running late，不说 I run late；过去说 was running late。running late 是还在路上、要晚了，I'm late 是已经迟到了。
be-running-late.example: Sorry, I'm running late — start the meeting without me.
be-running-late.en: We wanted to be here for lunch, but we were running late."
be-running-late.szh: 本来想赶过来吃午饭的，结果路上耽搁了。」

more.en: She was running late for a meeting, and she finally turned up at ten past nine.
more.szh: 她开会眼看要迟到，最后九点十分才赶到。

more.en: He's looked after children whose parents were running late.
more.szh: 有的家长来晚了，他就帮忙看孩子。

more.en: It was 8:55 on Saturday morning, and Tom and I were running late for the 9:03 to York.
more.szh: 那是周六早上八点五十五，我和 Tom 眼看要赶不上九点零三分去约克的火车了。

come-over.note: to come to the place where someone is, especially their home
come-over.tip: 说「到说话人这边来」，常指来家里；自己去别人那边用 go over。从国外过来也能用：come over from China。
come-over.example: Do you want to come over for dinner on Friday?
come-over.en: They decided to come over a day early.
come-over.szh: 他们决定提前一天过来。

more.en: And Mrs Wang's coming over tonight to help me sort out the food.
more.szh: 还有，王太太今晚过来，帮我把吃的弄好。

more.en: Afterwards, the CEO came over.
more.szh: 结束后，CEO 走了过来。

more.en: Should we tell him to come over and sit with us on Tuesdays?
more.szh: 要不要让他星期二过来跟我们坐一起？

w-panic.note: 过去式要加 k：panicked；Don't panic! 是「别慌！」。

make-it.note: to succeed in arriving somewhere, especially in time or after a difficult journey
make-it.tip: 后面可以跟地点：make it to the office / make it here；也可以单说 We made it!（赶上了／成功了）。
make-it.example: The train was delayed, but I made it to the interview with five minutes to spare.
make-it.en: Well, at least they made it here safely.
make-it.szh: 唉，至少他们平平安安到了。

more.en: The best one only has six tables, so you have to make it there before seven.
more.szh: 最好吃的那家只有六张桌子，得七点前赶到才有位子。

more.en: On Tuesday I had a terrible headache, so I couldn't make it.
more.szh: 周二我头疼得厉害，就没去成。

w-basically.note: 口语里很常用，意思接近 almost 或「说白了」：It's basically free。重音在第一个音节，ally 读 /li/。
w-basically.en: Well, I moved here two months ago, so I'm basically an expert.
w-basically.szh: 嗯，我两个月前搬过来的，差不多算半个专家了。

get-around.note: to travel from place to place
get-around.tip: 英式也说 get round。get around a problem 是另一个意思：绕开、解决问题。
get-around.example: The easiest way to get around the city centre is by bike.
get-around.en: What's the best way to get around?
get-around.szh: 在那儿出门，怎么走最方便？

more.en: So, what's the fastest way to get around the city in rush hour?
more.szh: 那么，早高峰在城里出行，哪种方式最快？

w-metro.note: 伦敦的地铁叫 the Underground 或 the Tube，美式说 subway；英式里的 subway 是「地下通道」。

w-fortune.note: cost a fortune 是「贵得要命」；fortune 本义是「财富、运气」：tell sb's fortune 算命。

get-lost.note: to become unable to find your way
get-lost.tip: 迷路说 get lost，不说 lost myself。完成时英式说 I've got lost，美式说 I've gotten lost。单说 Get lost! 是「走开」，很不客气。
get-lost.example: I got lost on my way to the client's office and arrived late.

more.en: He's got lost somewhere on the metro.
more.szh: 他在地铁里不知道哪儿迷路了。

more.en: He said getting lost was a good way to get to know people.
more.szh: 他说，迷路是认识人的好办法。

more.en: He was the man who'd got lost with Chen on his first day in London.
more.szh: 就是小陈第一天到伦敦时，跟他一起迷路的那位。

more.en: I left early so that I'd have time to get lost.
more.szh: 我提早出的门，专门留出迷路的时间。

w-loads.note: 口语说法，等于 lots of / a lot of：loads of work、loads of friends；比较随意，正式写作不用。

find-your-way.note: to reach a place by finding the right way to go
find-your-way.tip: your 跟着主语变：find my way / find his way；后面常接 out、home、around 或 to + 地点。
find-your-way.example: It took me a week to find my way around the new office.
find-your-way.en: Once it took me forty minutes to find my way out.
find-your-way.szh: 有一次我转了四十分钟才找到出口。

more.en: Raj finally found his way here at eight, just in time to eat.
more.szh: Raj 八点总算找到了地方，刚好赶上开饭。

try-out.note: to use or visit something new to see if you like it
try-out.tip: 代词放中间：try it out。try on 是「试穿」，别混。
try-out.example: We're trying out a new project tool this month.
try-out.en: I've tried out every noodle shop in the area.
try-out.szh: 这一片的面馆我全都试过了。

more.en: I'm going to try out a new recipe: lemon chicken with rice.
more.szh: 我打算试一道新菜：柠檬鸡配米饭。

w-deal.note: 对方提议时回一个 Deal. 就是「就这么说定了」；问对方同不同意可以说 Deal?

w-pub-quiz.note: 英国酒吧常见的活动：大家组队答各种题，赢了有小奖品；quiz 也指课堂上的小测验。
w-pub-quiz.en: Oh, there's a pub quiz on our street every Thursday.
w-pub-quiz.szh: 哦，我们这条街上的酒吧每周四有问答比赛。

it-s-worth-doing.note: used to say that something is good or useful enough to spend time or money on
it-s-worth-doing.tip: worth 后面直接接 -ing：worth going，不说 worth to go；也可以把东西放主语：The quiz is worth going to。
it-s-worth-doing.example: It's worth spending a little more on a good office chair.
it-s-worth-doing.en: It's worth going, even though we always come last.
it-s-worth-doing.szh: 很值得去，虽然我们每次都垫底。

more.en: It's also worth preparing two good questions for the interviewer.
more.szh: 再准备两个好问题留着问面试官，也很值得。

more.en: If your child takes something apart, it's worth staying calm.
more.szh: 所以要是你家孩子把东西拆了，先别急着发火，这口气忍得值。

feel-at-home.note: to feel comfortable and relaxed in a place
feel-at-home.tip: make sb feel at home 让人感到宾至如归；home 前面不加 my：不说 feel at my home。
feel-at-home.example: My new team made me feel at home on my first day.
feel-at-home.en: To be honest, I still don't feel completely at home.
feel-at-home.szh: 说实话，我还没完全找到家的感觉。

more.en: The funny thing is, for the first time, I really feel at home here.
more.szh: 好笑的是，我头一回在这儿真正有了家的感觉。

more.en: People feel at home faster when they're not alone.
more.szh: 有人陪着，新人会更快觉得自在。

w-brilliant.note: 英式口语里常用来夸人或事情「太棒了」，比 good 强得多；也有「聪明的」意思：a brilliant idea。
w-brilliant.en: Oh, and I've already told my flatmate Tom you're a brilliant cook.
w-brilliant.szh: 哦对了，我已经跟我室友 Tom 说了，你做饭特别拿手。

w-recipe.note: 读 /ˈresəpi/，三个音节，末尾的 e 要读出来。
w-recipe.en: I'm going to try out a new recipe: lemon chicken with rice.
w-recipe.szh: 我打算试一道新菜：柠檬鸡配米饭。

more.en: I know that guy's recipes inside out now, if that helps.
more.szh: 那个人的菜谱我现在倒背如流，要是这能算点什么的话。

make-a-mess.note: to make a place dirty or untidy, or to do something very badly
make-a-mess.tip: make a mess of + 地方或事情：make a mess of the kitchen，make a mess of the presentation（把演讲搞砸）。收拾残局是 clean up the mess。
make-a-mess.example: The builders made a mess of the new office.
make-a-mess.en: I've also made a mess of the kitchen.
make-a-mess.szh: 厨房也被我搞得一团糟。

more.en: The smell has taken over the whole building, and yes, I've made a terrible mess.
more.szh: 整栋楼都是那股香味，没错，我也把厨房弄得一塌糊涂。

w-flour.note: 和 flower（花）读音相同，都读 /ˈflaʊə/；面粉不可数。
w-flour.en: How is there flour on the ceiling?
w-flour.szh: 天花板上怎么会有面粉？

w-ceiling.en: How is there flour on the ceiling?
w-ceiling.szh: 天花板上怎么会有面粉？

more.en: In the summer holidays, I would lie on the kitchen floor for hours, staring at the ceiling.
more.szh: 放暑假的时候，我常常在厨房地板上一躺就是好几个小时，盯着天花板发呆。

set-the-table.note: to put plates, knives, forks and glasses on a table before a meal
set-the-table.tip: 英式也说 lay the table；饭后收拾餐桌是 clear the table。set 的过去式、过去分词都是 set。
set-the-table.example: Could you set the table while I finish the salad?
set-the-table.en: And I haven't set the table yet.

more.en: Or shall I set the table?
more.szh: 要不我去摆桌子？

on-time.note: at the right time, not late
on-time.tip: on time 是按时、不晚；in time 是「及时、来得及」：just in time to eat 正好赶上开饭。
on-time.example: For once, the release went out on time.
on-time.en: 7:00 p.m. The first guests have turned up — on time, of course.
on-time.szh: 七点。头一批客人到了——当然是准时到的。

more.en: Here we are, and on time too.
more.szh: 我们到了，还挺准时。

more.en: The app went live on time, and the new project's on track, isn't it?
more.szh: App 按时上线了，新项目也在按计划推进，对吧？

more.en: Last one: "Arrive on time. Stand-up starts at half past nine."
more.szh: 最后一条：「准时到。站会九点半开始。」

w-oven.note: 读 /ˈʌvn/，o 读 /ʌ/；put sth in the oven 放进烤箱，微波炉是 microwave。
w-oven.en: And the chicken hasn't even gone in the oven yet.
w-oven.szh: 可鸡连烤箱都还没进呢。

more.en: Small problem: my oven isn't working, and it's being repaired tomorrow between ten and one.
more.szh: 有个小问题：我的烤箱坏了，明天十点到一点之间有人来修。

take-over.note: to take control of something from someone else
take-over.tip: take over sth / take sth over 都行；过去式 took over，过去分词 taken over。名词 takeover 是「接管、收购」。
take-over.example: Priya will take over the project while I'm on holiday.
take-over.en: Ana from the design team used to be a chef, and she's just taken over my kitchen.
take-over.szh: 设计组的 Ana 以前当过厨师，她刚刚把我的厨房接管了。

more.en: The smell has taken over the whole building, and yes, I've made a terrible mess.
more.szh: 整栋楼都是那股香味，没错，我也把厨房弄得一塌糊涂。

w-pan.note: frying pan 煎锅；pots and pans 泛指锅碗瓢盆。
w-pan.en: So now I'm washing the pans.

help-yourself.note: to take food or drink without waiting for someone to serve you
help-yourself.tip: 对一群人说 help yourselves；要说拿什么，后面用 to：help yourself to some cake。
help-yourself.example: There's coffee in the kitchen — help yourself.
help-yourself.en: "Help yourselves to bread," I told the others.
help-yourself.szh: 「大家先吃点面包，别客气，」我招呼其他人。

more.en: On Tuesday, I left a note in the lift: "Free bananas — help yourself!"
more.szh: 周二，我在电梯里贴了张字条：「免费香蕉——随便拿！」

more.en: Right, help yourselves!
more.szh: 好了，大家随便吃！

can-t-wait-to.note: to be very excited about something and want it to happen soon
can-t-wait-to.tip: 后面接动词原形：can't wait to see you；也可以接名词：I can't wait for the weekend。
can-t-wait-to.example: I can't wait to see the new office.
can-t-wait-to.en: Everyone says they can't wait to come back.
can-t-wait-to.szh: 大家都说巴不得下次再来。

more.en: Honestly, I couldn't wait to go home.
more.szh: 说实话，我恨不得马上回家。

more.en: He was taking me home to meet his family for a week, and I couldn't wait to see the city.
more.szh: 他要带我回老家见家里人，待一个星期，我早就等不及想去看看那座城市了。

w-dessert.note: 重音在后：/dɪˈzɜːt/；别和 desert（沙漠，重音在前）弄混。英式口语也叫 pudding。
w-dessert.en: I've just opened the fridge and found the dessert.
w-dessert.szh: 我刚打开冰箱，发现了甜点。

w-serve.note: serve dinner 开饭、上菜；餐馆里服务员也用这个词：Are you being served?（有人招呼您吗？）

rush-hour.note: the busy time of day when most people are travelling to or from work
rush-hour.tip: 前面常用 in 或 during：in rush hour / during the rush hour；早高峰是 the morning rush hour。
rush-hour.example: I try not to take the metro in rush hour.
rush-hour.en: So, what's the fastest way to get around the city in rush hour?
rush-hour.szh: 那么，早高峰在城里出行，哪种方式最快？

more.en: I got there after an hour in rush-hour traffic.
more.szh: 晚高峰堵了一个小时，我才到。

w-block-of-flats.note: 英式说法，美式说 apartment building；文中后面简称 the same block。
w-block-of-flats.en: Yesterday at eight, Rob, Nina and Holly left the same block of flats in Northfield and raced to the Town Hall.
w-block-of-flats.szh: 昨天早上八点，Rob、Nina 和 Holly 从 Northfield 的同一栋公寓楼出发，比赛谁先到市政厅。

keep-up-with.note: to move or make progress at the same speed as someone or something
keep-up-with.tip: 跟上速度、进度、变化都能用：keep up with the news；跟不上是 can't keep up with。
keep-up-with.example: It's hard to keep up with all the new Swift features.
keep-up-with.en: "It was hard work keeping up with the other cyclists," he told us.
keep-up-with.szh: 「要跟上别的骑车的人，可真够累的，」他告诉我们。

more.en: I tried to make small talk, but I couldn't keep up with all the in-jokes.
more.szh: 我想跟人寒暄几句，可他们那些内部梗，我一个都接不上。

w-cyclist.note: cycle（骑车）+ -ist；cycling 是骑车这件事：Cycling saves time。
w-cyclist.en: "It was hard work keeping up with the other cyclists," he told us.
w-cyclist.szh: 「要跟上别的骑车的人，可真够累的，」他告诉我们。

w-crowded.note: a crowded train 挤满人的车；crowd 是名词「人群」。
w-crowded.en: Nina's journey was relaxing, but crowded.
w-crowded.szh: Nina 这一路挺轻松，就是挤。

get-stuck.note: to be unable to move, or unable to continue with something
get-stuck.tip: get stuck in traffic 堵在路上；get stuck on a problem 卡在某个问题上。说状态用 be stuck：We're stuck.
get-stuck.example: I got stuck on the same bug for two days.
get-stuck.en: Her taxi got stuck on the bridge for twenty-five minutes.
get-stuck.szh: 她的出租车在桥上堵了二十五分钟。

more.en: "You'll all get stuck," she told them.
more.szh: 「你们都会卡住，」她说，

w-still.note: sit still 坐着不动，stand still 站着不动；常见的副词意思是「仍然」。
w-still.en: "I've never paid so much to sit still," she said.
w-still.szh: 「我还从没花这么多钱，就为了坐着一动不动，」她说。

w-commute.note: 也能当动词：commute to work 通勤上班；通勤的人是 commuter。
w-commute.en: So, for a short commute, cycling saves time and money — at least when it isn't raining.
w-commute.szh: 所以，路程不远的话，骑车省时又省钱——至少不下雨的时候是这样。

save-time.note: to need less time to do something
save-time.tip: save sb time 省下某人的时间：This tool saves us an hour a day。time 前面不加 the。
save-time.example: Using a template saves time when we write release notes.
save-time.en: So, for a short commute, cycling saves time and money — at least when it isn't raining.
save-time.szh: 所以，路程不远的话，骑车省时又省钱——至少不下雨的时候是这样。

more.en: Add a screenshot to save time.
more.szh: 再加一张截图，省时间。

w-newsagent.note: 英国街角卖报纸、零食的小店；the newsagent's 是 the newsagent's shop 的省略，类似 the chemist's（药店）。
w-newsagent.en: He was only going to the newsagent's next to the Town Hall.
w-newsagent.szh: 他只是要去市政厅旁边的报刊店。

on-foot.tip: 交通方式一般用 by：by bike、by taxi、by metro；步行例外，说 on foot，不说 by foot。
on-foot.example: The office is ten minutes from the station on foot.
on-foot.en: He went on foot, took a shortcut through the park and got there second, at 8:40.
on-foot.szh: 他走路去的，抄近道穿过公园，八点四十分到，排第二。

take-a-shortcut.note: to go a quicker or shorter way
take-a-shortcut.tip: 穿过某处用 through，沿着某处用 along。shortcut 还指电脑的快捷键：a keyboard shortcut。
take-a-shortcut.example: We took a shortcut through the car park and got there early.
take-a-shortcut.en: He went on foot, took a shortcut through the park and got there second, at 8:40.
take-a-shortcut.szh: 他走路去的，抄近道穿过公园，八点四十分到，排第二。

w-half-asleep.note: 第 1 课学过 fast asleep（睡得很熟）；half asleep 是困得迷迷糊糊、还没完全睡着。
w-half-asleep.en: On Sunday night, I was ordering food online, half asleep, and I typed 50 instead of 5 by mistake.
w-half-asleep.szh: 周日晚上，我迷迷糊糊地在网上买菜，一不小心把 5 打成了 50。

w-delivery.note: 动词是 deliver；外卖也叫 food delivery；送货员也可以说 delivery driver。
w-delivery.en: The next morning, the lift was broken — again — and a delivery man carried an enormous box all the way up the stairs.
w-delivery.szh: 第二天早上，电梯又坏了，送货小哥扛着一个巨大的箱子，一路爬楼梯送上来。

more.en: Each time, I filled in the delivery form.
more.szh: 每次我都把收货信息填好了。

w-ripe.note: 没熟的是 unripe；香蕉熟透了还可以说 overripe，正适合做香蕉面包。
w-ripe.en: My kitchen is tiny, and ripe bananas go off really fast.
w-ripe.szh: 我的厨房小得可怜，熟透的香蕉又坏得特别快。

go-off.note: (of food) to become bad and no longer good to eat
go-off.tip: 英式说法，过去分词是 gone off；美式多说 go bad。go off 还能指闹钟「响」：My alarm went off at six。
go-off.example: Don't drink that milk — I think it's gone off.
go-off.en: My kitchen is tiny, and ripe bananas go off really fast.
go-off.szh: 我的厨房小得可怜，熟透的香蕉又坏得特别快。

more.en: He gives away any fruit that's starting to go off.
more.szh: 快放坏的水果，他都送人。

get-rid-of.note: to throw away, sell or give away something you do not want
get-rid-of.tip: of 后面接想扔掉、想摆脱的东西：get rid of old files；也能说摆脱问题：get rid of a bug。
get-rid-of.example: I finally got rid of my old laptop.
get-rid-of.en: I had to get rid of them, and quickly.
get-rid-of.szh: 我得把它们处理掉，还得赶紧。

more.en: And now you can't get rid of us.
more.szh: 现在想甩都甩不掉我们了。

more.en: Actually, a lot of them bring things they nearly got rid of.
more.szh: 其实，很多人拿来的都是差点就扔了的东西。

more.en: My wife wants me to get rid of it before Christmas.
more.szh: 我老婆想让我圣诞节前把它处理掉。

more.en: In exactly the colour I wanted to get rid of.
more.szh: 还是我最想甩掉的那个颜色。

give-away.note: to give something to someone for free
give-away.tip: 代词放中间：give them away。give away 还有「泄露（秘密）」的意思：Don't give away the ending!
give-away.example: The company gave away free T-shirts at the conference.
give-away.en: Since then, I've been trying to give them away.
give-away.szh: 从那以后，我一直在想办法把它们送出去。

more.en: He gives away any fruit that's starting to go off.
more.szh: 快放坏的水果，他都送人。

plenty-of.note: a lot of; more than enough
plenty-of.tip: 后面接可数名词复数或不可数名词都行：plenty of bananas / plenty of time；带「足够、还有富余」的意思。
plenty-of.example: Don't worry, we have plenty of time before the demo.
plenty-of.en: Tom's been taking a few to his restaurant, and the café downstairs has taken plenty of them for its smoothies.
plenty-of.szh: Tom 这几天一直往他的餐馆带几根，楼下的咖啡馆也拿了不少去做果昔。

more.en: Even when there's a queue, he's got plenty of time for a chat.
more.szh: 就算有人排队，他也总有工夫跟你聊上几句。

more.en: There's plenty of Roman history under our streets, but coins like this are rarely found by members of the public.
more.szh: 我们的街道底下埋着大量罗马时期的历史，可这样的硬币很少被普通人找到。

w-smoothie.note: 用水果加酸奶或牛奶打成的饮料；milkshake 是加冰淇淋的奶昔。
w-smoothie.en: Tom's been taking a few to his restaurant, and the café downstairs has taken plenty of them for its smoothies.
w-smoothie.szh: Tom 这几天一直往他的餐馆带几根，楼下的咖啡馆也拿了不少去做果昔。

end-up.note: to be in a place or situation in the end, often without planning it
end-up.tip: 后面接 doing 或地点：end up doing sth / end up in Paris，常带「本来没打算这样」的意思。
end-up.example: We ended up working until midnight.
end-up.en: Last night, I ended up baking banana bread.
end-up.szh: 昨晚，我最后干脆烤起了香蕉面包。

more.en: If you don't, we'll end up with nothing.
more.szh: 再这么下去，我们最后什么都吃不上。

more.en: I ended up standing by the snacks, where a woman was eating crisps and checking her phone.
more.szh: 最后我晃到了零食桌旁，那儿有个女人正一边吃薯片一边看手机。

more.en: So we turned back, and somehow we ended up in the car park.
more.szh: 于是我们往回走，结果不知怎么的，走到了停车场。

w-roll.note: a roll of tape / toilet paper；作动词是「滚动」。
w-roll.en: An old roll of baking paper from the back of a cupboard came in really handy.
w-roll.szh: 柜子最里面翻出来的一卷旧烘焙纸，这下可派上大用场了。

w-baking-paper.note: 垫在烤盘上防粘的纸，美式叫 parchment paper。
w-baking-paper.en: An old roll of baking paper from the back of a cupboard came in really handy.
w-baking-paper.szh: 柜子最里面翻出来的一卷旧烘焙纸，这下可派上大用场了。

come-in-handy.note: to be useful, especially when you did not expect it to be
come-in-handy.tip: handy 是形容词「有用的、方便的」，不能写成 come in hand。留着旧东西时常说 It might come in handy.（说不定用得上。）
come-in-handy.example: Those Swift notes came in handy during the interview.
come-in-handy.en: An old roll of baking paper from the back of a cupboard came in really handy.
come-in-handy.szh: 柜子最里面翻出来的一卷旧烘焙纸，这下可派上大用场了。

more.en: He keeps every old screw in a biscuit tin, because "it'll come in handy one day".
more.szh: 每一颗旧螺丝他都留着，装在一个饼干盒里，因为「总有一天用得上」。

more.en: Forty years of teaching history came in handy.
more.szh: 教了四十年历史，这下可派上用场了。

w-loaf.note: 复数是 loaves，f 变成 v 加 es，同类的还有 knife – knives、shelf – shelves。
w-loaf.en: I've baked two loaves so far.
w-loaf.szh: 到现在已经烤了两条了。

stay-in.note: to stay at home and not go out
stay-in.tip: 反义是 go out（出去玩）；也可以说 stay at home，stay in 更口语。
stay-in.example: I'm tired — I think I'll stay in tonight.
stay-in.en: If it rains, we'll stay in and eat on the living room floor.
stay-in.szh: 要是下雨，我们就待在家里，坐在客厅地板上吃。

more.en: I nearly stayed in.
more.szh: 我差点就窝在家里不去了。

it-depends.note: used to say that the answer will change because of something else
it-depends.tip: 说取决于什么用 on：It depends on the weather；单说 It depends. 也行，是一种不把话说死的回答。
it-depends.example: Will the meeting be long? — It depends on the client.
it-depends.en: Well, it depends what people like.

more.en: It depends.
more.szh: 看情况。

more.en: It depends, but a few months is normal.
more.szh: 看情况，不过几个月很正常。

make-up-your-mind.note: to decide something, especially after thinking about it for a long time
make-up-your-mind.tip: your 跟着主语变：make up my mind / his mind；拿不定主意是 can't make up your mind。
make-up-your-mind.example: I can't make up my mind about the new job offer.

more.en: I can't make up my mind!
more.szh: 我实在拿不定主意！

more.en: Rosie, please make up your mind.
more.szh: Rosie，你倒是拿个主意。

w-forecast.note: 完整说法是 weather forecast；作动词是「预测」：Rain is forecast for Sunday。
w-forecast.en: I've been checking the forecast all week.
w-forecast.szh: 我这一个星期一直在看天气预报。

just-in-case.tip: 放在句末最常见：Take an umbrella, just in case.；后面也可以接一句话：just in case it rains。别和 in case of（如果发生……时）混。
just-in-case.example: Save a copy of the file, just in case.
just-in-case.en: I'll bring umbrellas, just in case.

more.en: "Just in case," he said.
more.szh: 「以防万一嘛，」他说。

more.en: They put the coin in a sandwich bag, just in case, and handed it over on Monday morning.
more.szh: 他们把硬币装进一个三明治袋，以防万一，周一上午就交给了我们。

plan-ahead.note: to make plans for something before it happens
plan-ahead.tip: ahead 是「提前、在前面」：think ahead 提前考虑。plan ahead 后面一般不直接跟宾语。
plan-ahead.example: If you plan ahead, release week doesn't have to be stressful.
plan-ahead.en: If we plan ahead, nothing will go wrong.
plan-ahead.szh: 只要提前计划好，就出不了岔子。

more.en: I told you we needed to plan ahead.
more.szh: 我早说了，得提前安排。

more.en: So it's worth planning ahead.
more.szh: 所以最好早做打算。

more.en: So her family have learned to plan ahead.
more.szh: 所以家里人早就学会了提前打算。

w-famous-last-words.zh: 这话说早了；别把话说太满
w-famous-last-words.note: 别人说「肯定没问题」时，半开玩笑地回这么一句：这种话一说出口，往往就要出事。

turn-back.note: to return the way you came, before you reach the place you were going to
turn-back.tip: turn back 是半路掉头往回走；还没出发、或者已经到了再回去，一般用 go back。
turn-back.example: We had to turn back because the road was closed.
turn-back.en: If we turn back now, someone else will get the best spot.
turn-back.szh: 要是现在回去拿，最好的位置就被别人占了。

more.en: So we turned back, and somehow we ended up in the car park.
more.szh: 于是我们往回走，结果不知怎么的，走到了停车场。

w-spot.note: a good spot for a picnic 野餐的好地方；spot 还有「斑点」的意思。
w-spot.en: If we turn back now, someone else will get the best spot.
w-spot.szh: 要是现在回去拿，最好的位置就被别人占了。

w-enormous.note: 比 big 大得多，本身已经是「极大」，前面不加 very。第 9 课送货小哥扛的也是 an enormous box。
w-enormous.en: Look, here's Mrs Wang, with an enormous basket.
w-enormous.szh: 你看，王太太来了，还提着个大篮子。

w-basket.note: picnic basket 野餐篮；shopping basket 购物篮（网购的「购物车」英式也叫 basket）。
w-basket.en: Look, here's Mrs Wang, with an enormous basket.
w-basket.szh: 你看，王太太来了，还提着个大篮子。

more.en: I added the watch to my online basket three times.
more.szh: 我三次把这块表加进了网上的购物车。

w-water.note: water 作动词是「浇水」：water the plants 浇花；作名词才是「水」。
w-water.en: I was watering my plants when I saw you two leave with nothing in your hands.
w-water.szh: 我正在浇花，就看见你们俩两手空空地出门了。

w-days.note: work days 上白班，work nights 上夜班，和第 1 课的 night shifts 对着说：扫地机器人终于改成白天干活了。
w-days.szh: 不上了，它现在改上白班了。

w-vanish.note: 比 disappear 更突然，像凭空不见了一样；vanish into + 地方：一下钻进某处不见了。
w-vanish.en: Marcus said hello and then vanished into the kitchen.
w-vanish.szh: Marcus 跟我打了声招呼，转身就钻进厨房不见了。

make-small-talk.note: to have a polite conversation about unimportant things, especially with people you don't know well
make-small-talk.tip: small talk 是不可数名词，不说 a small talk；「闲聊」的动词用 make，不用 say 或 do。
make-small-talk.example: I'm not good at making small talk with clients before a meeting starts.
make-small-talk.en: I tried to make small talk, but I couldn't keep up with all the in-jokes.
make-small-talk.szh: 我想跟人寒暄几句，可他们那些内部梗，我一个都接不上。

more.en: I'm terrible at making small talk, but she didn't need any help.
more.szh: 我最不会跟人寒暄，可她根本用不着我帮忙。

more.en: First thing in the morning, I make coffee while my flatmate Tom's still asleep, so I don't have to make small talk.
more.szh: 早上一起来，我先煮咖啡，这时候室友 Tom 还在睡，我也就不用跟人寒暄。

w-in-joke.note: 只有一群熟人才听得懂的梗；美式英语说 inside joke。
w-in-joke.en: I tried to make small talk, but I couldn't keep up with all the in-jokes.
w-in-joke.szh: 我想跟人寒暄几句，可他们那些内部梗，我一个都接不上。

feel-left-out.zh: 觉得被冷落；觉得被排除在外
feel-left-out.note: to feel that you are not included in a group or an activity
feel-left-out.tip: left out 是「被落下」的意思，前面用 feel 或 be；「把某人晾在一边」是 leave sb out：Don't leave her out.
feel-left-out.example: New team members often feel left out when everyone talks about old projects.
feel-left-out.en: After ten minutes, I felt left out.
feel-left-out.szh: 才过了十分钟，我就觉得自己被晾在一边了。

more.en: Sometimes I feel left out, as if her other plans matter more.
more.szh: 有时候我觉得自己被冷落了，好像她别的安排都比我重要。

w-crisps.note: 英式英语里 crisps 是薯片，chips 是炸薯条；美式英语里薯片才叫 chips。
w-crisps.en: I ended up standing by the snacks, where a woman was eating crisps and checking her phone.
w-crisps.szh: 最后我晃到了零食桌旁，那儿有个女人正一边吃薯片一边看手机。

more.en: Your knee was fine when you stopped to buy crisps at the corner shop.
more.szh: 你半路停下来去街角小店买薯片的时候，膝盖可好好的。

break-the-ice.zh: 打破沉默；（跟陌生人）打开话匣子
break-the-ice.note: to say or do something that helps people relax when they meet for the first time
break-the-ice.tip: ice 前面一定带 the。主语也可以是一件事：A joke about the weather broke the ice.
break-the-ice.example: Our manager always breaks the ice with a silly question at the start of a workshop.
break-the-ice.en: Then I tried to break the ice: "Have you ever heard worse music?"
break-the-ice.szh: 然后找了个话头：「你听过比这更难听的音乐吗？」

more.en: Smile when you walk in — it always breaks the ice.
more.szh: 进门的时候笑一笑——一笑气氛就松下来了。

to-my-surprise.note: used to say that something was not what you expected
to-my-surprise.tip: 一般放句首，后面加逗号；换人称就换物主代词：to her surprise、to our surprise。介词只能用 to，不说 for my surprise。
to-my-surprise.example: To my surprise, the client liked our first design.

more.en: To my surprise, nobody listened when I tried to explain.
more.szh: 没想到，我想解释，根本没人听。

more.en: Her stories were so funny that, to my surprise, I forgot to be nervous.
more.szh: 她的故事太好笑了，没想到，我连紧张都忘了。

more.en: "And to my surprise, my house turned out to be an old sweet shop."
more.szh: 「结果没想到，我家以前居然是一家糖果店。」

more.en: To his surprise, it wasn't bad at all.
more.szh: 没想到，味道一点都不差。

w-armchair.note: 坐在扶手椅里用 in：sit in an armchair；坐在普通椅子上用 on：sit on a chair。
w-armchair.en: "Never," she said, and pointed at an old man in an armchair.
w-armchair.szh: 「从来没有，」她说着，指了指扶手椅里的一位老先生。

have-a-lot-in-common.note: to share many of the same interests, opinions or experiences
have-a-lot-in-common.tip: 跟谁有共同点用 with：I have a lot in common with her。反过来是 have nothing in common。不说 have many common points。
have-a-lot-in-common.example: My new colleague and I have a lot in common — we both hate long meetings.
have-a-lot-in-common.en: Actually, we had a lot in common.
have-a-lot-in-common.szh: 其实，我们俩有很多共同点。

more.en: It turned out we had a lot in common.
more.szh: 结果发现我们俩还挺合得来。

more.en: He and Chen will have a lot in common.
more.szh: 他和小陈肯定很聊得来。

get-along-with.note: to have a friendly relationship with someone
get-along-with.tip: 英式英语也常说 get on with。后面不跟人时去掉 with：We got along straight away.
get-along-with.example: I get along with my new manager much better than I expected.
get-along-with.en: I got along with her straight away.
get-along-with.szh: 我跟她一下子就聊得来。

more.en: I think I'll get along with them.
more.szh: 我觉得我能跟他们处得来。

w-straight-away.note: 英式口语，和 right away、immediately 意思一样，放在句末。
w-straight-away.en: I got along with her straight away.
w-straight-away.szh: 我跟她一下子就聊得来。

w-birthday-girl.note: 不管多大年纪都可以这么叫，带点亲昵；男的说 birthday boy。
w-birthday-girl.en: "Where's the birthday girl, anyway?" I asked.

w-grin.note: 比 smile 笑得更开，常带点得意或调皮；也能当动词：She grinned at me.
w-grin.en: "Oh, she could be anywhere," she said with a grin.
w-grin.szh: 「哦，那可说不好，哪儿都有可能，」她咧嘴一笑。

w-corner-shop.note: 英国街区里卖日用品、零食和报纸的小店，开得早、关得晚，常常也是街坊的消息中心。
w-corner-shop.en: He's run the corner shop on our street since 1996.
w-corner-shop.szh: 从 1996 年起，他就在我们这条街上开街角小店。

more.en: He leaves his phone in the kitchen and buys a £6 alarm clock from the corner shop.
more.szh: 他把手机留在厨房，又在街角小店买了个 6 英镑的闹钟。

run-a-shop.note: to own or manage a shop and be responsible for it
run-a-shop.tip: run 在这里是「经营、管理」：run a café、run a team 都这么说。open a shop 只是「开张」那一下，说长期经营要用 run。
run-a-shop.example: My aunt runs a small flower shop near the station.
run-a-shop.en: "Running a shop is easy," he says with a grin.

more.en: Mum told my aunt, my aunt told my uncle, and my uncle runs a shop.
more.szh: 妈告诉了姨妈，姨妈告诉了舅舅，而舅舅偏偏是开店的。

w-stock.note: 名词 stock 是「库存」：in stock 有货，out of stock 缺货。
w-stock.en: He gets up at five and stocks the shelves on his own.
w-stock.szh: 他每天五点起床，一个人把货架摆满。

on-your-own.note: alone, or without help from anyone
on-your-own.tip: your 要跟着主语变：on my own、on his own、on our own；意思和 by yourself 一样。
on-your-own.example: I fixed the bug on my own in the end.
on-your-own.en: He gets up at five and stocks the shelves on his own.
on-your-own.szh: 他每天五点起床，一个人把货架摆满。

more.en: I've been doing all the cleaning on my own.
more.szh: 打扫卫生一直是我一个人在干。

more.en: She insisted on finishing everything on her own.
more.szh: 她坚持所有事都要自己做完。

more.en: You got that old build working on your own.
more.szh: 那个旧版本是你一个人弄好的。

take-a-day-off.note: to have a day away from work
take-a-day-off.tip: off 是「不上班」：休一下午是 take the afternoon off，泛说「请假」用 take time off。
take-a-day-off.example: I'm taking a day off on Friday to help my parents move.
take-a-day-off.en: Actually, until last Sunday, he hadn't taken a day off for ten years.
take-a-day-off.szh: 说起来，直到上周日之前，他已经整整十年没休过一天假了。

more.en: Last week I told Mum on the phone that I was taking a day off to see a specialist.
more.szh: 上周我在电话里跟妈说，我要请一天假去看专科医生。

look-after.note: to take care of someone or something and keep them safe and well
look-after.tip: 英式英语里很常用，和 take care of 意思接近；后面直接接人或东西，不加 for。
look-after.example: My neighbour looks after my cat when I'm travelling for work.
look-after.en: He's looked after children whose parents were running late.
look-after.szh: 有的家长来晚了，他就帮忙看孩子。

more.en: And he looks after every broken thing like it's his own.
more.szh: 每一件坏了的东西，他都当自己的一样爱惜。

more.en: Login screen, release notes — Rachel asked me to look after those — and a reply to Arjun.
more.szh: 登录页、发版说明——这个是 Rachel 让我负责的——还有回 Arjun 一条消息。

w-spare.note: spare keys 备用钥匙；spare time 空闲时间；spare room 客房。
w-spare.en: He keeps spare keys for half the street, too.
w-spare.szh: 半条街的备用钥匙也都放在他那儿。

w-wallet.note: 英式英语里，女士用的长款钱包常叫 purse。
w-wallet.en: If you forget your wallet, you don't have to pay straight away.
w-wallet.szh: 忘带钱包也没关系，钱可以回头再给。

more.en: Keep your wallet closed, and see you next time.
more.szh: 把钱包捂紧，我们下期见。

count-on.note: to trust someone to help you or to do what they have promised
count-on.tip: 常见句型 count on sb to do sth；意思相近的还有 rely on、depend on。
count-on.example: You can count on me to finish the report by Friday.
count-on.en: So everyone knows they can count on him.
count-on.szh: 所以大家都知道，有事找他准没错。

more.en: I knew I could count on you for a pep talk.
more.szh: 我就知道找你准没错，你最会给人打气了。

mean-a-lot-to.note: to be very important to someone
mean-a-lot-to.tip: 主语是那件重要的事或那个人：It means a lot to me. 不说 I mean a lot to it。表示感谢也常说 That means a lot.
mean-a-lot-to.example: Your message after the launch meant a lot to the whole team.
mean-a-lot-to.en: The shop means a lot to the street, and the street means a lot to him.
mean-a-lot-to.szh: 这家店对这条街很重要，这条街对他也一样。

more.en: And tell her the friendship means a lot to you.
more.szh: 还要告诉她，这份友情对你很重要。

more.en: Sorry, I know it's a lot, but this job means a lot to me.
more.szh: 不好意思，我知道有点多，可这份工作对我真的很重要。

w-sweets.note: 英式说 sweets，美式说 candy。
w-sweets.en: And kids who used to buy sweets from him now bring their own kids.
w-sweets.szh: 当年在他这儿买糖的小孩，现在都带着自己的孩子来了。

w-seaside.note: go to the seaside 是英国人常说的「去海边玩一天」，比 the beach 更有出游的味道。
w-seaside.en: Anyway, last Sunday the whole street closed the shop and took him to the seaside.
w-seaside.szh: 总之，上周日，整条街的人把店一关，拉着他去了海边。

be-nervous-about.note: to feel worried and a little afraid about something that is going to happen
be-nervous-about.tip: about 后面接名词或 doing：nervous about the interview / about speaking。说「让人紧张的事」不用 nervous，用 stressful：a stressful day。
be-nervous-about.example: I'm always nervous about speaking English in big meetings.
be-nervous-about.en: Jess, I'm so nervous about tomorrow!

more.en: I was so nervous about it that I couldn't sleep the night before.
more.szh: 我紧张得前一天晚上都没睡着。

more.en: I'm just really nervous about the deadline.
more.szh: 主要是截止日期快到了，我特别紧张。

more.en: To be honest, I was nervous about joining them.
more.szh: 说实话，跟他们一起参赛我有点紧张。

w-weakness.note: 面试常问 What are your strengths and weaknesses?（你有什么长处和短处）。
w-weakness.en: What if they ask about my weaknesses?
w-weakness.szh: 要是他们问我有什么缺点，怎么办？

calm-down.note: to stop feeling upset, angry or nervous
calm-down.tip: 对正在气头上的人直接说 Calm down! 常常适得其反；温和一点可以说 Don't worry 或 Take your time。
calm-down.example: Let's all calm down and look at the logs again.

more.en: So calm down first, and then talk to her face to face.
more.szh: 所以先让自己冷静下来，再当面跟她谈。

more.en: OK, calm down.
more.szh: 好啦，别急。

w-interviewer.note: -er 是提问的人，-ee 是被问的人：interviewer 面试官，interviewee 面试者。
w-interviewer.en: It's also worth preparing two good questions for the interviewer.
w-interviewer.szh: 再准备两个好问题留着问面试官，也很值得。

give-it-a-try.note: to try doing something to see if it works or if you like it
give-it-a-try.tip: it 指要试的那件事；英式口语也常说 give it a go，美式常说 give it a shot。
give-it-a-try.example: The new framework looks hard, but let's give it a try.
give-it-a-try.en: Good idea, I'll give it a try.

more.en: Just give it a try — twenty minutes on the sofa.
more.szh: 就试一下——在沙发上躺二十分钟。

more.en: OK, I'll give it a try.
more.szh: 好，我试试。

w-iron.note: 名词是「熨斗」，也是「铁」；读 /ˈaɪən/，r 不发音。

more.en: It's made of iron, and it's older than me.
more.szh: 是口铁锅，岁数比我还大。

w-pep-talk.note: 别人紧张、泄气时的一番鼓励；give sb a pep talk 给某人打气。
w-pep-talk.en: Thanks for the pep talk, stranger!
w-pep-talk.szh: 谢谢你给我打气，陌生人！

w-stranger.note: 直接管对方叫 stranger，是熟络的玩笑口吻，像中文的「这位陌生朋友」。
w-stranger.en: Thanks for the pep talk, stranger!
w-stranger.szh: 谢谢你给我打气，陌生人！

wish-sb-luck.note: to say that you hope someone will be successful
wish-sb-luck.tip: 考试、面试、比赛之前常说 Wish me luck!；回一句 Good luck! 最自然，I wish you good luck 听起来偏正式。
wish-sb-luck.example: We all wished her luck before her first big presentation.

more.en: Wish me luck!
more.szh: 祝我好运吧！

w-zombie.note: 口语里形容人没睡好、无精打采：I'm a zombie this morning.
w-zombie.en: If you don't, you'll look like a zombie.
w-zombie.szh: 不然明天你就跟个僵尸似的。

go-well.note: to happen in the way that you hoped
go-well.tip: 主语是事情，不是人：The interview went well，不说 I went well。问「怎么样了」用 How did it go?
go-well.example: How did the demo go? — Really well, thanks.
go-well.en: It went well — I got the job!
go-well.szh: 面试很顺利——我被录用了！

more.en: "So did it go well?" Mum asked at last.
more.szh: 「那……看得顺利吗？」妈终于开口问。

make-sure.note: to do or check something so that you are certain it happens
make-sure.tip: 后面直接接句子：make sure you …；提醒别人时放句首，语气比 must 柔和。
make-sure.example: Make sure you save your work before the update.
make-sure.en: Make sure you thank Jess for her great advice.
make-sure.szh: 记得好好谢谢 Jess 的「金玉良言」哦。

more.en: And make sure you call, not text.
more.szh: 记得是打电话，别发消息。

more.en: Anyway, make sure there are no mistakes before you send it.
more.szh: 总之，发之前检查一下有没有写错。

more.en: Can someone make sure login works?
more.szh: 谁确认一下登录能用了没？

w-profile-picture.note: 聊天软件、社交软件里的头像，口语常缩成 profile pic。
w-profile-picture.en: Wait, is that you in your profile picture?
w-profile-picture.szh: 等等，你头像上那个是你吗？

fall-out-with.note: to argue with someone and stop being friendly with them
fall-out-with.tip: 过去式 fell out，过去分词 fallen out；闹翻的原因用 over 或 about：fall out with sb over money。
fall-out-with.example: She fell out with her manager over the new deadline.

more.en: I don't want to fall out with her.
more.szh: 我不想跟她闹翻。

w-row.note: 这个意思读 /raʊ/，和 cow 押韵；读 /rəʊ/ 是「一排」。have a row with sb 跟某人吵架。

more.en: Yes, Freya, I can hear you clapping in the front row.
more.szh: 是的，Freya，我听见你在第一排鼓掌了。

w-sink.note: 动词 sink 是「下沉」：The boat sank。
w-sink.en: He leaves dirty pans in the sink for days, and it really gets on my nerves.
w-sink.szh: 他老把脏锅扔在水槽里，一放就是好几天，烦死我了。

get-on-sb-s-nerves.note: to annoy someone, especially by doing something again and again
get-on-sb-s-nerves.tip: sb's 要换成具体的人：gets on my nerves、gets on her nerves；主语是让人烦的那个人或那件事。
get-on-sb-s-nerves.example: The noise from the building site is starting to get on my nerves.
get-on-sb-s-nerves.en: He leaves dirty pans in the sink for days, and it really gets on my nerves.
get-on-sb-s-nerves.szh: 他老把脏锅扔在水槽里，一放就是好几天，烦死我了。

more.en: But her excuses are starting to get on my nerves.
more.szh: 可她那些借口越来越让我心烦。

w-face-to-face.note: 放在名词前要加连字符：a face-to-face meeting。
w-face-to-face.en: You should have talked to him face to face.

take-it-personally.zh: 往心里去；觉得是冲着自己来的
take-it-personally.note: to feel that someone's words or actions are an attack on you, when they may not be
take-it-personally.tip: 多用在否定句里：Don't take it personally（别往心里去）；中间的 it 不能省。
take-it-personally.example: The client didn't like the design, but don't take it personally.
take-it-personally.en: Don't take it personally — he's exhausted, not lazy.
take-it-personally.szh: 别往心里去——他是累坏了，不是懒。

more.en: Am I taking it too personally?
more.szh: 是不是我太往心里去了？

w-exhausted.note: 比 tired 程度重得多；前面不再加 very，要加强就说 completely exhausted。
w-exhausted.en: Don't take it personally — he's exhausted, not lazy.
w-exhausted.szh: 别往心里去——他是累坏了，不是懒。

see-sb-s-point.zh: 明白某人的意思；觉得某人说得有道理
see-sb-s-point.note: to understand why someone thinks something, and accept that they may be right
see-sb-s-point.tip: 常用来先认同、再说不同意见：I see your point, but …；「同意你的观点」不说 agree your point。
see-sb-s-point.example: I see your point, but we still need to finish the tests first.

more.en: All right, I see your point.
more.szh: 好吧，你说得在理。

more.en: I see your point, but a reminder only works if somebody reads it.
more.szh: 你说得有道理，可提醒也得有人看才管用。

make-up-with.note: to become friends with someone again after an argument
make-up-with.tip: 正好是本课 fall out with 的反义；后面不跟人时直接说 make up：They've made up.
make-up-with.example: Have you made up with your brother yet?
make-up-with.en: Well, you should make up with him before the weekend.
make-up-with.szh: 那你赶在周末之前得跟他和好。

more.en: So, did you make up with Tom in the end?
more.szh: 对了，你最后跟 Tom 和好了吗？

w-capital-letters.note: 也叫 capitals 或 caps；小写字母是 small letters 或 lower case。

apologise-for.note: to say sorry for something you have done
apologise-for.tip: 向谁道歉用 to：apologise to Tom for the message。英式拼写 apologise，美式 apologize。
apologise-for.example: I apologise for the late reply — I was on holiday.
apologise-for.en: Then you should apologise for the capital letters.
apologise-for.szh: 那你就该为那些大写字母道歉。

more.en: I apologised for the capital letters, and now he even washes his own pans.
more.szh: 我为那些大写字母道了歉，现在他连自己的锅都自己洗了。

w-yoghurt.note: 英式拼法 yoghurt，美式 yogurt；一盒酸奶是 a pot of yoghurt。
w-yoghurt.en: My flatmate's been eating my yoghurt for weeks, so last night I sent her a very long message.
w-yoghurt.szh: 我室友偷吃我的酸奶好几个星期了，所以昨晚我给她发了一条超长的消息。

w-specialist.note: see a specialist 看专科医生；an eye specialist 眼科医生。重音在第一个音节：SPE-cial-ist。
w-specialist.en: Last week I told Mum on the phone that I was taking a day off to see a specialist.
w-specialist.szh: 上周我在电话里跟妈说，我要请一天假去看专科医生。

w-line.note: The line is bad. 信号不好；The line is busy. 占线。
w-line.en: The line was bad, so she must have heard "someone special".
w-line.szh: 电话信号不好，她肯定是把 specialist（专科医生）听成了 someone special（一个特别的人）。

word-gets-around.zh: 消息传开；一传十，十传百
word-gets-around.note: used to say that news spreads quickly from person to person
word-gets-around.tip: word 在这里是不可数名词，指「消息、传言」，前面不加 a 或 the；说过去的事用 word got around。
word-gets-around.example: Word got around that the company was moving offices.
word-gets-around.en: Well, word gets around fast in my family.
word-gets-around.szh: 嗯，在我们家，消息传得飞快。

more.en: Well, word has got around, and people now come from three towns away.
more.szh: 这下名声传开了，现在连隔着三个镇的人都专门跑来。

w-doubt.note: b 不发音，读 /daʊt/；have doubts about sth 对某事有疑问。
w-doubt.en: Only my sister Lily had doubts.
w-doubt.szh: 只有我妹妹 Lily 不信。

w-curtains.note: 一般用复数，因为窗帘多是两片；拉上窗帘是 draw the curtains。
w-curtains.en: "He can't have found a girlfriend — he hasn't even bought curtains yet."
w-curtains.szh: 「他不可能找到女朋友——他连窗帘都还没买呢。」

get-the-wrong-idea.tip: 误会的对象用 about：get the wrong idea about sb。英式过去分词是 got，美式是 gotten。
get-the-wrong-idea.example: Don't get the wrong idea — I'm only asking because I need help.
get-the-wrong-idea.en: By Sunday's video call, the whole family had got the wrong idea.
get-the-wrong-idea.szh: 到了周日视频通话的时候，全家人都想歪了。

more.en: And they might have got the wrong idea about our team.
more.szh: 说不定还对我们团队有了误会。

more.en: I don't want anyone to get the wrong idea, so here's the plan.
more.szh: 我不想让大家误会，所以先把安排说清楚。

set-sb-up-with.note: to arrange for two people to meet because you hope they will start a romantic relationship
set-sb-up-with.tip: 人放在 set 和 up 中间：set me up with her；被人介绍是 be set up with sb。
set-sb-up-with.example: My colleague keeps trying to set me up with her cousin.
set-sb-up-with.en: My uncle even offered to set me up with his friend's daughter.
set-sb-up-with.szh: 舅舅还说要把他朋友的女儿介绍给我。

more.en: Stop trying to set Mei up with your cousin.
more.szh: 别老想着把你表弟介绍给 Mei。

make-a-fuss.note: to get too excited or worried about something, often in a noisy way
make-a-fuss.tip: 为某事大惊小怪用 about：make a fuss about sth；make a fuss of sb（英式）则是「对某人格外殷勤」。
make-a-fuss.example: Please don't make a fuss — it's only my birthday.
make-a-fuss.szh: 大家七嘴八舌，闹成一团。

more.en: She hates it when people make a fuss about her birthday.
more.szh: 她最烦别人为她过生日大张旗鼓了。

more.en: And she never made a fuss, which somehow made it worse.
more.szh: 她也从来没为这事说过什么，不知怎么的，这反而更难受。

in-front-of.note: where someone can see or hear you; in a position before someone or something
in-front-of.tip: 别和 in the front of 搞混：in front of the car 在车的前方（车外），in the front of the car 在车里的前排。
in-front-of.example: I hate giving feedback in front of the whole team.
in-front-of.en: In the end, I explained in front of everyone: the "someone special" was an eye specialist.
in-front-of.szh: 最后，我当着所有人的面讲清楚了：那个「特别的人」，其实是眼科医生。

more.en: Mr Okafor managed to fix the toaster in ten minutes, in front of a small crowd.
more.szh: 当着一小群围观的人，Okafor 先生十分钟就把烤面包机修好了。

more.en: And please don't bring up the vegetarian thing in front of Gran.
more.szh: 还有，千万别在奶奶面前提吃素的事。

w-silence.note: 形容词是 silent；in silence 默默地。

w-mumble.note: 说得小声又不清楚，常因为害羞或不好意思；比较 whisper 是有意压低声音说悄悄话。

keep-a-secret.note: to not tell other people something that you have been asked not to tell
keep-a-secret.tip: 要别人替某件事保密，说 keep it a secret（it 指那件事）；也可以说 keep sth secret，不加 a。
keep-a-secret.example: Can you keep a secret? I'm leaving the company in June.

more.en: Can you keep a secret?
more.szh: 能替我保密吗？

more.en: Well, she's terrible at keeping secrets.
more.szh: 可问题是，她最守不住秘密了。

keep-sb-waiting.note: to make someone wait, usually because you are late
keep-sb-waiting.tip: 人放在中间：keep me waiting；道歉常说 Sorry to keep you waiting 或 Sorry I kept you waiting。
keep-sb-waiting.example: Sorry to keep you waiting — the last meeting ran over.
keep-sb-waiting.en: She keeps me waiting for half an hour, sometimes a whole hour.
keep-sb-waiting.szh: 她一让我等就是半小时，有时候整整一小时。

more.en: I mean, we'd kept the client waiting all weekend!
more.szh: 要知道，我们让客户白等了一整个周末啊！

more.en: Then a user wrote, "Still waiting. Please don't keep us waiting until Christmas."
more.szh: 后来有个用户留言：「还在等。别让我们等到圣诞节啊。」

w-excuse.note: 名词读 /ɪkˈskjuːs/，动词读 /ɪkˈskjuːz/；make an excuse 找借口。
w-excuse.en: And she's always got an excuse.

more.en: "Didn't notice. But my flatmate used it as an excuse not to do the washing-up all weekend.
more.szh: 「我没注意到。不过我室友拿它当借口，整个周末都没洗碗。

w-punctual.note: 名词是 punctuality；口语里也常说 always on time。
w-punctual.en: I'm very punctual, so I usually get there first.
w-punctual.szh: 我特别守时，所以一般都是我先到。

let-sb-down.note: to not do what someone trusted or expected you to do
let-sb-down.tip: 人放在中间：let me down；过去式、过去分词都是 let。名词 a letdown 是「令人失望的事」。
let-sb-down.example: The team is counting on me, and I don't want to let them down.
let-sb-down.en: Last Saturday she let me down again.

more.en: I was sure I'd let the team down.
more.szh: 我当时觉得，肯定是我拖了大家后腿。

more.en: But as Rachel says, "Nobody's given up, and nobody's let the client down."
more.szh: 不过就像 Rachel 说的：「没人放弃，也没人让客户失望。」

lose-your-temper.tip: your 跟着主语变：lost my temper、lost his temper；反过来「忍住不发火」是 keep your temper。
lose-your-temper.example: He lost his temper when the build failed for the fifth time.
lose-your-temper.en: We missed the start of a film, and I nearly lost my temper in the queue.
lose-your-temper.szh: 电影开头没赶上，排队的时候我差点发火。

more.en: But Rachel didn't lose her temper.
more.szh: 可 Rachel 没发火。

be-fed-up-with.note: to be annoyed or bored with something that has gone on for too long
be-fed-up-with.tip: with 后面接让人烦的事，也可以接 doing：fed up with waiting；口语里常单说一句 I'm fed up.
be-fed-up-with.example: I'm fed up with meetings that could have been an email.
be-fed-up-with.en: Maybe I shouldn't have got so angry, but I'm fed up with it.
be-fed-up-with.szh: 也许我不该那么生气，可我真的受够了。

more.en: She must be fed up with us.
more.szh: 她肯定被我们烦死了。

more.en: "I'm so fed up with myself," she said.
more.szh: 「我真受够我自己了，」她说。

more.en: Sorry, you must be fed up with my lists by now.
more.szh: 不好意思，我的清单你大概早就听烦了。

w-matter.note: 当动词用，主语是事情：It doesn't matter.（没关系）不要说 It's not matter。
w-matter.en: No, you're not — your time matters too.
w-matter.szh: 没有——你的时间也很宝贵。

w-upset.note: 比 angry 轻，多指心里难受；get upset 变得不高兴。
w-upset.en: If I say something, she'll get upset.
w-upset.szh: 我要是说了，她会不高兴的。

be-honest-with.note: to tell someone the truth, even when it is difficult
be-honest-with.tip: 对谁坦诚用 with，不用 to；honest 的 h 不发音，前面用 an：an honest answer。
be-honest-with.example: To be honest with you, I don't think the plan will work.
be-honest-with.en: If I were you, I'd be honest with her.
be-honest-with.szh: 换我是你，我就跟她直说。

more.en: Now be honest with me.
more.szh: 你老实跟我说，

on-the-other-hand.note: used to introduce a different or opposite point
on-the-other-hand.tip: 可以和 on the one hand 前后呼应，但单独用更常见；中间的 the 别漏掉。
on-the-other-hand.example: The job pays well. On the other hand, the hours are long.
on-the-other-hand.en: On the other hand, if you lost your temper, she'd only defend herself.
on-the-other-hand.szh: 反过来，你要是冲她发火，她只会急着替自己辩解。

more.en: "On the other hand, I can't make a decision about the login screen without the latest version."
more.szh: 「不过话说回来，没有最新版本，登录页的事我没法做决定。」

w-defend.note: defend yourself 为自己辩解；名词英式拼 defence，美式拼 defense。
w-defend.en: On the other hand, if you lost your temper, she'd only defend herself.
w-defend.szh: 反过来，你要是冲她发火，她只会急着替自己辩解。

w-friendship.note: -ship 表示关系或状态，同类的词还有 relationship、partnership。
w-friendship.en: And tell her the friendship means a lot to you.
w-friendship.szh: 还要告诉她，这份友情对你很重要。

w-volunteer.note: 也能当动词：volunteer at a library 在图书馆做志愿者。重音在最后：vol-un-TEER。
w-volunteer.en: Volunteers fix things that people would normally throw away, and they do it for free.
w-volunteer.szh: 志愿者帮大家修那些本来要扔掉的东西，而且一分钱不收。

more.en: A busy volunteer sold her a box of old postcards for £2.
more.szh: 一位忙得团团转的志愿者，2 英镑就把一盒旧明信片卖给了她。

throw-away.note: to get rid of something you don't want, usually by putting it in the bin
throw-away.tip: 代词放中间：throw it away；它说的就是「扔进垃圾桶」，比 get rid of 具体。
throw-away.example: Don't throw away the box — we might need it for returns.
throw-away.en: Volunteers fix things that people would normally throw away, and they do it for free.
throw-away.szh: 志愿者帮大家修那些本来要扔掉的东西，而且一分钱不收。

more.en: He made forty slides and threw away half of them.
more.szh: 他做了四十页，又删掉了一半。

for-free.note: without having to pay, or without being paid
for-free.tip: for free 放在动词后面：work for free、get it for free；当形容词直接说 free：The app is free.
for-free.example: You can use the app for free for the first month.
for-free.en: Volunteers fix things that people would normally throw away, and they do it for free.
for-free.szh: 志愿者帮大家修那些本来要扔掉的东西，而且一分钱不收。

more.en: So a farmer took her to the church on his tractor — for free.
more.szh: 结果一个农民开着拖拉机把她送到了教堂——一分钱没要。

w-retired.note: 动词 retire 退休，名词 retirement 退休（生活）。
w-retired.en: The most popular volunteer is Mr Okafor, a retired engineer.
w-retired.szh: 最受欢迎的志愿者是 Okafor 先生，一位退休工程师。

more.en: One of those students is Pauline Hall, a sixty-seven-year-old retired bus driver.
more.szh: 其中一位学生是 Pauline Hall，今年六十七岁，是位退休的公交车司机。

w-screw.note: 螺丝刀是 screwdriver；动词 screw 是「拧」。
w-screw.en: He can fix anything with a screw or a battery.
w-screw.szh: 只要带螺丝或者电池的东西，他都能修。

more.en: I kept every screw in a teacup.
more.szh: 每颗螺丝我都收在一个茶杯里。

w-toaster.note: toast 烤面包片，-er 表示做这件事的机器，同类的还有 printer、heater。
w-toaster.en: Last week, a woman brought in a toaster that broke down after just one week.
w-toaster.szh: 上周，一位女士拿来一台烤面包机，才用了一个星期就坏了。

more.en: I even gave the toaster to my neighbour.
more.szh: 连烤面包机都送给了邻居。

break-down.note: to stop working, used about machines and cars
break-down.tip: 主语是机器或车，后面不接宾语；名词 a breakdown 是「故障」。
break-down.example: Our car broke down on the way to the airport.
break-down.en: Last week, a woman brought in a toaster that broke down after just one week.
break-down.szh: 上周，一位女士拿来一台烤面包机，才用了一个星期就坏了。

more.en: Once, her car broke down on her wedding day.
more.szh: 有一回，她结婚那天车坏在了半路。

w-late.note: 放在名词前、指人时是「已故的」：my late grandmother。别和第 16 课「迟到」的 late 搞混。
w-late.en: A man brought his late father's fifty-year-old radio.
w-late.szh: 还有一位男士，带来了他已故父亲留下的一台五十年的老收音机。

w-crowd.note: a small crowd 一小群人；crowded 拥挤的。
w-crowd.en: Mr Okafor managed to fix the toaster in ten minutes, in front of a small crowd.
w-crowd.szh: 当着一小群围观的人，Okafor 先生十分钟就把烤面包机修好了。

give-sb-a-hand.note: to help someone, especially with a practical job
give-sb-a-hand.tip: 人放在 give 后面：give me a hand；帮着做什么用 with：give sb a hand with sth。
give-sb-a-hand.example: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?
give-sb-a-hand.en: Younger volunteers who want to learn give him a hand.
give-sb-a-hand.szh: 想学手艺的年轻志愿者会给他打下手。

more.en: Tom, could you give me a hand with an email?
more.szh: Tom，能帮我看看一封邮件吗？

more.en: On Monday, I asked Maya to give me a hand with my demo.
more.szh: 周一，我请 Maya 帮我弄一下我的演示。

more.en: "When something was urgent, people still gave each other a hand."
more.szh: 「真有急事的时候，大家照样互相搭把手。」

be-proud-of.note: to feel pleased and satisfied about something you have done or own
be-proud-of.tip: of 后面接让人自豪的事或人，也可以接 doing：proud of finishing on time。
be-proud-of.example: I'm really proud of the app we built this year.
be-proud-of.en: He's proud of every single repair.
be-proud-of.szh: 每修好一件，他都很自豪。

more.en: She was clearly proud of him.
more.szh: 看得出来，她特别为这个孙子骄傲。

more.en: Thank you, everyone — I'm so proud of this team.
more.szh: 谢谢大家——我真为这个团队骄傲。

as-good-as-new.note: in very good condition again, almost like something new
as-good-as-new.tip: 常跟 be、look、work 连用：It looks as good as new.
as-good-as-new.example: After the repair, my laptop is as good as new.
as-good-as-new.en: "If you do it properly, it's as good as new," he says.

more.en: Every time I fix one screen, it's as good as new.
more.szh: 每次修好一个页面，看着是彻底没毛病了。

w-otherwise.note: 常放句首，意思相当于 if not：Hurry, otherwise we'll miss the train.
w-otherwise.szh: 「不然大家会在这儿待上一整天。」

w-rubber-gloves.note: 洗碗、打扫时戴的手套；rubber 是橡胶，也指橡皮擦（英式）。
w-rubber-gloves.en: Right, where are your rubber gloves?
w-rubber-gloves.szh: 好了，你的橡胶手套在哪儿？

w-absolutely.note: 单说 Absolutely! 是「当然！」；Absolutely not 是「绝对不行」。
w-absolutely.en: Absolutely not — you've just done four night shifts in a row.
w-absolutely.szh: 想都别想——你刚连上了四个夜班。

take-care-of.note: to look after someone or something
take-care-of.tip: 和第 12 课的 look after 意思接近；take care of 还能指「处理（事情）」：I'll take care of the bill。不带 of 的 Take care! 是告别语「保重」。
take-care-of.example: My parents take care of our son on Fridays.
take-care-of.en: This weekend, I'm taking care of you.

more.en: I'll take care of the dessert — she loves chocolate.
more.szh: 甜点我来管——她爱吃巧克力。

put-your-feet-up.note: to sit down and relax, often with your feet resting on something
put-your-feet-up.tip: your 跟着主语变：put my feet up；不一定真的把脚翘起来，意思就是「放松休息」。
put-your-feet-up.example: After the release, I went home and put my feet up.
put-your-feet-up.en: Could you just sit down and put your feet up?
put-your-feet-up.szh: 你就坐下来，把脚跷起来歇会儿，行吗？

more.en: Put your feet up and don't open your laptop.
more.szh: 好好歇着，别碰电脑。

feel-like-doing.zh: 想（做某事）；有心情（做某事）
feel-like-doing.note: to want to do something at a particular moment
feel-like-doing.tip: like 是介词，后面接 doing 或名词：feel like going out，不说 feel like to go。
feel-like-doing.example: I don't feel like cooking tonight — let's order pizza.
feel-like-doing.en: You know I don't feel like sitting around.

more.en: I don't feel like eating pasta again.
more.szh: 我可不想再吃意面了。

w-chore.note: household chores 家务；也指让人觉得烦的例行小事：Ironing is a chore.
w-chore.en: Mum used to make us share every chore, remember?
w-chore.szh: 小时候妈让我们什么家务都分着干，记得吧？

more.en: If you tick off a chore on the Tube, it just disappears.
more.szh: 你在地铁上勾掉一项家务，它直接就没了。

insist-on.note: to say firmly that you will do something, or that something must happen
insist-on.tip: on 后面接 doing 或名词：insist on paying；也可以只说一句 I insist!（我坚持！）
insist-on.example: My manager insisted on paying for lunch.
insist-on.en: That's why I insist on cooking tonight.
insist-on.szh: 所以今晚这顿饭非我做不可。

more.en: She insisted on finishing everything on her own.
more.szh: 她坚持所有事都要自己做完。

more.en: We agreed on a new rule, and Mia insisted on writing it down.
more.szh: 我们商定了一条新规矩，Mia 非要把它写下来。

take-it-easy.note: to relax and not work too hard
take-it-easy.tip: 中间的 it 不能省；对着急的人说 Take it easy! 还有「别急、别激动」的意思。
take-it-easy.example: The doctor told me to take it easy for a week.
take-it-easy.en: When did you last take it easy?
take-it-easy.szh: 你上一次好好歇着是什么时候？

more.en: OK, take it easy tonight.
more.szh: 好了，今晚放松一下。

more.en: Before exams, she told nervous students to take it easy.
more.szh: 考试前，她会让紧张的学生放轻松。

w-smoke-alarm.note: smoke 是不可数名词「烟」，不说 a smoke；fire alarm 是火警警报。
w-smoke-alarm.en: It's been twenty minutes, and the smoke alarm's beeping.
w-smoke-alarm.szh: 二十分钟到了，烟雾报警器怎么在嘀嘀叫？

w-beep.note: 电子设备发出的短促响声；名词也是 beep：Leave a message after the beep.
w-beep.en: It's been twenty minutes, and the smoke alarm's beeping.
w-beep.szh: 二十分钟到了，烟雾报警器怎么在嘀嘀叫？

w-under-control.note: 反义是 out of control（失控）；get sth under control 把某事控制住。

in-that-case.note: used to say what you will do because of the situation that has just been described
in-that-case.tip: 接着对方刚说的情况来回应，放句首，后面加逗号。
in-that-case.example: The meeting's been cancelled? In that case, I'll work from home.
in-that-case.en: In that case, let me help.

more.en: In that case, let's go for the barbecue.
more.szh: 那就选烤肉吧。

w-remote.note: remote team 远程团队；work remotely 远程办公。
w-remote.en: Last month I flew to Berlin to meet my remote team for the first time.
w-remote.szh: 上个月，我飞去柏林，第一次跟远程团队的同事见面。

more.en: He'd also taken his TV remote apart, just to see how it worked.
more.szh: 他还把电视遥控器拆了，说只是想看看里面怎么回事。

w-accent.note: a strong accent 口音很重；重音在前：AC-cent。
w-accent.en: On the plane, I kept thinking: they'll probably hate my accent, and I might forget everyone's names.
w-accent.szh: 在飞机上，我脑子里一直在想：他们多半会嫌弃我的口音，我说不定还会把大家的名字全忘了。

strike-up-a-conversation.zh: （和陌生人）攀谈起来；搭起话来
strike-up-a-conversation.note: to start talking to someone you don't know
strike-up-a-conversation.tip: strike 的过去式是 struck；跟谁搭话用 with：strike up a conversation with sb。
