strike-up-a-conversation.example: I struck up a conversation with a designer at the conference.
strike-up-a-conversation.en: Then the old lady next to me struck up a conversation: "Have you ever been to Berlin?"
strike-up-a-conversation.szh: 这时，邻座的老太太跟我搭起话来：「你去过柏林吗？」

more.en: He was easy to talk to, and we soon struck up a conversation.
more.szh: 他很好聊，我们很快就聊开了。

more.en: Then I struck up a conversation with the man in the phone shop downstairs, and he lent me four old phones.
more.szh: 然后我跟楼下手机店的老板聊了起来，他借给我四部旧手机。

w-tractor.note: 坐交通工具用 on：on his tractor、on the bus；小汽车用 in：in a car。
w-tractor.en: So a farmer took her to the church on his tractor — for free.
w-tractor.szh: 结果一个农民开着拖拉机把她送到了教堂——一分钱没要。

w-clearly.note: 放在 be 动词后面，表示「一看就知道」；也有「清楚地」的意思：speak clearly。
w-clearly.en: She was clearly proud of him.
w-clearly.szh: 看得出来，她特别为这个孙子骄傲。

by-coincidence.note: by chance, in a surprising way that was not planned
by-coincidence.tip: 也可以说 by chance；感叹「真巧！」说 What a coincidence!
by-coincidence.example: By coincidence, my new colleague went to the same university as me.
by-coincidence.en: By coincidence, he was a software engineer in Berlin too.
by-coincidence.szh: 巧的是，他也是软件工程师，也在柏林。

more.en: By coincidence, he was going to the same meeting.
more.szh: 真巧，他要去的也是这个会。

show-sb-around.zh: 带某人参观；带某人四处转转
show-sb-around.note: to take someone to see the different parts of a place
show-sb-around.tip: 人放在 show 和 around 中间：show you around；带着参观哪里直接接地点：show sb around the city。
show-sb-around.example: On my first day, my manager showed me around the office.
show-sb-around.en: "And my grandson will definitely show you around."
show-sb-around.szh: 「我孙子肯定会带你到处转转。」

more.en: "I'll show you around after lunch."
more.szh: 「午饭后我带你四处转转。」

more.en: On day one, she showed the new students around the lab.
more.szh: 开学第一天，她带新生参观机房。

in-the-middle-of.note: during something, or at the centre of a place
in-the-middle-of.tip: 既能说地方（in the middle of the room），也能说事情进行到一半（in the middle of dinner）。
in-the-middle-of.example: My phone rang in the middle of the meeting.
in-the-middle-of.en: Somewhere in the middle of her fourth story, I nodded off.
in-the-middle-of.szh: 她讲到第四个故事的时候，我不知不觉睡着了。

more.en: "I know you're in the middle of a busy week, so there's no need to reply straight away."
more.szh: 「我知道您这周正忙，所以不必马上回复。」

more.en: Last Tuesday, in the middle of the call, a nasty noise started.
more.szh: 上周二，会开到一半，响起了一阵刺耳的噪音。

nod-off.note: to fall asleep without meaning to, especially when sitting
nod-off.tip: 比 fall asleep 口语，常指坐着不小心睡着；过去式要双写 d：nodded off。
nod-off.example: I nodded off on the train and missed my stop.
nod-off.en: Somewhere in the middle of her fourth story, I nodded off.
nod-off.szh: 她讲到第四个故事的时候，我不知不觉睡着了。

more.en: Last night I was so tired that I nodded off at my desk.
more.szh: 昨晚我累得在桌前打起了瞌睡。

w-arrivals.note: 机场里的 arrivals 到达区，departures 出发区，两个词都用复数。
w-arrivals.en: At arrivals, Jonas from my team was waiting with a sign that said "Chen".
w-arrivals.szh: 到达大厅里，团队的 Jonas 举着写着「Chen」的牌子在等我。

w-hug.note: 过去式双写 g：hugged；名词也是 hug：give sb a hug。
w-hug.en: Before I could say hello, the old lady ran past me and hugged him.
w-hug.szh: 我还没来得及打招呼，老太太就从我身边冲过去，一把抱住了他。

it-s-a-small-world.note: used when you are surprised to meet someone you know, or to find a connection with someone, in an unexpected place
it-s-a-small-world.tip: 碰到意想不到的巧合时说的感叹，基本就用这一种说法，不说 The world is small。
it-s-a-small-world.example: You know my old boss too? It's a small world!
it-s-a-small-world.en: It's a small world, I thought.

more.en: It's a small world, isn't it?
more.szh: 世界真小，是吧？

w-barbecue.note: 也常写成 BBQ；have a barbecue 办一场烧烤。
w-barbecue.en: Shall we book the Italian place or the Korean barbecue?
w-barbecue.szh: 我们订那家意大利餐厅，还是那家韩国烤肉？

split-the-bill.note: to share the cost of a meal or service between several people
split-the-bill.tip: 平分成几份用 ways：split it four ways；各付各的也可以说 go Dutch，但现在不太常用。
split-the-bill.example: Shall we split the bill, or is it my turn to pay?
split-the-bill.en: Both are quite expensive, but we could split the bill three ways.
split-the-bill.szh: 两家都不便宜，不过我们可以三个人平摊。

more.en: Thanks — but let's split the bill.
more.szh: 谢谢——不过咱们 AA 吧。

w-obviously.note: 放在句末是口语里的「那还用说」；形容词 obvious 明显的。
w-obviously.en: Mei doesn't have to pay, obviously.

book-a-table.note: to arrange to have a table at a restaurant at a particular time
book-a-table.tip: 英式说 book a table，美式常说 make a reservation；订几个人的位用 for：book a table for four。
book-a-table.example: I've booked a table for six at eight o'clock.
book-a-table.en: We should book a table tonight.

more.en: Good, because I've booked a table for dinner at eight.
more.szh: 那就好，我订了今晚八点的餐厅。

w-fully-booked.note: 餐厅、酒店、航班都能说；也可以说 There are no tables left.

go-for.tip: 在几个选项里挑一个时常用，比 choose 口语；点菜时也说 I'll go for the fish。
go-for.example: I'll go for the vegetarian option, please.
go-for.en: In that case, let's go for the barbecue.

w-after-all.note: 放在句末，补一个大家都知道的理由；放在句首或句中还有「终究、到头来」的意思：He came after all.（他最后还是来了）

it-s-up-to-you.note: used to say that someone else should make the decision
it-s-up-to-you.tip: you 可以换成别人：It's up to her、It's up to the team；不说 It's up to your decision。
it-s-up-to-you.example: We can meet online or in the office — it's up to you.

more.en: "It's up to you."
more.szh: 「都听您的。」

make-a-decision.note: to choose what to do after thinking about it
make-a-decision.tip: 中文说「做决定」，英文用 make，不用 do；也可以只用一个动词 decide。
make-a-decision.example: We have to make a decision about the new design by Friday.

more.en: "On the other hand, I can't make a decision about the login screen without the latest version."
more.szh: 「不过话说回来，没有最新版本，登录页的事我没法做决定。」

w-single.note: 也有「单个的」「单程的」意思：a single room 单人间，a single ticket 单程票。

i-d-rather-than.note: used to say what you would prefer to do
i-d-rather-than.tip: 'd rather 后面接动词原形，than 后面也是动词原形：I'd rather stay than go，不说 I'd rather to stay。
i-d-rather-than.example: I'd rather work late tonight than come in on Saturday.
i-d-rather-than.en: And I'd rather cook at home than read fifty more.
i-d-rather-than.szh: 我宁可在家做饭，也不想再看五十条。

more.en: "I'd rather fix ten bugs than give a talk," said Chen.
more.szh: 「我宁可去修十个 bug，也不想上台讲，」小陈说。

w-dumplings.note: dumpling 泛指各种面皮包馅的点心；包饺子是 make dumplings。

in-charge-of.note: responsible for a person, group or piece of work
in-charge-of.tip: 人做主语：he's in charge of the backend；前面的 be 不能丢。take charge of 是「接手、接管」。
in-charge-of.example: Who's in charge of the release this week?
in-charge-of.en: He's in charge of the backend.

more.en: She also pointed out that nobody was actually in charge of pressing Send.
more.szh: 她还指出，其实根本没有人负责按「发送」。

more.en: So Rachel, who's in charge of the interns, asked me to have a word with her.
more.szh: 于是负责带实习生的 Rachel 让我去跟她聊聊。

more.en: He won't be in charge of certificates.
more.szh: 证书不归他管。

as-soon-as-possible.tip: 邮件里常缩写成 ASAP，语气比较急；想客气一点，可以说 when you get a chance（你方便的时候）。
as-soon-as-possible.example: The app keeps crashing, so we need a fix as soon as possible.
as-soon-as-possible.en: I need the API document as soon as possible.
as-soon-as-possible.szh: 我得尽快拿到 API 文档。

more.en: I just wanted to send it as soon as possible, with a big apology.
more.szh: 我只想赶紧把报告发过去，再好好道个歉。

w-order.note: 这里不是「订单」。give an order 下命令；sound like an order 听着像在下命令。
w-order.en: But Rachel says "Send me the API document" sounds like an order in English.
w-order.szh: 可 Rachel 说，「Send me the API document」这种说法在英语里听着像下命令。

w-favour.note: 英式拼写，美式写 favor。开口求人常说 Can I ask you a favour?；帮某人一个忙是 do sb a favour。
w-favour.en: "I'm afraid I have a small favour to ask."

w-possibly.note: 放在 could you 后面，让请求更客气：Could you possibly …? 平时的意思是「可能」：It's possibly the best app I've used.
w-possibly.en: "I was wondering if you could possibly send me the API document."
w-possibly.szh: 「不知您能否发我一份 API 文档。」

w-up-to-date.note: 放在名词前要加连字符：an up-to-date version；反义是 out of date（过时的）。
w-up-to-date.en: "I've been reading an old version since Monday, but I'm not sure whether it's still up to date."
w-up-to-date.szh: 「我从周一起一直在看一份旧版本，但不确定它现在还是不是最新的。」

look-over.note: to read or examine something quickly in order to check it
look-over.tip: look over 是快速过一遍，逐条细看一般说 go through；代词常放中间：Could you look it over?
look-over.example: Could you look over my pull request before lunch?
look-over.en: "Would you mind looking over my questions when you have time?"
look-over.szh: 「您有空的时候，能否帮我看看我的问题？」

more.en: Before you send a long message, ask a colleague to look it over.
more.szh: 发长消息之前，请同事帮你看一遍。

more.en: Then the wifi went down, and a guard came along and looked over our tickets.
more.szh: 后来车上的 Wi-Fi 断了，一位列车员过来把我们的票查了一遍。

get-back-to.note: to reply to someone later, by phone, email or message
get-back-to.tip: to 不能丢：get back to sb。「回复你」不说 reply you，要说 reply to you；工作里最常听到的是 I'll get back to you。
get-back-to.example: Let me check with the team and get back to you this afternoon.
get-back-to.en: "Could you get back to me when you're free?"
get-back-to.szh: 「您方便的时候能否回复我一下？」

more.en: I'll get back to you when the tests pass — probably in about an hour.
more.szh: 测试一通过我就回你们——大概一个小时吧。

more.en: Anyway, let me get back to my dad.
more.szh: 好了，说回我爸。

in-advance.note: before a particular time or event
in-advance.tip: Thanks in advance 是邮件常见结尾，但对方还没答应就先谢，有人会觉得像在催；不想有这层意思，写 Thanks for your help 更稳。
in-advance.example: Please send me the slides in advance so I can read them before the meeting.

more.en: Ask in advance, and keep people posted when plans change.
more.szh: 提前问，计划有变就及时告诉大家。

more.en: I mean, I'd rather plan the day in advance than let Slack plan it for me.
more.szh: 说白了，我宁可自己提前把一天安排好，也不想让 Slack 替我安排。

w-regards.note: Kind regards / Best regards 都是常用落款，比 Best 正式；表示「问候」时总用复数：Give my regards to your team.

w-ps.note: postscript 的缩写，写在落款后面补一句。读作 /ˌpiː ˈes/，前面用 a。

w-formal.note: 反义是 informal 或 casual；a formal email 正式邮件。
w-formal.en: "PS: You don't have to be that formal."

get-started.tip: 比 start 口语；开始做什么用 on：get started on the new feature。开会时常说 Shall we get started?
get-started.example: We'll get started when everyone has joined the call.

more.en: Then he asked whether the team had got started on the new app.
more.szh: 又问团队是不是已经开始做新 App 了。

more.en: "Right, let's get started," said the CEO, and Chen walked to the front.
more.szh: 「好，我们开始吧，」CEO 话音刚落，小陈走到了前面。

more.en: Today's tour is fully booked, so let's get started.
more.szh: 今天的导览名额全满了，我们这就开始吧。

w-status-report.note: status 是项目的「状态、进展」；开会时「同步一下进度」可以说 give a quick status update。
w-status-report.en: So, every Friday, our team sends a status report to the client.
w-status-report.szh: 是这样，每周五我们团队都要给客户发一份进度报告。

w-approve.note: approve sth 是批准某事；approve of sb/sth 是「赞成、看得惯」，意思不一样。名词是 approval。
w-approve.en: Arjun writes it, I check it, and Rachel approves it.
w-approve.szh: Arjun 写，我检查，Rachel 审批。

more.en: Before any work starts, plans must be sent to the council and approved by an officer.
more.szh: 动工之前，方案必须先交到市政厅，还得由专门的官员批准。

be-supposed-to.note: used to say what someone should do because of a rule, a plan or what others expect
be-supposed-to.tip: 强调规定、安排或别人的期望，常暗示实际上没做到：I was supposed to call him.（本该打电话，结果没打）。
be-supposed-to.example: I'm supposed to send the build to QA by six, but it's still failing.
be-supposed-to.en: The team's done it like this for three years, so everyone knows what they're supposed to do.
be-supposed-to.szh: 团队这么干已经三年了，所以每个人都清楚自己该干什么。

more.en: The release is supposed to be next Friday, and we're behind schedule.
more.szh: 按计划下周五就要发版，可我们进度已经落后了。

more.en: I wasn't even supposed to be working on it.
more.szh: 其实我压根就不该碰它。

w-somehow.note: 说不清原因时用：Somehow I lost my keys. 也可以表示「想办法、总归」：We'll finish it somehow.
w-somehow.en: Well, last Friday was crazy, and somehow the report slipped everyone's mind.
w-somehow.szh: 结果上周五忙疯了，不知怎么的，报告的事大家全忘了。

slip-your-mind.note: if something slips your mind, you forget it
slip-your-mind.tip: 主语是被忘掉的事，不是人：It slipped my mind，不说 I slipped my mind。your 要换成对应的人：slipped his mind、slipped everyone's mind。
slip-your-mind.example: Sorry, your email completely slipped my mind — I'll reply today.
slip-your-mind.en: Well, last Friday was crazy, and somehow the report slipped everyone's mind.
slip-your-mind.szh: 结果上周五忙疯了，不知怎么的，报告的事大家全忘了。

more.en: And booking the meeting room slipped her mind, so the team had their stand-up in the kitchen.
more.szh: 订会议室的事她也忘了，大家只好挤在茶水间开站会。

w-pass-on.note: pass sth on to sb，代词放中间：pass it on。传话也能用：I'll pass on your message.
w-pass-on.en: I said I'd checked it and passed it on to her.
w-pass-on.szh: 我说我检查完了，已经转给她了。

be-to-blame.note: to be responsible for something bad that has happened
be-to-blame.tip: 形式是主动的，意思却是「该被怪」：Who is to blame?；怪的是什么事用 for：Nobody is to blame for the delay。
be-to-blame.example: The old router was to blame for the slow Wi-Fi.

more.en: So who, or what, was to blame?
more.szh: 那到底该怪谁，或者说该怪什么？

w-fault.note: It's my fault. 是「怪我」，强调责任在谁；mistake 只说「做错的事」。
w-fault.en: She said it was her fault, not ours, and she took responsibility for the whole thing.
w-fault.szh: 她说这是她的错，不怪我们，把责任全揽了下来。

take-responsibility-for.note: to accept that something is your job or your fault
take-responsibility-for.tip: responsibility 前面不加 the；介词用 for，不用 of。比 be responsible for 更强调「主动认下来」。
take-responsibility-for.example: As team lead, I take responsibility for the delay.
take-responsibility-for.en: She said it was her fault, not ours, and she took responsibility for the whole thing.
take-responsibility-for.szh: 她说这是她的错，不怪我们，把责任全揽了下来。

more.en: You took responsibility for that, didn't you?
more.szh: 那次是你把责任揽下来的，对吧？

more.en: Nobody expects you to take responsibility for the whole app in your first week.
more.szh: 没人指望你第一周就把整个 App 扛起来。

point-out.note: to tell someone something they did not know or had not noticed
point-out.tip: 常接 that 从句：point out that …；指出某个东西，代词放中间：point it out。
point-out.example: Thanks for pointing out the typo on the login screen.
point-out.en: She also pointed out that nobody was actually in charge of pressing Send.
point-out.szh: 她还指出，其实根本没有人负责按「发送」。

more.en: Then Chen pointed out something strange.
more.szh: 这时，小陈指出了一个奇怪的地方。

more.en: If someone points out a mistake, thank them.
more.szh: 有人指出错误的话，记得谢谢人家。

more.en: My maths teacher pointed out that seven times eight isn't fifty-four.
more.szh: 数学老师指出来，七乘八不等于五十四。

follow-up.note: to contact someone again, or do more, after something has happened
follow-up.tip: 跟进某人用 with，跟进某事用 on：follow up with the client、follow up on the bug。名词写成 follow-up：a follow-up email。
follow-up.example: I'll follow up with an email after the meeting.
follow-up.en: Then she said she'd follow up with the client herself, and picked up the phone.
follow-up.szh: 然后她说她亲自去跟客户沟通，说完就拿起了电话。

more.en: I've followed up with QA.
more.szh: 我已经找 QA 跟进了。

more.en: He always follows up first thing in the morning.
more.szh: 他总是第二天一早再跟进。

w-client.note: client 多指买服务的客户，比如外包、咨询、律师的客户；在店里买东西的顾客是 customer。
w-client.en: Then she said she'd follow up with the client herself, and picked up the phone.
w-client.szh: 然后她说她亲自去跟客户沟通，说完就拿起了电话。

more.en: Most of my clients wanted to make a complaint about a neighbour's tree or wall.
more.szh: 我的客户大多是来投诉邻居家的树或者墙的。

w-apparently.note: 转述刚听来的消息时常放句首，意思是「据说、听人说」；不是「显然」，「显然」是 obviously。
w-apparently.en: "Apparently, our reports go to an old email address that nobody checks."
w-apparently.szh: 「原来我们的报告一直发到一个没人看的旧邮箱。」

more.en: Apparently, "I'm not sure that's a good idea" means "absolutely not".
more.szh: 据说，「我不太确定这是个好主意」，意思就是「绝对不行」。

work-on.note: to spend time doing, making or improving something
work-on.tip: 问别人在忙什么，最常说 What are you working on?；on 别丢。work at 后面接单位或地点：She works at Google。
work-on.example: I'm working on the new sign-up screens this sprint.
work-on.en: So, Chen, what have you been working on this week?
work-on.szh: 那么小陈，你这周在忙什么？

more.en: "The thing is, I'm already working on two other tasks."
more.szh: 「是这样的，我手上已经有两件事了。」

more.en: On the way, he asked me what I was working on.
more.szh: 路上，他问我在做什么。

more.en: Although he was exhausted after a long day, he worked on his slides until two in the morning.
more.szh: 虽然忙了一整天已经累坏了，他还是做幻灯片做到了凌晨两点。

more.en: I wasn't even supposed to be working on it.
more.szh: 其实我压根就不该碰它。

more.en: For one day a week, instead of sitting in calls, everyone worked on a single task.
more.szh: 每周有一天，大家不开会，各自专心做一件事。

w-layout.note: 界面元素怎么摆放就是 layout；layout bug 指界面错位、重叠之类的问题。
w-layout.en: I've been trying to fix a layout bug for three days.
w-layout.szh: 我在修一个布局 bug，已经修了三天了。

w-nasty.note: 口语里常说问题、病、意外「很麻烦」：a nasty bug、a nasty cold、a nasty surprise。
w-nasty.en: It must be a nasty one.

run-into.note: to experience a problem or difficulty, often one you did not expect
run-into.tip: run into a problem / trouble 遇到麻烦；run into sb 是碰巧遇见某人。过去式是 ran，过去分词是 run。
run-into.example: We ran into a problem with the payment API last night.
run-into.en: And then I run into the same problem on another one.
run-into.szh: 然后换个页面，又碰上同样的问题。

more.en: He'd run into this problem before.
more.szh: 他以前就碰到过这种问题。

more.en: On our way back, we ran into the guard, and she promised to ask around.
more.szh: 往回走的路上，我们碰到了那位列车员，她答应帮我们问问。

figure-out.note: to understand or solve something after thinking about it
figure-out.tip: 后面常接 why / how / what 从句；代词放中间：figure it out。find out 是打听、查到事实，figure out 是自己想明白。
figure-out.example: It took us an hour to figure out why the build was failing.
figure-out.en: I still can't figure out why.
figure-out.szh: 我到现在都搞不明白为什么。

more.en: And nobody could figure out where it was coming from.
more.szh: 可谁也搞不清声音是从哪儿来的。

more.en: It's no big deal if you can't figure everything out at once.
more.szh: 一下子弄不明白所有事，没什么大不了的。

w-deadline.note: 按时完成是 meet a deadline，错过期限是 miss a deadline。
w-deadline.en: I'm just really nervous about the deadline.
w-deadline.szh: 主要是截止日期快到了，我特别紧张。

w-release.note: 也能当动词：We release a new version every two weeks. 更新说明叫 release notes。
w-release.en: The release is supposed to be next Friday, and we're behind schedule.
w-release.szh: 按计划下周五就要发版，可我们进度已经落后了。

behind-schedule.tip: 反义是 ahead of schedule（提前）；按计划进行是 on schedule。落后多少放前面：two weeks behind schedule。
behind-schedule.example: The project is two weeks behind schedule.
behind-schedule.en: The release is supposed to be next Friday, and we're behind schedule.
behind-schedule.szh: 按计划下周五就要发版，可我们进度已经落后了。

more.en: Last week we were behind schedule.
more.szh: 上周我们进度还落后。

more.en: We're already behind schedule.
more.szh: 咱们已经晚了。

w-bother.note: 打扰别人时常这样开口：Sorry to bother you, but …；Don't bother. 是「不用麻烦了」。
w-bother.en: Everyone's so busy that I didn't want to bother anyone.
w-bother.szh: 大家都那么忙，我不想去打扰别人。

more.en: "Don't bother trying to find out. I spent three weeks trying."
more.szh: 「别费劲去查了。我查了三个星期。」

take-a-break.note: to stop working or doing something for a short time
take-a-break.tip: 英式英语也常说 have a break；歇多久放在 break 前面：a ten-minute break。
take-a-break.example: Let's take a ten-minute break and come back at three.
take-a-break.en: If you're stuck for an hour, take a break.
take-a-break.szh: 要是卡了一个小时，就先歇一歇。

more.en: She'd even taken a break for lunch.
more.szh: 甚至还停下来好好吃了顿午饭。

more.en: Let's take a break.
more.szh: 我们歇会儿吧。

ask-for-help.note: to tell someone that you need them to help you
ask-for-help.tip: 向谁求助，人放中间：ask Arjun for help；for 不能丢，不说 ask help。
ask-for-help.example: Don't be afraid to ask for help in your first month.
ask-for-help.en: Then ask for help — after an hour, not three days.
ask-for-help.szh: 然后找人帮忙——一个小时就该找，别拖三天。

more.en: "And remember, asking for help isn't a crime," I added.
more.szh: 「还有，记住：找人帮忙又不犯法，」我补了一句。

more.en: Should we ask for help?
more.szh: 要不要找人帮忙？

w-beginner.note: a complete beginner 纯新手；beginner's luck 新手的好运气。

w-intern.note: 实习这份工作叫 internship；去实习是 do an internship。
w-intern.en: Our new intern, Maya, is someone who says yes to everything.
w-intern.szh: 我们新来的实习生 Maya，是个什么都答应的人。

take-on.note: to accept a job or a responsibility
take-on.tip: 常说 take on too much（揽的活太多）；代词放中间：take it on。还有「招人」的意思：take on new staff。
take-on.example: Don't take on more work than you can finish this sprint.
take-on.en: In her first week, she took on every job that anyone mentioned.
take-on.szh: 来的第一周，谁提到什么活儿她都接。

more.en: I'll take it on.
more.szh: 交给我吧。

more.en: Could I take on a few tickets tomorrow?
more.szh: 明天我能接几个工单吗？

keep-a-promise.note: to do what you said you would do
keep-a-promise.tip: 反义是 break a promise（食言）；promise 可数，答应过很多事就说 keep your promises。
keep-a-promise.example: If you can't keep a promise, tell people early.
keep-a-promise.en: Soon she was working until midnight, and she still couldn't keep her promises.
keep-a-promise.szh: 很快她就天天干到半夜，可答应的事还是做不完。

more.en: I promised you a proper coffee, and I've kept my promise, haven't I?
more.szh: 我答应过请你喝杯像样的咖啡，说到做到了吧？

w-stand-up.note: 开发团队每天的简短碰头会，大家站着开，几分钟结束，也叫 daily stand-up。
w-stand-up.en: And booking the meeting room slipped her mind, so the team had their stand-up in the kitchen.
w-stand-up.szh: 订会议室的事她也忘了，大家只好挤在茶水间开站会。

w-have-a-word-with.note: 英式口语，指私下简短地谈，有时带一点提醒的意思：Can I have a word with you?
w-have-a-word-with.en: So Rachel, who's in charge of the interns, asked me to have a word with her.
w-have-a-word-with.szh: 于是负责带实习生的 Rachel 让我去跟她聊聊。

w-surrounded.note: be surrounded by sth / sb；动词 surround 是「包围」。
w-surrounded.en: I video-called Maya at her desk, where she was surrounded by sticky notes.
w-surrounded.szh: 我给 Maya 打了个视频电话，她坐在工位上，周围贴满了便利贴。

w-sticky-note.note: 也常叫 Post-it（品牌名）；stick 是「粘」。
w-sticky-note.en: Then I wrote a polite answer on a sticky note and held it up to the camera.
w-sticky-note.szh: 然后我在一张便利贴上写了一句客气的回答，举到镜头前。

i-m-afraid.zh: 恐怕；（客气地说出坏消息）
i-m-afraid.note: used to politely say something that the other person may not want to hear
i-m-afraid.tip: 不是「我害怕」，而是让拒绝和坏消息听起来客气些；简短回答可以说 I'm afraid not.（恐怕不行）
i-m-afraid.example: I'm afraid the meeting room is booked all afternoon.

more.en: "I'm afraid not," said Chen.
more.szh: 「恐怕不是，」小陈说。

more.en: I'm afraid it won't.
more.szh: 恐怕停不了。

more.en: I'm afraid I'll be out of the office tomorrow morning.
more.szh: 明天上午我恐怕来不了办公室了。

the-thing-is.note: used to introduce a reason or a problem
the-thing-is.tip: 用来引出理由或难处，后面加逗号；比直接说 because 柔和，听起来像在解释，不像在找借口。
the-thing-is.example: I'd love to come. The thing is, I've got a deadline on Friday.
the-thing-is.en: "The thing is, I'm already working on two other tasks."
the-thing-is.szh: 「是这样的，我手上已经有两件事了。」

more.en: "The thing is, the noise stops whenever Rachel speaks."
more.szh: 「问题是，Rachel 一说话，噪音就停。」

on-top-of.note: in addition to something, especially something difficult
on-top-of.tip: 既能说位置（on top of the fridge 冰箱顶上），也常说「在…之外又加上」，多用来说事情多、压力大。
on-top-of.example: On top of the release, we have three new people to train.
on-top-of.en: "And that's on top of the demo."

more.en: On top of the noise, Arjun's audio kept cutting out.
more.szh: 除了噪音，Arjun 的声音还一直断断续续。

more.en: "On top of that, a lot of the snacks we reach for at work are high in sugar."
more.szh: 「再加上，我们上班时随手拿的零食，很多含糖量都很高。」

turn-down.note: to say no to a request or an offer
turn-down.tip: 代词放中间：turn it down；比 refuse 委婉。另一个常见意思是「调小音量」：turn the music down。
turn-down.example: He turned down the job because the commute was too long.
turn-down.en: A week later, she'd turned down four requests.
turn-down.szh: 一周后，她已经推掉了四个请求。

more.en: He wanted to turn it down.
more.szh: 他想推掉。

more.en: I turned down cake for this, so it had better not happen again.
more.szh: 为了这事我连蛋糕都没吃，所以最好别有下次了。

w-request.note: 提出请求是 make a request；也能当动词，但比 ask 正式。
w-request.en: A week later, she'd turned down four requests.
w-request.szh: 一周后，她已经推掉了四个请求。

more.en: Once we've listed the top three requests, we can plan the next update.
more.szh: 等我们把呼声最高的三个需求列出来，就可以规划下一次更新了。

in-person.note: if you do something in person, you go somewhere or meet someone yourself, not by phone or online
in-person.tip: 反义是 online、on a call、by email；「见到本人」可以说 meet sb in person。
in-person.example: It's easier to explain this in person than on Slack.
in-person.en: So, after two months of video calls, I finally went to our London office in person.
in-person.szh: 是这样，视频通话了两个月，我终于亲自去了一趟伦敦办公室。

more.en: Chen! Finally, in person!
more.szh: 小陈！终于见到真人了！

more.en: I've seen this place on Instagram, but it's much busier in person.
more.szh: 我在 Instagram 上见过这地方，不过亲眼看比照片上热闹多了。

w-yawn.note: 也能当名词：give a big yawn（打了个大哈欠）。
w-yawn.en: I was still yawning after the early train, and it was raining, of course.
w-yawn.szh: 坐了早班火车，我还在打哈欠，而且不出所料，天在下雨。

w-maze.note: 常用来形容一个地方很难找路：The hospital is a maze.
w-maze.en: The company had just moved to a new building, and it was a maze.
w-maze.szh: 公司刚搬进一栋新楼，楼里跟迷宫似的。

be-about-to.note: to be going to happen or do something very soon
be-about-to.tip: 后面接动词原形；比 be going to 更「马上」，所以不和具体时间连用：不说 I'm about to leave at six。
be-about-to.example: I was about to leave when the client called.
be-about-to.en: My first meeting was about to start, and I didn't know where room 4B was.
be-about-to.szh: 第一个会马上就要开了，可我不知道 4B 会议室在哪儿。

more.en: He was about to begin when his laptop died.
more.szh: 他刚要开口，笔记本电脑突然黑屏了。

more.en: I was about to give up when they finally got round to it last spring.
more.szh: 我都准备放弃了，结果去年春天他们总算处理了。

have-no-idea.note: to not know something at all
have-no-idea.tip: 比 I don't know 语气重；后面可以接 wh- 从句，用陈述语序：I have no idea where it is。
have-no-idea.example: I have no idea why the build failed.
have-no-idea.en: "I have no idea," he said with a smile.

more.en: He had no idea how to give a talk without slides.
more.szh: 没有幻灯片，他完全不知道该怎么讲。

more.en: I've worked here for two years, and I have no idea.
more.szh: 我在这儿干了两年了，完全不知道。

more.en: The beef has to be cooked for at least two hours, so I've no idea how this is going to work.
more.szh: 牛肉至少得烤两个小时，我真不知道这下该怎么弄。

more.en: When I moved in with Tom, I had no idea he came from a place like this.
more.szh: 刚搬去跟 Tom 合租的时候，我完全不知道他是从这样一个地方来的。

head-for.tip: head 在这里是动词；问别人去哪儿可以说 Where are you heading?
head-for.example: After the meeting, we headed for the pub.
head-for.en: We headed for the fourth floor together.

more.en: "Hold on," said Chen, and he headed for the window.
more.szh: 「等一下，」小陈说着，走到了窗边。

more.en: I was heading for the door to grab a bite, but dinner can wait.
more.szh: 我正要出门随便吃点东西，晚饭等等再说。

on-the-way.tip: 去某地的路上是 on the way to + 地点；home 前面不加 to：on the way home。in the way 是「挡路」，别混。
on-the-way.example: Can you pick up some milk on the way home?
on-the-way.en: On the way, he asked me what I was working on.

more.en: The fix is on the way.
more.szh: 修复马上就来。

more.en: I'll reply on the way back.
more.szh: 我回来的路上再回你。

more.en: On our way back, we ran into the guard, and she promised to ask around.
more.szh: 往回走的路上，我们碰到了那位列车员，她答应帮我们问问。

w-any-good.note: 多用在疑问句和否定句里：Is the film any good? / The map wasn't any good.
w-any-good.en: He also wanted to know if the coffee machine was any good.
w-any-good.szh: 他还想知道咖啡机好不好用。

w-reception.note: 说「在前台」常不加冠词：Ask at reception. 前台接待员是 receptionist。
w-reception.en: "Do you know if there's a map at reception?" I asked.
w-reception.szh: 「您知道前台有没有地图吗？」我问。

w-car-park.note: 英式说法，美式说 parking lot。
w-car-park.en: So we turned back, and somehow we ended up in the car park.
w-car-park.szh: 于是我们往回走，结果不知怎么的，走到了停车场。

get-to-know.note: to spend time with someone so that you learn more about them
get-to-know.tip: know 是状态，get to know 是「慢慢熟起来」的过程；初次见面说 meet，不说 know：Nice to meet you。
get-to-know.example: It took me a few months to get to know my new team.
get-to-know.en: He said getting lost was a good way to get to know people.
get-to-know.szh: 他说，迷路是认识人的好办法。

more.en: We've really got to know each other this year, haven't we?
more.szh: 这一年咱们真是熟了不少，对吧？

more.en: And it's a lovely way for children to get to know the history of their own city.
more.szh: 而且这是让孩子们了解自己城市历史的好办法。

w-ceo.zh: 首席执行官；公司一把手
w-ceo.note: chief executive officer 的缩写，按字母读 C-E-O。
w-ceo.en: "Oh good, Chen — I see you've already met our CEO."
w-ceo.szh: 「太好了，小陈——看来你已经见过我们的 CEO 了。」

w-drill.note: 名词 a drill 是电钻；drill a hole 钻个孔。
w-drill.en: It sounded as if someone was drilling through a wall.
w-drill.szh: 听起来像有人在墙上钻孔。

it-sounds-like.note: used to say what you think something is, from what you hear
it-sounds-like.tip: like 后面接名词，口语里也常接句子：It sounds like you're busy. 听别人讲完一件事也能用：That sounds like fun!
it-sounds-like.example: It sounds like the meeting went well.
it-sounds-like.en: "It sounds like a building site," said Arjun.

more.en: If it sounds like a complaint, you'd better rewrite it.
more.szh: 要是读起来像在抱怨，最好重写。

more.en: Honestly, it sounds like something from a children's book.
more.szh: 说真的，听着就像童话书里的故事。

w-building-site.note: 英式说法，美式多说 construction site。
w-building-site.en: "It sounds like a building site," said Arjun.

w-redecorate.note: 多指刷墙、换墙纸这类室内装修；大改造用 renovate。
w-redecorate.en: "Chen, didn't you say your neighbours were redecorating?"
w-redecorate.szh: 「小陈，你不是说你家邻居在装修吗？」

be-on-mute.note: if you are on mute in a call, other people cannot hear you
be-on-mute.tip: 开静音是 mute yourself / go on mute，取消静音是 unmute。开会时最常听到的一句：You're on mute!（你没开麦！）
be-on-mute.example: Sorry, I was on mute — can you hear me now?

more.en: I'm always on mute now.
more.szh: 我现在开会一直开着静音。

more.en: So I'll be on mute anyway.
more.szh: 反正我也是「静音」状态。

w-audio.note: 视频会议里 audio 指声音，video 指画面：Your audio is fine, but your video is frozen.
w-audio.en: On top of the noise, Arjun's audio kept cutting out.
w-audio.szh: 除了噪音，Arjun 的声音还一直断断续续。

cut-out.zh: （声音、信号）断断续续；突然中断
cut-out.note: if a sound or a machine cuts out, it suddenly stops working for a short time
cut-out.tip: 主语是声音、信号或人都行：You're cutting out.（你那边断断续续的。）kept cutting out 是「老是断」。
cut-out.example: Sorry, you're cutting out — could you say that again?
cut-out.en: On top of the noise, Arjun's audio kept cutting out.
cut-out.szh: 除了噪音，Arjun 的声音还一直断断续续。

more.en: Sorry if I'm slow today, by the way — my Wi-Fi keeps cutting out.
more.szh: 对了，今天我回得慢的话见谅——我这边 Wi-Fi 老是断。

more.en: Lots of you were happy to lose those calls where somebody's sound kept cutting out.
more.szh: 很多人也庆幸，终于不用再开那种有人声音老断断续续的会了。

w-frozen.note: freeze 的过去分词；电脑、画面卡死都能说 freeze：My laptop froze.
w-frozen.en: Then it looked as if his screen had frozen, and for a moment the call went quiet.
w-frozen.szh: 接着他的画面看起来像是卡住了，通话一时安静了下来。

more.en: "People go on about expensive superfoods, but frozen peas are just as good for you," she says.
more.szh: 「大家老念叨那些贵得要命的超级食物，其实冷冻豌豆对身体一样好，」她说。

go-quiet.tip: go 在这里是「变得」，后面接形容词；同类说法还有 go red（脸红）、go wrong（出错）。
go-quiet.example: The room went quiet when the CEO walked in.
go-quiet.en: Then it looked as if his screen had frozen, and for a moment the call went quiet.
go-quiet.szh: 接着他的画面看起来像是卡住了，通话一时安静了下来。

more.en: While he was trying to restart it, the room went quiet, and his mind went blank.
more.szh: 他正忙着重启，会场一下子安静了，他的脑子一片空白。

hold-on.note: used to ask someone to wait for a short time
hold-on.tip: 口语里比 wait 客气；打电话常说 Hold on a second / Hold on a minute。
hold-on.example: Hold on — I just need to find the link.
hold-on.en: "Hold on," said Chen, and he headed for the window.
hold-on.szh: 「等一下，」小陈说着，走到了窗边。

more.en: Hold on — I've just found a small bug on older phones.
more.szh: 等一下——我刚在老款手机上发现一个小 bug。

more.en: Hold on, I thought.
more.szh: 等等，我心想。

by-the-way.note: used to add something, often on a different subject
by-the-way.tip: 用来顺带提一件事或转换话题，常放句首；anyway 是把话题拉回来，方向正好相反。
by-the-way.example: By the way, the client moved our call to Thursday.

more.en: Sorry if I'm slow today, by the way — my Wi-Fi keeps cutting out.
more.szh: 对了，今天我回得慢的话见谅——我这边 Wi-Fi 老是断。

more.en: Oh, by the way, "ASAP" is not a deadline.
more.szh: 哦，顺便说一句，「ASAP」可不是截止日期。

more.en: Dan keeps messaging me, by the way.
more.szh: 对了，Dan 一直给我发消息。

w-talented.note: 名词是 talent：She has a real talent for design.

go-live.note: if a product, website or system goes live, people can start using it
go-live.tip: 上线之后的状态用 be live：We're live! / The app is live. go 的过去式 went：It went live last night。
go-live.example: The new checkout page goes live on Monday.
go-live.en: We'll go live as soon as Arjun's fix is merged.
go-live.szh: Arjun 的修复一合并，我们就上线。

more.en: The app went live on time, and the new project's on track, isn't it?
more.szh: App 按时上线了，新项目也在按计划推进，对吧？

more.en: Rachel's team had to move a client meeting at short notice, and one feature went live a day late.
more.szh: Rachel 的团队临时改了一次客户会，还有一个功能晚了一天上线。

w-merge.note: 把分支合进主干：merge a branch / a pull request。
w-merge.en: We'll go live as soon as Arjun's fix is merged.
w-merge.szh: Arjun 的修复一合并，我们就上线。

on-track.note: making good progress and likely to finish on time
on-track.tip: on track for sth 说「有望按时完成某事」；偏离计划是 off track。right 加在前面表示「完全」。
on-track.example: Are we still on track for the Friday release?
on-track.en: But today we're right on track.
on-track.szh: 不过今天完全按计划走。

more.en: The app went live on time, and the new project's on track, isn't it?
more.szh: App 按时上线了，新项目也在按计划推进，对吧？

more.en: Decisions should be made within eight weeks, but my application was never on track.
more.szh: 按规定八周内就该给答复，可我的申请就没按时推进过。

sign-off-on.note: to give official approval to something
sign-off-on.tip: 不带宾语时去掉 on：I'm signing off.（我批了。）sign off 另一个意思是「（邮件、节目）结束、落款」。
sign-off-on.example: The manager has to sign off on the budget first.
sign-off-on.en: I won't sign off on anything until QA says it's OK.
sign-off-on.szh: QA 不点头，我什么都不签字放行。

more.en: Rachel signed off on the rest over breakfast, although she said they were still a bit long.
more.szh: Rachel 边吃早饭边批了剩下的，不过她说还是有点长。

w-qa.note: quality assurance 的缩写，常指测试团队，按字母读 Q-A。
w-qa.en: I won't sign off on anything until QA says it's OK.
w-qa.szh: QA 不点头，我什么都不签字放行。

keep-sb-posted.note: to keep telling someone the latest news about something
keep-sb-posted.tip: 人放中间：keep me / you / everyone posted；常用在一件事还没结束的时候，比 tell me 更口语。
keep-sb-posted.example: The client is still deciding — I'll keep you posted.
keep-sb-posted.szh: 所以有进展请随时告诉我。

more.en: Ask in advance, and keep people posted when plans change.
more.szh: 提前问，计划有变就及时告诉大家。

more.en: She just told me to keep her posted.
more.szh: 她只是让我有进展就告诉她。

w-fingers-crossed.note: 交叉手指是西方祈求好运的手势，说一句 Fingers crossed! 就是「但愿顺利」。

w-sideways.note: 手机横屏也叫 landscape，竖屏叫 portrait。
w-sideways.en: When you turn the phone sideways, our old friend the Save button disappears again.
w-sideways.szh: 把手机横过来，咱们的老朋友「保存」按钮又不见了。

at-the-last-minute.note: at the latest possible time, just before something happens
at-the-last-minute.tip: 常带「太晚了、来不及」的抱怨语气；当形容词用要加连字符：a last-minute change。
at-the-last-minute.example: The client changed the design at the last minute.
at-the-last-minute.en: At the last minute, of course!

more.en: And don't ask for things at the last minute.
more.szh: 还有，别到最后一刻才找人要东西。

double-check.note: to check something again to make sure it is correct
double-check.tip: 中间有连字符，一个词；后面可以直接接宾语，也可以接 that 从句：double-check that the link works。
double-check.example: Can you double-check the date before you send the invite?
double-check.szh: 他们正在把所有东西再核对一遍。

more.en: Finally, double-check your message before you press Send.
more.szh: 最后，按「发送」之前再检查一遍。

more.en: I double-checked the fix on all four.
more.szh: 我在四部手机上把修复后的效果都仔细测了一遍。

w-forgive.note: forgive sb for (doing) sth；过去式 forgave，过去分词 forgiven。
w-forgive.en: If we find another bug, my wife will never forgive me.
w-forgive.szh: 要是再冒出一个 bug，我老婆永远不会原谅我。

w-announce.note: 名词是 announcement；announce a new product 发布新产品。
w-announce.en: We announced it yesterday, and the post already has two thousand likes.
w-announce.szh: 我们昨天就发了公告，那条帖子已经有两千个赞了。

give-a-presentation.note: to talk to a group of people about a subject, often using slides
give-a-presentation.tip: 动词最常用 give，正式一点用 make，口语里也说 do a presentation；换个说法是 give a talk。
give-a-presentation.example: I have to give a presentation to the client on Monday.
give-a-presentation.en: On Wednesday evening, Rachel asked Chen to give a presentation to the whole company — in English.
give-a-presentation.szh: 周三晚上，Rachel 让小陈给全公司做一场报告——还得用英语。

more.en: I even gave a presentation about next year's plans without mentioning it once.
more.szh: 我甚至做了一次明年计划的分享，从头到尾一次都没提它。

more.en: He's giving a presentation in Leeds that morning, so he might be a bit late.
more.szh: 他那天上午要在利兹做个报告，可能会晚一点到。

at-short-notice.note: with very little warning or time to prepare
at-short-notice.tip: 英式说法，美式多说 on short notice；道歉时常加 such：Sorry to ask at such short notice。
at-short-notice.example: Thanks for joining the call at such short notice.
at-short-notice.en: The person who was supposed to speak had cancelled, so she needed someone at short notice.
at-short-notice.szh: 原本要讲的人临时来不了了，她得临时找个人顶上。

more.en: Rachel's team had to move a client meeting at short notice, and one feature went live a day late.
more.szh: Rachel 的团队临时改了一次客户会，还有一个功能晚了一天上线。

more.en: Tours are rarely cancelled at short notice.
more.szh: 导览很少临时取消。

w-packed.note: 口语常说 The train was packed.；意思接近 crowded，但更夸张。
w-packed.en: At ten o'clock, the room was so packed that people were standing at the back.
w-packed.szh: 十点钟，会议室挤得满满当当，后面的人只能站着。

more.en: The bus was packed, so the eggs were likely to break.
more.szh: 车上挤得要命，鸡蛋多半要碎。

go-blank.note: if your mind goes blank, you suddenly cannot remember or think of anything
go-blank.tip: 主语多是 mind；屏幕也能 go blank（黑屏）。go 在这里是「变得」，同类说法有 go quiet、go red。
go-blank.example: When the interviewer asked my first question, my mind went blank.
go-blank.en: While he was trying to restart it, the room went quiet, and his mind went blank.
go-blank.szh: 他正忙着重启，会场一下子安静了，他的脑子一片空白。

more.en: At stand-up, my mind nearly went blank, so I got straight to the point.
more.szh: 站会上我脑子差点一片空白，干脆直奔主题。

more.en: Quiz questions in English always make my mind go blank.
more.szh: 一碰到英文问答题，我脑子就一片空白。

keep-it-simple.note: to do something in a simple way, without too many details
keep-it-simple.tip: it 不指具体的东西，是固定说法；工程师常说的 KISS 原则就是 Keep it simple, stupid。
keep-it-simple.example: Keep it simple — one screen, one button.
keep-it-simple.en: So he decided to keep it simple and just tell them a story.
keep-it-simple.szh: 于是他决定简单点，就给大家讲个故事。

more.en: Don't worry, I'll keep it simple.
more.szh: 放心，我长话短说。

w-thanks-to.note: 后面接名词，多说好的原因；也能带点讽刺说坏结果：Thanks to the traffic, I was late.
w-thanks-to.en: Thanks to their app, she could finally video-call her grandson in Canada.
w-thanks-to.szh: 多亏了他们的 App，她终于能和远在加拿大的孙子视频通话了。

w-shake.note: 过去式 shook，过去分词 shaken；紧张时常说 My hands were shaking.
w-shake.en: Even though his voice was shaking at first, the audience listened.
w-shake.szh: 虽然一开始他的声音在发抖，大家还是认真听着。

w-audience.note: 指全体听众，是一个整体；说其中一个人用 a member of the audience。
w-audience.en: Even though his voice was shaking at first, the audience listened.
w-audience.szh: 虽然一开始他的声音在发抖，大家还是认真听着。

speak-up.note: to speak more loudly so that people can hear you
speak-up.tip: 还有「站出来说话、发表意见」的意思：Don't be afraid to speak up in meetings。
speak-up.example: Could you speak up a bit? The line is bad.
speak-up.en: He spoke up so that the people at the back could hear.
speak-up.szh: 他提高了嗓门，好让后排的人也听得见。

more.en: If you can't hear me at the back, please speak up, because the next group is right behind us.
more.szh: 后面要是听不见，请大声说一下，因为下一组游客就紧跟在我们后面。

get-your-message-across.zh: 把意思讲清楚；让人听明白
get-your-message-across.note: to make people understand what you want to tell them
get-your-message-across.tip: your 随主语变：get his / her / our message across；across 不能丢。
get-your-message-across.example: Short sentences help you get your message across.
get-your-message-across.en: And slowly, he got his message across.
get-your-message-across.szh: 慢慢地，他把想说的都讲清楚了。

more.en: She was good at getting her message across without saying much.
more.szh: 她很会用不多的几句话把意思讲明白。

more.en: Perfect. You've got your message across.
more.szh: 完美，意思说得很清楚。

w-afterwards.note: 英式常用 afterwards，美式多说 afterward；放句首、句末都可以。

w-ban.note: ban sth / ban sb from doing sth；过去式 banned 要双写 n。名词 a ban on sth。
w-ban.en: Then he banned slides for a month.
w-ban.szh: 接着，他宣布一个月内禁用幻灯片。

w-the-hard-way.note: learn sth the hard way 是「吃了苦头才明白」；反过来是 the easy way。
w-the-hard-way.en: Everything I'm going to tell you, I've learned the hard way.
w-the-hard-way.szh: 下面要说的，全是我吃过亏才学到的。

get-to-the-point.note: to start talking or writing about the most important thing
get-to-the-point.tip: 对别人说 Could you get to the point?（能说重点吗？），就算用了 could 也透着不耐烦，开会时要慎用；自己先说 Let me get to the point 就很自然。
get-to-the-point.example: I'll get to the point: we need two more developers.
get-to-the-point.en: First, get to the point in the first line.

more.en: At stand-up, my mind nearly went blank, so I got straight to the point.
more.szh: 站会上我脑子差点一片空白，干脆直奔主题。

more.en: "A teacher's job is simple," she says, getting straight to the point.
more.szh: 「老师的活儿很简单，」她开门见山地说。

make-it-clear.note: to say or show something in a way that people cannot misunderstand
make-it-clear.tip: it 是形式宾语，真正的内容在后面：make it clear who / that / what …；也可以说 make sth clear。
make-it-clear.example: Please make it clear in the ticket which version you tested.
make-it-clear.en: Second, make it clear who should act.

more.en: She made it clear that she'd never give you the answer.
more.szh: 她早就说明白了：答案她是绝不会直接给你的。

more.en: Before I could make it clear that my name was Chen, our team got registered as "Shane and the Taylors".
more.szh: 我还没来得及说清楚我叫小陈，我们队就被登记成了「Shane 和 Taylor 一家」。

step-by-step.note: doing one thing at a time, in a fixed order
step-by-step.tip: 当副词放在动词后面；放在名词前要加连字符：a step-by-step guide。
step-by-step.example: The guide explains the setup step by step.
step-by-step.en: Third, describe bugs step by step.
step-by-step.szh: 第三，一步一步地描述 bug。

more.en: A week later, I took it apart, step by step.
more.szh: 一个星期后，我一步一步把它拆了。

more.en: It was my grandfather's, and he taught me to use it step by step.
more.szh: 那是我爷爷的，是他一步一步教我用的。

w-reproduce.note: 开发里常说 reproduce a bug，口语缩写成 repro；平时也指「复制、繁殖」。
w-reproduce.en: Write down every step so that anyone can reproduce the problem.
w-reproduce.szh: 把每一步都写下来，好让谁都能复现问题。

w-screenshot.note: 截图是 take a screenshot；口语里也直接当动词：screenshot the error。
w-screenshot.en: Add a screenshot to save time.

in-detail.note: including all the facts and small parts of something
in-detail.tip: detail 在这里不加 s，也不加冠词；「更详细地」说 in more detail。
in-detail.example: We'll discuss the design in detail on Thursday.
in-detail.en: But you don't need to explain the whole history in detail.
in-detail.szh: 不过来龙去脉不用写得那么细。

more.en: I got up first thing in the morning for Margaret's walk along the walls, and she explained every gate in detail.
more.szh: 我一大早就起床去参加 Margaret 的城墙徒步，每一座城门她都讲得清清楚楚。

it-s-a-good-idea-to.note: used to give advice in a friendly way
it-s-a-good-idea-to.tip: 后面接动词原形；比 you should 委婉，像在给朋友出主意。否定说 It's not a good idea to …。
it-s-a-good-idea-to.example: It's a good idea to back up your work before the update.
it-s-a-good-idea-to.en: It's a good idea to end with one simple question.
it-s-a-good-idea-to.szh: 最好用一个简单的问题结尾。

more.en: "It's a good idea to stop using screens an hour before bed," she said.
more.szh: 「睡前一个小时最好别再看屏幕，」她说。

be-on-the-same-page.zh: 想法一致；（对情况）理解一致
be-on-the-same-page.note: to understand a situation in the same way as other people
be-on-the-same-page.tip: 开会常用：Are we on the same page?（大家理解一致吧？）不是「在同一页」的字面意思。
be-on-the-same-page.example: Before we start, let's make sure we're all on the same page.
be-on-the-same-page.en: That way, everyone's on the same page.
be-on-the-same-page.szh: 这样大家就不会各想各的了。

more.en: Are we all on the same page so far?
more.szh: 到这儿大家都跟上了吧？

w-second-opinion.note: 原指「再找一位医生看看」；工作里指请另一个人再看一遍、给个意见。
w-second-opinion.szh: 第五，请别人帮你把把关。

w-complaint.note: 动词是 complain；正式投诉是 make a complaint。
w-complaint.en: If it sounds like a complaint, you'd better rewrite it.
w-complaint.szh: 要是读起来像在抱怨，最好重写。

w-ignore.note: 工作群里常见的一句「请忽略上一条」；ignore sb 是「不理某人」。
w-ignore.en: Then you'll never have to write, "Please ignore my last message."
w-ignore.szh: 这样你就永远不用再发「请忽略我上一条消息」了。

have-a-chat.note: to talk with someone in a friendly, informal way
have-a-chat.tip: 比 talk 随意；chat 也能当动词：We chatted for an hour。英式口语常说 have a quick chat。
have-a-chat.example: Have you got five minutes? I'd like to have a chat about the new project.
have-a-chat.en: It's so nice to have a chat, isn't it?

more.en: At the end of our chat, I asked how many portions she'd had that day.
more.szh: 聊到最后，我问她那天吃了几份蔬果。

w-proper.note: 英式口语很常用：a proper breakfast（一顿像样的早餐）；副词 properly 是「好好地」：let's catch up properly。
w-proper.en: I promised you a proper coffee, and I've kept my promise, haven't I?
w-proper.szh: 我答应过请你喝杯像样的咖啡，说到做到了吧？

w-silly.note: 对方客气时回一句 Don't be silly，意思是「别客气了」，语气亲切，不是骂人。
w-silly.en: Don't be silly, it's my treat.

more.en: You ought to warm up for five minutes first, even if you feel silly walking fast round the park.
more.szh: 跑之前应该先热身五分钟，哪怕绕着公园快走会觉得自己有点傻。

w-treat.note: It's my treat. / My treat. 都是「我请」；动词 treat sb to sth 是「请某人吃…」。
w-treat.en: Don't be silly, it's my treat.

catch-up.note: to talk to someone you have not seen for a while and hear their news
catch-up.tip: 跟谁叙旧用 with：catch up with sb；另一个常见意思是「补上落下的」：I need to catch up on my emails。
catch-up.example: Let's grab a coffee next week and catch up.

more.en: When Chen was ill for a month, she helped him catch up.
more.szh: 小陈病了一个月，是她帮他把落下的课补上的。

more.en: The people on the stairs can catch up.
more.szh: 楼梯上的朋友可以跟上来。

w-hardly.note: hardly 本身就是否定，后面不再加 not；它也不是 hard 的副词，「努力地」还是 hard。
w-hardly.en: I used to be so nervous on calls that I hardly said a word.
w-hardly.szh: 以前开视频会，我紧张得几乎一句话都不敢说。

make-progress.note: to improve, or to move forward towards a goal
make-progress.tip: progress 不可数：make a lot of progress，不说 make progresses；动词用 make，不用 do 或 get。
make-progress.example: We're making good progress on the new design.
make-progress.en: You've made a lot of progress.

more.en: Last week, Rachel told me I was making good progress.
more.szh: 上周 Rachel 还跟我说，我进步很大。

more.en: By half past ten, he's switched off the light and feels he's making progress.
more.szh: 十点半，他已经关了灯，觉得自己总算有进步了。

all-in-all.note: used to give a general opinion after thinking about every part of something
all-in-all.tip: 多放在句首、后面加逗号，用来做总结；比生硬的 in a word 自然得多。
all-in-all.example: There were a few problems, but all in all the launch went well.
all-in-all.en: All in all, it's been a good year.
all-in-all.szh: 总的来说，这一年挺好的。

more.en: So, all in all, it was the most expensive lesson my dad ever paid for.
more.szh: 所以总的来说，这是我爸付过的最贵的一堂课。

more.en: All in all, I've had the time of my life.
more.szh: 总之，这一周是我过得最开心的日子。

w-disaster.note: 口语里常夸张地用来说搞砸了的事：The meeting was a disaster.
w-disaster.en: But we've had a few disasters, haven't we?
w-disaster.szh: 不过也出过几次大乱子，是吧？

look-on-the-bright-side.zh: 往好处想；看到好的一面
look-on-the-bright-side.note: to find something good in a bad situation
look-on-the-bright-side.tip: 常跟在坏消息后面，冒号或破折号后接「好的一面」：Look on the bright side: …
look-on-the-bright-side.example: The flight was cancelled, but look on the bright side — we get an extra day here.
look-on-the-bright-side.en: Look on the bright side: we don't write it any more.
look-on-the-bright-side.szh: 往好处想：咱们再也不用写它了。

more.en: Look on the bright side — you'll probably find things you forgot you had.
more.szh: 往好处想——说不定能翻出你自己都忘了的东西。

w-practise.note: 英式拼写：动词是 practise，名词是 practice；美式两者都写 practice。
w-practise.en: My son practises every day — it sounds like a building site at home.
w-practise.szh: 我儿子天天练，家里听着跟工地似的。

keep-up-the-good-work.note: used to tell someone to continue doing something well
keep-up-the-good-work.tip: 多是上级、老师对人说的鼓励话，常跟在表扬后面；the good work 是固定说法。
keep-up-the-good-work.example: Great demo today, everyone — keep up the good work!
keep-up-the-good-work.en: Anyway, keep up the good work, Chen.

more.en: Calling tonight was a good first step, so keep up the good work.
more.szh: 今晚打这个电话就是很好的第一步，继续保持。

first-thing-in-the-morning.note: very early in the morning, before you do anything else
first-thing-in-the-morning.tip: 整块用，first 前面不加 the；也常放句尾：I'll call you first thing tomorrow.
first-thing-in-the-morning.example: I'll send you the report first thing in the morning.
first-thing-in-the-morning.en: First thing in the morning, I make coffee while my flatmate Tom's still asleep, so I don't have to make small talk.
first-thing-in-the-morning.szh: 早上一起来，我先煮咖啡，这时候室友 Tom 还在睡，我也就不用跟人寒暄。

more.en: On Saturdays, I switched the computer on first thing in the morning and left it running all day.
more.szh: 每个星期六，我一大早就开机，让它开一整天。

more.en: He always follows up first thing in the morning.
more.szh: 他总是第二天一早再跟进。

more.en: I got up first thing in the morning for Margaret's walk along the walls, and she explained every gate in detail.
more.szh: 我一大早就起床去参加 Margaret 的城墙徒步，每一座城门她都讲得清清楚楚。

w-to-do-list.note: make / write a to-do list；清单上的一项叫 item。
w-to-do-list.en: Instead, I enjoy writing a short to-do list on paper.
w-to-do-list.szh: 我更喜欢在纸上写一张短短的待办清单。

go-through-sth.note: to look at or check something carefully from beginning to end
go-through-sth.tip: through 后面直接接要检查的东西：go through the list / your notes / the code；另一个常见意思是「经历（难事）」：go through a hard time。
go-through-sth.example: Let's go through the slides before the client arrives.
go-through-sth.en: This morning, I went through the list at a quarter past eight.
go-through-sth.szh: 今天早上八点一刻，我把清单过了一遍。

more.en: Let's go through my list, then.
more.szh: 那我们把我的清单过一遍吧。

more.en: He goes through his options: a pillow, a drawer, the window.
more.szh: 他把办法挨个想了一遍：拿枕头捂上、塞进抽屉、扔出窗外。

w-release-notes.note: App 每次更新时写给用户看的「这次改了什么」，总是用复数。
w-release-notes.en: Login screen, release notes — Rachel asked me to look after those — and a reply to Arjun.
w-release-notes.szh: 登录页、发版说明——这个是 Rachel 让我负责的——还有回 Arjun 一条消息。

have-a-quick-look-at-sth.text: have a quick look at sth
have-a-quick-look-at-sth.note: to look at something for a short time
have-a-quick-look-at-sth.tip: 英式口语很常用，比 look at 随意；美式更常说 take a quick look。at 别丢：have a look at sth。
have-a-quick-look-at-sth.example: Could you have a quick look at my email before I send it?
have-a-quick-look-at-sth.en: Then I had a quick look at an old bug, just for five minutes.
have-a-quick-look-at-sth.szh: 然后我去瞄了一眼一个老 bug，说好就看五分钟。

more.en: I put my backpack on the rack above them, and Tom had a quick look at the little screen.
more.szh: 我把背包放到他们头顶的行李架上，Tom 凑过去看了一眼座位上方的小屏幕。

more.en: Feel free to have a quick look at it now.
more.szh: 你现在就可以去看一眼。

get-distracted.note: to stop paying attention to what you are doing because something else gets your interest
get-distracted.tip: 被什么分心用 by：get distracted by the news。别说 I distracted（那是「我让别人分心」）。
get-distracted.example: I get distracted when my phone is on the desk.
get-distracted.en: Then I got distracted by a comment someone wrote back in 2019.
get-distracted.szh: 后来又被一行 2019 年留下的注释勾住了。

more.en: Leave your phone at home, or you'll only get distracted.
more.szh: 手机放家里，不然你只会分心。

w-comment.note: 写代码时留给别人看的说明；平时也指评论：leave a comment。
w-comment.en: Then I got distracted by a comment someone wrote back in 2019.
w-comment.szh: 后来又被一行 2019 年留下的注释勾住了。

w-seriously.note: 单独一个词放在句尾，是加重语气：「我不是开玩笑」。也能当疑问：Seriously?（不会吧？）
w-seriously.szh: 上面写着：「别碰这里。我是认真的。」

lose-track-of-time.zh: 忘了时间；不知不觉过了很久
lose-track-of-time.note: to forget what time it is because you are busy or interested in something
lose-track-of-time.tip: track 在这里是「跟踪、掌握」；lose track of 后面还能接别的：lose track of the score（记不清比分了）。
lose-track-of-time.example: We were chatting so much that we lost track of time.
lose-track-of-time.en: So of course I touched it, and I completely lost track of time.
lose-track-of-time.szh: 那我当然就碰了，然后完全忘了时间。

more.en: "When you're busy, you lose track of time and eat whatever's nearest."
more.szh: 「一忙起来就忘了时间，手边有什么就吃什么。」

be-in-a-good-mood.tip: 反过来是 be in a bad mood；mood 是一时的心情，不是性格。
be-in-a-good-mood.example: The boss is in a good mood today — ask her now.
be-in-a-good-mood.en: I was in a good mood, and I don't mind talking first.
be-in-a-good-mood.szh: 我心情不错，第一个发言也无所谓。

more.en: And you were in a very good mood for someone who'd just done fifty squats.
more.szh: 一个刚做完五十个深蹲的人，心情未免也太好了。

w-cancelled.note: 英式拼写双写 l：cancelled、cancelling；美式是 canceled。
w-cancelled.en: "Stand-up cancelled today — my train's delayed. Enjoy the extra hour!"
w-cancelled.szh: 「今天站会取消——我的火车晚点了。好好享受多出来的一小时吧！」

w-delayed.note: 火车、航班晚点最常用 be delayed；晚了多久：delayed by 20 minutes。
w-delayed.en: "Stand-up cancelled today — my train's delayed. Enjoy the extra hour!"
w-delayed.szh: 「今天站会取消——我的火车晚点了。好好享受多出来的一小时吧！」

fill-sb-in.zh: 给某人讲讲情况；补上信息
fill-sb-in.note: to tell someone the details of something they do not know yet
fill-sb-in.tip: 人放在 fill 和 in 中间：fill me in；讲的内容用 on：fill sb in on the project。
fill-sb-in.example: I missed the meeting — can you fill me in?
fill-sb-in.en: I'm Chen. Rachel asked me to fill you in on the app.
fill-sb-in.szh: 我是小陈。Rachel 让我给你讲讲这个 App 的情况。

more.en: And someone needs to fill him in on the kitchen rules, so he doesn't take anyone's milk.
more.szh: 还得有人跟他讲讲茶水间的规矩，免得他拿了别人的牛奶。

more.en: Tom's fast asleep, so I'll fill you in on my week.
more.szh: Tom 睡得正香，那我给大家讲讲我这一周。

w-right.zh: 好吧；行（表示听到了、接受了）
w-right.note: 单独一个 Right. 不是「对」，是「好吧，知道了」，语气平平，常带点无奈。

w-ticket.note: IT 工作里指系统里的一条任务或问题；平时是「票」：a train ticket。
w-ticket.en: And I'm planning to read every old ticket in the bug tracker.
w-ticket.szh: 还打算把 bug 系统里的旧工单全读一遍。

w-bug-tracker.note: 记录、分配和跟进 bug 的工具，比如 Jira。track 是「跟踪」。
w-bug-tracker.en: And I'm planning to read every old ticket in the bug tracker.
w-bug-tracker.szh: 还打算把 bug 系统里的旧工单全读一遍。

w-typo.note: typing error 的简称；make a typo 打错字。
w-typo.en: And I've already managed to find three typos in the welcome email.
w-typo.szh: 而且已经在欢迎邮件里挑出三个错别字了。

w-welcome-email.note: 新人入职或新用户注册时收到的第一封邮件。
w-welcome-email.en: And I've already managed to find three typos in the welcome email.
w-welcome-email.szh: 而且已经在欢迎邮件里挑出三个错别字了。

w-expect.note: expect sb to do 指望某人做某事；也有「预计」的意思：I expect it'll rain。
w-expect.en: Nobody expects you to take responsibility for the whole app in your first week.
w-expect.szh: 没人指望你第一周就把整个 App 扛起来。

show-sb-the-ropes.zh: 教某人入门；带某人熟悉门道
show-sb-the-ropes.note: to teach someone how to do a job or how things work in a new place
show-sb-the-ropes.tip: ropes 总是复数；自己「摸清门道」说 learn the ropes。只用在新人身上，不能说 show sb the rope。
show-sb-the-ropes.example: Sam will show you the ropes on your first day.
show-sb-the-ropes.en: Come on, I'll show you the ropes.

more.en: We ended up standing by the doors in coach H, and Tom showed me the ropes.
more.szh: 最后我们只好跑到 H 车厢的车门边站着，Tom 顺便给我讲了讲坐火车的门道。

more.en: The owner insists on showing him the ropes, even though it's only got two buttons.
more.szh: 店老板非要手把手教他怎么用，虽然那闹钟一共就两个按钮。

feel-free-to-do.note: used to tell someone that they can do something if they want to
feel-free-to-do.tip: 常用祈使句，客气又热情；后面接 to do：feel free to ask，不说 feel free asking。
feel-free-to-do.example: Feel free to call me if you have any problems.
feel-free-to-do.en: And feel free to ask me anything.

more.en: Morning! Feel free to pick it up.
more.szh: 早上好！随便拿起来看。

more.en: Feel free to have a quick look at it now.
more.szh: 你现在就可以去看一眼。

out-of-curiosity.note: because you want to know something, not for any special reason
out-of-curiosity.tip: 问私人一点的问题前加一句，显得没有恶意；常说 just out of curiosity。
out-of-curiosity.example: Just out of curiosity, how much did your new laptop cost?
out-of-curiosity.en: So, out of curiosity, why did you choose testing?
out-of-curiosity.szh: 对了，我好奇问一句，你为什么选了做测试？

more.en: Quick question, out of curiosity.
more.szh: 问你个事，纯属好奇。

that-s-a-good-question.zh: 问得好（常用来争取时间或回避）
that-s-a-good-question.note: something you say when you need time to think, or when you do not know the answer
that-s-a-good-question.tip: 不一定是夸对方，很多时候意思是「这个我也答不上来」。语气要靠上下文听。
that-s-a-good-question.example: "When will it be ready?" "That's a good question."

more.en: Well, Nadia, that's a good question.
more.szh: 嗯，Nadia，这个问题问得好。

get-the-hang-of-sth.note: to learn how to do something, especially after some practice
get-the-hang-of-sth.tip: 最常见的是 get the hang of it；hang 在这里没有「挂」的意思，整块记。
get-the-hang-of-sth.example: Driving on the left is strange at first, but you'll get the hang of it.
get-the-hang-of-sth.en: You're getting the hang of it, aren't you?
get-the-hang-of-sth.szh: 你已经慢慢上手了，对吧？

more.en: He soon got the hang of it, but he still wouldn't eat it.
more.szh: 他很快就学会了，可还是不肯吃。

w-error.note: get an error 报错；error message 报错信息。比 mistake 正式，机器出错多用 error。
w-error.en: Login isn't working, and I keep getting the same error on all my test phones.
w-error.szh: 登录用不了，我所有测试机都一直报同一个错。

more.en: In plain words, a one-off server error copied an empty list over your real one.
more.szh: 说白了，就是服务器偶然出了一次错，用一张空清单盖掉了你们真正的清单。

go-down.note: if a computer system goes down, it stops working
go-down.tip: IT 里最常用的说法，主语是系统、服务器、网络；恢复了说 be back up / be back to normal。
go-down.example: The website went down for two hours last night.
go-down.en: Looks like the login server's gone down.
go-down.szh: 看样子是登录服务器挂了。

more.en: Then the wifi went down, and a guard came along and looked over our tickets.
more.szh: 后来车上的 Wi-Fi 断了，一位列车员过来把我们的票查了一遍。

more.en: To be honest, my standards went down a bit when I moved in with Tom.
more.szh: 说实话，跟 Tom 合租以后，我的标准是降了点。

more.en: So that's why the Wi-Fi kept going down at night?
more.szh: 难怪一到晚上网就老断？

i-m-on-it.note: used to say that you have started dealing with a problem or task
i-m-on-it.tip: 工作群里很常见，说明「我已经在处理了」，别人就不用再动手；不能说 I'm on this problem。
i-m-on-it.example: "Can someone check the payment page?" "I'm on it."

more.en: So, the family emailed me a photo at nine on Sunday night, and I wrote back, "I'm on it."
more.szh: 是这样，周日晚上九点，他们家给我发了张照片，我回了一句：「马上处理。」

more.en: Whenever her boss emails her late in the afternoon, she says "I'm on it" and makes another flat white.
more.szh: 每次老板快下班了还发邮件派活儿，她就回一句「马上办」，然后再冲一杯馥芮白。

grab-a-bite.tip: 口语，吃得快、吃得简单；也说 grab a bite to eat。正式场合说 have lunch / have something to eat。
grab-a-bite.example: Let's grab a bite before the film starts.
grab-a-bite.en: I was heading for the door to grab a bite, but dinner can wait.
grab-a-bite.szh: 我正要出门随便吃点东西，晚饭等等再说。

more.en: Now let's grab a bite and buy Mum's pickle.
more.szh: 走，先随便吃点，再给我妈买罐酱。

more.en: Every evening I get home at six, grab a bite and sit on the same sofa with the same three apps until midnight.
more.szh: 每天晚上六点到家，随便吃两口，然后坐在同一张沙发上，刷同样三个 App，一直刷到半夜。

in-the-meantime.note: in the period of time between two events
in-the-meantime.tip: 常放句首加逗号；也可以放句尾：Let's wait and see in the meantime。
in-the-meantime.example: The engineer is coming at three. In the meantime, please don't use the lift.
in-the-meantime.en: In the meantime, could everyone please stop pushing new code?
in-the-meantime.szh: 这段时间大家先别推新代码了，好吗？

more.en: He left the slices in salt for twenty minutes, and in the meantime, he beat the eggs.
more.szh: 苦瓜片用盐腌二十分钟，趁这工夫，他把鸡蛋打散。

w-push.note: 程序员用语：把本地的代码改动传到共享的代码库，来自 git push 这个命令。
w-push.en: In the meantime, could everyone please stop pushing new code?
w-push.szh: 这段时间大家先别推新代码了，好吗？

get-to-the-bottom-of-sth.text: get to the bottom of sth
get-to-the-bottom-of-sth.zh: 查个水落石出；弄清根本原因
get-to-the-bottom-of-sth.note: to find out the real cause of a problem
get-to-the-bottom-of-sth.tip: 说的是查问题、查原因，不用在「读到底」上；后面常跟 it / this / the problem。
get-to-the-bottom-of-sth.example: We need to get to the bottom of these crashes.
get-to-the-bottom-of-sth.en: To get to the bottom of it, I need to know one thing.
get-to-the-bottom-of-sth.szh: 要查清楚，我得先知道一件事。

more.en: Pens kept disappearing from a drawer at the nurses' station, and it took a week to get to the bottom of it.
more.szh: 护士站抽屉里的笔老是不见，查了一个星期才弄清楚。

w-certificate.note: 网站用来证明「我是我」的电子证书，有有效期，过期了就连不上。平时也指证书、证明：a birth certificate。
w-certificate.en: Did anyone remember to renew the security certificate?
w-certificate.szh: 有人记得给安全证书续期吗？

more.en: "Most of our adult students want a second chance, not a certificate," said the college director, Sunita Rao.
more.szh: 「我们大多数成年学生想要的是第二次机会，而不是一张证书，」学院院长 Sunita Rao 说。

w-reminder.note: set a reminder 设提醒；动词是 remind sb to do sth。
w-reminder.en: I see your point, but a reminder only works if somebody reads it.
w-reminder.szh: 你说得有道理，可提醒也得有人看才管用。

w-midday.note: 就是 12 p.m.，英式常说 midday，也说 noon。午夜是 midnight。
w-midday.en: OK, the certificate ran out at midday.
w-midday.szh: 好，证书中午十二点到期了。

w-renew.note: renew a passport / a contract / a subscription：到期前再续一段时间。

be-back-to-normal.note: to be the way it usually is again after a problem
be-back-to-normal.tip: normal 前面不加 the；「慢慢恢复」说 get back to normal。
be-back-to-normal.example: The trains are back to normal after the strike.

more.en: And if you miss a week, you'll be back to normal in a few days.
more.szh: 哪周没跑也没关系，几天就能恢复过来。

be-out-of-the-office.zh: 不在办公室；外出（不上班）
be-out-of-the-office.note: to be away from work, for example on holiday or at an appointment
be-out-of-the-office.tip: 自动回复邮件里最常见：out-of-office reply。只说人不在，不说明原因，比 I'm absent 自然得多。
be-out-of-the-office.example: I'm out of the office until Monday, so please email Sam.
be-out-of-the-office.en: I'm afraid I'll be out of the office tomorrow morning.
be-out-of-the-office.szh: 明天上午我恐怕来不了办公室了。

more.en: Anyway, I'm out of the office until next Monday, so I've got all week to practise.
more.szh: 反正我下周一之前都不用上班，有一整个星期可以练。

more.en: Even when I'm out of the office on holiday, I just kill time on my phone.
more.szh: 就连休假不用上班的时候，我也就是拿着手机打发时间。

w-crack.note: crack a tooth 把牙咬裂；名词也是 crack（裂缝）：a crack in the screen。
w-crack.en: I cracked a tooth on Tom's homemade toffee at dinner.
w-crack.szh: 晚饭吃 Tom 自己做的太妃糖，把一颗牙咬裂了。

more.en: Bad news from the kiln, I'm afraid: your mug for Tom has cracked.
more.szh: 恐怕是个坏消息：你给 Tom 做的杯子在窑里裂了。

w-homemade.note: homemade bread / cake；反义是 shop-bought（店里买的）。
w-homemade.en: I cracked a tooth on Tom's homemade toffee at dinner.
w-homemade.szh: 晚饭吃 Tom 自己做的太妃糖，把一颗牙咬裂了。

w-toffee.note: 用黄油和糖熬的硬糖，英国很常见，咬起来很黏、很硬。
w-toffee.en: I cracked a tooth on Tom's homemade toffee at dinner.
w-toffee.szh: 晚饭吃 Tom 自己做的太妃糖，把一颗牙咬裂了。

hand-sth-over.note: to give work or responsibility for something to another person
hand-sth-over.tip: 交给谁用 to；代词放中间：hand it over to Mia。名词 handover 就是「交接」。
hand-sth-over.example: Before her holiday, she handed the project over to me.
hand-sth-over.en: I've handed the login screen over to Mia.
hand-sth-over.szh: 登录页我已经交给 Mia 了。

more.en: They put the coin in a sandwich bag, just in case, and handed it over on Monday morning.
more.szh: 他们把硬币装进一个三明治袋，以防万一，周一上午就交给了我们。

more.en: It's been handed over to the cleaners.
more.szh: 已经转交给保洁阿姨了。

let-sb-know.zh: 告诉某人一声；通知某人
let-sb-know.tip: 比 tell 更随和，邮件结尾常用：Let me know what you think. know 前面不加 to。
let-sb-know.example: Let me know if you need anything else.
let-sb-know.en: And I've asked her to let Arjun know when the tests pass.
let-sb-know.szh: 也让她等测试过了跟 Arjun 说一声。

more.en: Every few weeks, someone promised to let me know "very soon".
more.szh: 每隔几个星期，就有人答应「很快」给我回音。

more.en: And let me know how everything is on Ward 6.
more.szh: 也跟我说说六病区最近怎么样。

w-kindly.note: 放在动词前，表示对方帮忙是出于好意：kindly offered 好心主动提出。也常用来客气地请求：Could you kindly …?
w-kindly.en: Arjun's kindly offered to cover for me at the eleven o'clock call with the client.
w-kindly.szh: Arjun 人很好，主动说十一点跟客户的电话会帮我顶一下。

cover-for-sb.note: to do someone's work while they are away
cover-for-sb.tip: for 后面接被顶替的人；也有「替某人打掩护」的意思，要看上下文。
cover-for-sb.example: Can you cover for me on Friday? I've got a doctor's appointment.
cover-for-sb.en: Arjun's kindly offered to cover for me at the eleven o'clock call with the client.
cover-for-sb.szh: Arjun 人很好，主动说十一点跟客户的电话会帮我顶一下。

more.en: I'm Dan, I've been a trainer in Hackney for fifteen years, and Kim is covering for me at the gym tonight.
more.szh: 我是 Dan，在哈克尼当了十五年健身教练，今晚健身房那边是 Kim 替我顶班。

if-anything-comes-up.zh: 有什么事的话；万一出了状况
if-anything-comes-up.note: if something happens that needs attention, especially something you did not plan for
if-anything-comes-up.tip: come up 是「（意外地）出现」；if 从句里用一般现在时 comes，不用 will come。
if-anything-comes-up.example: I'll be at home all day, so call me if anything comes up.

more.en: She told me to email customer service if anything else came up.
more.szh: 她让我以后再有什么问题，就给客服发邮件。

get-in-touch-with-sb.note: to contact someone by phone, email or message
get-in-touch-with-sb.tip: 说的是「联系上」这个动作；保持联系是 keep in touch（第 4 课）。
get-in-touch-with-sb.example: Please get in touch with our support team if the app stops working.
get-in-touch-with-sb.en: Then please get in touch with me by text, not by phone.
get-in-touch-with-sb.szh: 那就发短信联系我，别打电话。

more.en: Mum got in touch with me last week just to check you were eating your vegetables.
more.szh: 上周妈专门联系我，就为了问你有没有好好吃菜。

w-filling.note: have a filling 补牙。也指食物的馅：pie filling。
w-filling.en: Chen, it's a filling, not a holiday.
w-filling.szh: 小陈，你这是去补个牙，又不是去度假。

w-handover.note: 来自 hand over；write a handover 写交接文档。
w-handover.en: But to be honest, this is the best handover we've ever had.
w-handover.szh: 不过说实话，这是我们有过的最好的一次交接。

more.en: Handover takes thirty minutes, and people take their breaks seriously.
more.szh: 交接班要半个小时，大家也很把休息当回事。

w-export.note: 软件里把内容存成别的格式：export to PDF / Excel。另一个意思是「出口（货物）」。
w-export.en: Last March, users kept asking us to add "Export to PDF", and Rachel asked me to do it.
w-export.szh: 去年三月，用户一直要我们加个「导出为 PDF」，Rachel 就让我来做。

keep-meaning-to-do.note: to plan to do something many times but not actually do it
keep-meaning-to-do.tip: mean to do 是「打算做」，加上 keep 就是「老想着、老没做」，带一点愧疚。meaning 后面接 to do。
keep-meaning-to-do.example: I keep meaning to call my grandmother, but the week just goes.
keep-meaning-to-do.en: I kept meaning to start it, but I never got round to it.
keep-meaning-to-do.szh: 我一直想着要动手，可就是没顾上。

more.en: We keep meaning to visit the museum, and now we've got a very good reason!
more.szh: 我们一直说要去博物馆看看，这下总算有个特别好的理由了！

more.en: "Most people keep meaning to eat better," she told me.
more.szh: 「大多数人一直都打算吃得健康点，」她跟我说。

get-round-to-sth.note: to finally do something that you have wanted or planned to do for a long time
get-round-to-sth.tip: 英式说 round，美式说 around；后面接名词或 doing：get round to answering emails。
get-round-to-sth.example: I finally got round to fixing the bike last weekend.
get-round-to-sth.en: I kept meaning to start it, but I never got round to it.
get-round-to-sth.szh: 我一直想着要动手，可就是没顾上。

more.en: I was about to give up when they finally got round to it last spring.
more.szh: 我都准备放弃了，结果去年春天他们总算处理了。

more.en: So when exactly are you going to get round to going back?
more.szh: 那你到底打算什么时候回去？

w-secretly.note: 形容词是 secret；secretly hope / want 是「心里偷偷盼着」，嘴上不说。
w-secretly.en: At every stand-up, I secretly wanted someone else to offer.
w-secretly.szh: 每次站会，我心里都盼着别人主动接过去。

w-offer.note: 单独用 offer 就是「主动说我来」；后面也能接 to do：offer to help。
w-offer.en: At every stand-up, I secretly wanted someone else to offer.
w-offer.szh: 每次站会，我心里都盼着别人主动接过去。

drag-on.note: to continue for longer than you want or expect
drag-on.tip: 主语是事情（会议、项目、谈判），不是人；常和 for + 时间连用。
drag-on.example: The meeting dragged on until seven.
drag-on.en: Anyway, the whole thing dragged on for eight months.
drag-on.szh: 总之，这事就这么拖了八个月。

more.en: Planning this lunch has dragged on all week, but we're nearly there.
more.szh: 这顿饭筹划了整整一个星期，总算快搞定了。

more.en: To be honest, the first week dragged on.
more.szh: 说实话，第一个星期特别难熬。

w-feature.note: App 里能用的一项功能就是一个 feature：add a new feature 加新功能。平时也指「特点、特色」。
w-feature.en: New features felt more exciting, and the button felt like a waste of time.
w-feature.szh: 新功能做起来更带劲，这个按钮感觉就是浪费时间。

a-waste-of-time.note: something that is not useful or does not give good results
a-waste-of-time.tip: a 不能丢；加强语气说 a complete / total waste of time。浪费钱是 a waste of money。
a-waste-of-time.example: That meeting was a complete waste of time.
a-waste-of-time.en: New features felt more exciting, and the button felt like a waste of time.
a-waste-of-time.szh: 新功能做起来更带劲，这个按钮感觉就是浪费时间。

more.en: Honestly, arguing with her felt like a waste of time.
more.szh: 说真的，再跟她争下去也是白费工夫。

w-mention.note: mention sth 直接接宾语，不加 about：mention the problem，不说 mention about it。
w-mention.en: I even gave a presentation about next year's plans without mentioning it once.
w-mention.szh: 我甚至做了一次明年计划的分享，从头到尾一次都没提它。

more.en: Believe it or not, most people don't even mention it.
more.szh: 说来你可能不信，大多数人提都没提。

w-cooking-show.note: 英式也说 cookery programme；TV show 泛指电视节目。
w-cooking-show.en: Tom was away, so nobody could make me watch another cooking show.
w-cooking-show.szh: Tom 不在家，也就没人拉我再看一集烹饪节目了。

get-on-with-sth.note: to start or continue doing a job, especially after a delay
get-on-with-sth.tip: 英式口语，常带「别磨蹭了」的意思；和 get on with sb（和某人相处）同形，要看后面是事还是人。
get-on-with-sth.example: Stop talking and get on with your work!
get-on-with-sth.en: So I made a cup of tea and finally got on with it.
get-on-with-sth.szh: 于是我泡了杯茶，终于动手干了。

more.en: Let's get on with it — the post office closes at half five.
more.szh: 赶紧办吧，邮局五点半就关门了。

once-and-for-all.note: completely and finally, so that something does not happen or need doing again
once-and-for-all.tip: 常放句尾，带一点「受够了」的语气；不要说 once for all。
once-and-for-all.example: Let's fix this printer once and for all.
once-and-for-all.en: I wanted to finish it once and for all.
once-and-for-all.szh: 我想一次把它彻底搞定。

more.en: Last spring, she decided to sort out her wardrobe once and for all.
more.szh: 去年春天，她下定决心要把衣柜彻底收拾一遍。

according-to.note: as shown by a report, a study or what someone has said
according-to.tip: 后面接消息来源（报告、调查、某人），不接自己：不说 according to me，要说 in my opinion。
according-to.example: According to the weather app, it'll rain all weekend.
according-to.en: According to our survey after the trial, developers freed up three and a half hours a week on average.
according-to.szh: 根据试行结束后的调查，开发人员平均每周多出了三个半小时。

more.en: According to the council's website, owners who ignore the rules can be fined thousands of pounds.
more.szh: 据市政厅网站说，不守规矩的房主可能被罚好几千英镑。

more.en: According to your calendar, you had a session with Dan at seven on Tuesday.
more.szh: 你日历上写着，周二七点你跟 Dan 有节课。

more.en: That's according to a new survey of 2,000 people.
more.szh: 这是一项针对 2000 人的新调查得出的结果。

w-survey.note: do / carry out a survey 做调查；fill in a survey 填问卷。
w-survey.en: According to our survey after the trial, developers freed up three and a half hours a week on average.
w-survey.szh: 根据试行结束后的调查，开发人员平均每周多出了三个半小时。

more.en: A new survey has found that only one in three UK adults eats five portions a day.
more.szh: 一项新调查发现，英国成年人里只有三分之一每天能吃够五份。

more.en: That's according to a new survey of 2,000 people.
more.szh: 这是一项针对 2000 人的新调查得出的结果。

more.en: Have you seen the beta survey?
more.szh: 你们看测试版的问卷了吗？

w-trial.note: on trial 在试行中；free trial 免费试用。另一个意思是「审判」。
w-trial.en: According to our survey after the trial, developers freed up three and a half hours a week on average.
w-trial.szh: 根据试行结束后的调查，开发人员平均每周多出了三个半小时。

free-up-sth.note: to make time, money or space available for something else
free-up-sth.tip: 宾语可以放中间：free some time up；代词只能放中间：free it up。
free-up-sth.example: Deleting old photos freed up a lot of space on my phone.
free-up-sth.en: According to our survey after the trial, developers freed up three and a half hours a week on average.
free-up-sth.szh: 根据试行结束后的调查，开发人员平均每周多出了三个半小时。

more.en: I'm painting the garden chairs on it, but I'll move them tomorrow to free up some space.
more.szh: 我在上面刷花园的椅子，明天挪走，腾点地方出来。

more.en: She also skips her afternoon coffees now, which has freed up about ten pounds a week.
more.szh: 她现在下午也不喝咖啡了，每周还因此省下差不多 10 英镑。

on-average.note: used to say what is usual when you look at many different amounts
on-average.tip: 常放句首或句尾；介词是 on，不说 in average。
on-average.example: On average, I get about fifty emails a day.
on-average.en: According to our survey after the trial, developers freed up three and a half hours a week on average.
on-average.szh: 根据试行结束后的调查，开发人员平均每周多出了三个半小时。

more.en: On average, about twenty people turn up, even in the rain.
more.szh: 平均每次来二十个人左右，下雨也照来不误。

more.en: On average, I've walked six kilometres a day.
more.szh: 平均下来，我每天走了六公里。

get-more-done.zh: 干成更多的事；效率更高
get-more-done.note: to finish more work in the same amount of time
get-more-done.tip: get sth done 是「把事做完」；get more done、get a lot done 都很常用，比 be more productive 口语。
get-more-done.example: I get more done in the morning than in the afternoon.
get-more-done.en: Most of them said they got more done on Wednesdays than on any other day.
get-more-done.szh: 大多数人说，星期三干的活比哪天都多。

more.en: And we'd get more done if you put your phone away.
more.szh: 还有，你把手机收起来，咱们效率能高点。

cut-down-on-sth.note: to do, use or eat less of something
cut-down-on-sth.tip: on 后面接要减少的东西；减少多少用 by：cut down on coffee by half。
cut-down-on-sth.example: I'm trying to cut down on sugar.
cut-down-on-sth.en: Testers cut down on "quick calls" by half.
cut-down-on-sth.szh: 测试那边的「快速电话」少了一半。

more.en: Since then, she's cut down on new clothes.
more.szh: 从那以后，她新衣服买得少多了。

w-focus.note: 专注于什么用 on：focus on one task。名词也是 focus。
w-focus.en: Arjun, one of our backend developers in Bangalore, told us, "I'm good at focusing, but only when nobody's talking to me."
w-focus.szh: 班加罗尔的后端开发 Arjun 跟我们说：「我专注力很强，前提是没人跟我说话。」

w-staff.note: staff 指一个单位的全体员工，不加 s；说一个员工用 a member of staff。
w-staff.en: Seventy-eight per cent of staff are in favour of keeping it.
w-staff.szh: 78% 的员工赞成继续搞下去。

be-in-favour-of-sth.note: to support an idea or a plan
be-in-favour-of-sth.tip: of 是介词，后面接名词或 doing：in favour of keeping it。英式拼写 favour，美式 favor。
be-in-favour-of-sth.example: Most of the team are in favour of a four-day week.
be-in-favour-of-sth.en: Seventy-eight per cent of staff are in favour of keeping it.
be-in-favour-of-sth.szh: 78% 的员工赞成继续搞下去。

more.en: For a start, I'm in favour of shorter showers.
more.szh: 首先，我赞成洗澡时间短一点。

w-urgent.note: an urgent email 急件；邮件标题常写 URGENT。
w-urgent.en: "When something was urgent, people still gave each other a hand."
w-urgent.szh: 「真有急事的时候，大家照样互相搭把手。」

more.en: The offer looked so urgent that I paid without reading a single review.
more.szh: 那个优惠看着十万火急，我连一条评价都没看就付了钱。

w-management.note: the management 指公司里管事的那批人；manage 的名词形式。
w-management.en: To decide the details, the management team has booked a two-hour meeting.
w-management.szh: 为了敲定细节，管理层已经订了一个两小时的会。

bring-up.note: to start talking about a subject
bring-up.tip: 代词放中间：bring it up，不说 bring up it。另一个意思是「抚养」：She was brought up in Leeds。
bring-up.example: I'll bring it up at the next team meeting.
bring-up.en: Every Monday, someone brought it up at stand-up, and we all agreed it was "not a priority".
bring-up.szh: 每周一的站会上总有人提起它，大家也都同意它「不急」。

more.en: And please don't bring up the vegetarian thing in front of Gran.
more.szh: 还有，千万别在奶奶面前提吃素的事。

more.en: She decided to bring it up with her doctor.
more.szh: 她决定跟医生说说这事。

w-priority.note: top priority 头等大事；工作里说 not a priority，常常是「先放着」的委婉说法。
w-priority.en: Every Monday, someone brought it up at stand-up, and we all agreed it was "not a priority".
w-priority.szh: 每周一的站会上总有人提起它，大家也都同意它「不急」。

put-off.note: to decide to do something later than planned
put-off.tip: 代词要放中间：put it off；后面接动作用 doing：put off calling the bank。
put-off.example: Don't put off the code review until Friday.
put-off.en: Honestly, I'd got used to putting it off.
put-off.szh: 老实说，我也渐渐习惯了一拖再拖。

more.en: "I put off my project for weeks," she says.
more.szh: 「我把作业拖了好几个星期，」她说。

more.en: Chen had put off cooking it for years.
more.szh: 这道菜小陈拖了好多年都没做。

w-complain.note: complain about sth 抱怨某事；名词 complaint（第 29 课）。
w-complain.en: She wasn't used to complaining, she wrote, but the app had crashed four times that morning.
w-complain.szh: 她说自己不太习惯投诉，可那天上午 App 崩了四次。

w-abroad.note: abroad 是副词，前面不加介词：live abroad、go abroad，不说 go to abroad。
w-abroad.en: She'd lost a long message to her son, who lives abroad.
w-abroad.szh: 她给在国外的儿子写的一条长消息也没了。

look-into.note: to try to find out the facts about a problem
look-into.tip: 和 look at 不同：look at 是「看」，look into 是「深入查原因」；代词放在后面：look into it。
look-into.example: Can you look into why the build failed?
look-into.en: So I looked into it that afternoon.

more.en: Tom asked the quizmaster to look into one of them, but he refused.
more.szh: Tom 请主持人把其中一道题再查一查，可他不肯。

more.en: Before you two start making excuses, let me look into the meter readings.
more.szh: 你俩先别急着找借口，我来查查电表读数。

track-down.note: to find something or someone after searching for a long time
track-down.tip: 代词放中间：track it down；强调找得辛苦，找 bug、找人都能用。
track-down.example: It took us a week to track down the cause of the crash.
track-down.en: It took me three hours to track it down.
track-down.szh: 我花了三个小时才找到原因。

more.en: I'll happily spend twenty minutes tracking down a discount code for a £4 candle.
more.szh: 为了一根 4 英镑的蜡烛，我能乐呵呵地花二十分钟去找折扣码。

run-out-of.note: to use all of something so that none is left
run-out-of.tip: 人或物做主语都行，后面接用完的东西；不接宾语时去掉 of：The memory ran out。
run-out-of.example: We've run out of coffee in the office.
run-out-of.en: It was one line of code that ran out of memory in power-saving mode.
run-out-of.szh: 是一行代码，在省电模式下把内存用光了。

more.en: She's run out of shelf space, so lots of albums now live under her bed.
more.szh: 书架早就放不下了，所以很多集邮册现在都住在她床底下。

w-memory.note: 电脑和手机的「内存」也是 memory；人的「记性」也是：I have a bad memory。
w-memory.en: It was one line of code that ran out of memory in power-saving mode.
w-memory.szh: 是一行代码，在省电模式下把内存用光了。

w-power-saving-mode.note: 手机电量低时打开的模式；也说 low power mode。
w-power-saving-mode.en: It was one line of code that ran out of memory in power-saving mode.
w-power-saving-mode.szh: 是一行代码，在省电模式下把内存用光了。

agree-on.note: to decide something together after discussing it
agree-on.tip: agree on 某件事；agree with 某人；agree to do 同意去做。
agree-on.example: We couldn't agree on a name for the project.
agree-on.en: We agreed on a new rule, and Mia insisted on writing it down.
agree-on.szh: 我们商定了一条新规矩，Mia 非要把它写下来。

more.en: They couldn't even agree on the colour.
more.szh: 他们连颜色都说不到一块儿去。

deal-with.note: to take action to solve a problem or finish a task
deal-with.tip: 过去式和过去分词都是 dealt，读 /delt/；被动是 be dealt with，with 不能丢。
deal-with.example: I'll deal with the emails after lunch.
deal-with.en: Any bug that's been on the list for more than a week has to be dealt with first.
deal-with.szh: 在清单上挂了一周以上的 bug，都得先处理。

more.en: Who'll deal with my return, and do I have to pay for postage?
more.szh: 退货由谁来处理？邮费要我自己出吗？

looking-back.note: used when you think about something that happened in the past
looking-back.tip: 常放句首，后面加逗号；常和 should have 连用，说当初该怎么做。
looking-back.example: Looking back, I should have asked for help earlier.
looking-back.en: Looking back, the hardest part wasn't the code.
looking-back.szh: 回头看，最难的不是代码。

more.en: Looking back, both the toaster and the coffee machine were a waste of money.
more.szh: 现在回头看，烤面包机和咖啡机都是白花钱。

w-admit.note: admit doing / admit that …：承认自己做了（不太光彩的）事。
w-admit.en: It was admitting that "not a priority" really meant "not my problem".
w-admit.szh: 而是承认：「不急」其实就是「不关我的事」。

more.en: Well... I have to admit, it was actually Biscuit who found it.
more.szh: 嗯……我得承认，其实是 Biscuit 找到的。

w-programming.note: program 是程序，programming 是编程这门手艺；programmer 是程序员。
w-programming.en: Ms Gao taught programming at Chen's university in Chengdu for twenty-five years.
w-programming.szh: 高老师在小陈读书的成都那所大学教了二十五年编程。

w-loop.note: 编程里让一段代码重复执行的结构，比如 for loop；平时也指「圈、环」。
w-loop.en: In his first year, he had trouble understanding loops.
w-loop.szh: 大一那年，他怎么都搞不懂循环。

w-stare.note: stare at sth 长时间盯着；比 look at 时间长，常带「看不懂、发愣」的意思。
w-stare.en: He spent whole weekends staring at error messages.
w-stare.szh: 好几个周末都是整天盯着报错信息发呆。

be-patient-with-sb.note: to stay calm and not get angry when someone is slow or makes mistakes
be-patient-with-sb.tip: 对人用 with；对事也可以用 about：be patient about the results。反义 impatient。
be-patient-with-sb.example: Be patient with him — it's only his second week.
be-patient-with-sb.en: She was patient with beginners and often went out of her way to help them.
be-patient-with-sb.szh: 她对初学者很有耐心，还常常特意抽时间帮他们。

more.en: "But Mrs Taylor was very patient with me."
more.szh: 「可 Taylor 老师对我特别有耐心。」

more.en: She was always patient with him.
more.szh: 奶奶对他一直很有耐心。

go-out-of-your-way-to-do.text: go out of your way to do
go-out-of-your-way-to-do.note: to make a special effort to do something, especially to help someone
