go-out-of-your-way-to-do.tip: your 要跟着主语变：she went out of her way、they went out of their way；后面接 to do。
go-out-of-your-way-to-do.example: The hotel staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome.
go-out-of-your-way-to-do.en: She was patient with beginners and often went out of her way to help them.
go-out-of-your-way-to-do.szh: 她对初学者很有耐心，还常常特意抽时间帮他们。

more.en: Tom's mum even went out of her way to make me a name badge.
more.szh: Tom 的妈妈甚至还特意给我做了个名牌。

more.en: She's gone out of her way to explain the computer system.
more.szh: 她专门抽时间给我讲电脑系统。

w-lab.note: laboratory 的简称；computer lab 就是机房。
w-lab.en: Every Saturday morning, she opened the empty lab and spent three hours answering questions from anyone who turned up.
w-lab.szh: 每个星期六上午，她都会打开空荡荡的机房，谁来了就给谁答疑，一答就是三个小时。

pay-attention-to.note: to watch, listen to or think about something carefully
pay-attention-to.tip: to 是介词，后面接名词或 doing；不说 pay attention on。
pay-attention-to.example: Please pay attention to the warning signs.
pay-attention-to.en: She made students pay attention to every error message.
pay-attention-to.szh: 她要求学生认真看每一条报错信息。

more.en: To be honest, I paid more attention to the trains than to my bag.
more.szh: 说实话，我光顾着看火车了，没怎么留意包。

more.en: And I pay no attention to "only 2 left in stock".
more.szh: 还有，「库存仅剩 2 件」这种话，我一概不理。

w-repeat.note: repeat yourself 是「把自己说过的话再说一遍」；Could you repeat that? 请再说一遍。

learn-from-your-mistakes.note: to understand what you did wrong so that you do better next time
learn-from-your-mistakes.tip: your 跟着主语变：he learned from his mistakes。犯错是 make a mistake，不说 do a mistake。
learn-from-your-mistakes.example: Everyone gets things wrong — the important thing is to learn from your mistakes.
learn-from-your-mistakes.en: And, "Learn from your mistakes. You'll make plenty."
learn-from-your-mistakes.szh: 还有：「要从错误里学。你们会犯很多错的。」

more.en: Well, she learned from her mistakes.
more.szh: 好在她吸取了教训。

point-sb-in-the-right-direction.text: point sb in the right direction
point-sb-in-the-right-direction.zh: 给某人指个方向；点拨一下
point-sb-in-the-right-direction.note: to give someone a little help or advice so they can find the answer themselves
point-sb-in-the-right-direction.tip: 人放在 point 后面；只给思路，不给答案，所以很适合请教别人时客气地说。
point-sb-in-the-right-direction.example: I don't need the full answer — can you just point me in the right direction?
point-sb-in-the-right-direction.en: She'd only point you in the right direction.

more.en: Priya tried to point me in the right direction.
more.szh: Priya 想给我指条明路。

w-cruel.note: 这里是半开玩笑的夸张：不给答案，在学生看来简直「太狠了」。
w-cruel.en: Chen used to think this was cruel.
w-cruel.szh: 小陈以前觉得这样太狠了。

make-a-difference.note: to have a good effect on someone or something
make-a-difference.tip: 对谁有影响用 to；加强语气：make a big / real difference。没影响：make no difference。
make-a-difference.example: A good manager can make a big difference to a team.
make-a-difference.en: Hundreds of her old students now work abroad, and she made a difference to every one of them.
make-a-difference.szh: 她教过的学生里，光在国外工作的就有好几百个，每一个都受过她的影响。

more.en: Please take this seriously, because a quick reply would make a difference.
more.szh: 请认真对待这件事，能尽快回复我就帮大忙了。

w-slides.note: 做演讲用的 PPT 每一页叫 a slide；a slide deck 是一整套幻灯片。
w-slides.en: After last year, you'll notice there are no slides.
w-slides.szh: 有了去年的教训，大家会发现今天没有幻灯片。

take-sth-apart.note: to separate something into its different parts
take-sth-apart.tip: 宾语放中间：take it apart；装回去是 put it back together。
take-sth-apart.example: He took the old radio apart to fix it.
take-sth-apart.en: A week later, I took it apart, step by step.
take-sth-apart.szh: 一个星期后，我一步一步把它拆了。

more.en: Pete got so stressed that he took a beer mat apart.
more.szh: Pete 急得把一张啤酒杯垫拆得七零八落。

more.en: He'd also taken his TV remote apart, just to see how it worked.
more.szh: 他还把电视遥控器拆了，说只是想看看里面怎么回事。

w-repair-shop.note: repair 修理；也常说 a phone repair shop、a bike repair shop。
w-repair-shop.en: The repair shop took two days and 300 yuan to sort it out.
w-repair-shop.szh: 修理店花了两天、收了 300 块才弄好。

w-yuan.note: 单复数同形：one yuan、300 yuan，不加 s。
w-yuan.en: The repair shop took two days and 300 yuan to sort it out.
w-yuan.szh: 修理店花了两天、收了 300 块才弄好。

have-a-go-at-sth.note: to try to do something, often for the first time
have-a-go-at-sth.tip: 英式口语，鼓励别人尝试时很常用：Go on, have a go!；后面接 doing 也可以：have a go at fixing it。
have-a-go-at-sth.example: I've never cooked fish before, but I'll have a go at it.
have-a-go-at-sth.en: "Have a go at this," he said.

more.en: I had a go at the train driving game.
more.szh: 我玩了一会儿开火车的游戏。

more.en: Then, if I were you, I'd have a go at one of those free running tests in a sports shop.
more.szh: 到那时候，要是我，就去运动用品店试试他们免费的跑步测试。

get-into-sth.zh: 开始喜欢上；迷上（某爱好）
get-into-sth.note: to start to be interested in an activity
get-into-sth.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：get into photography / get into running。说「怎么入的坑」：How did you get into coding?
get-into-sth.example: She got into running during the lockdown.
get-into-sth.en: I got into making little games, just for fun.
get-into-sth.szh: 我迷上了做小游戏，纯粹是好玩。

more.en: Good, because if you get into Viking history after today, the shop sells a great book.
more.szh: 很好，因为今天之后要是你们迷上了维京历史，商店里有本很棒的书。

more.en: And I got into board games.
more.szh: 还迷上了桌游。

for-fun.note: for enjoyment, not for money or a serious reason
for-fun.tip: 常加 just：just for fun；不说 for funny。
for-fun.example: I learned Japanese just for fun.
for-fun.en: I got into making little games, just for fun.
for-fun.szh: 我迷上了做小游戏，纯粹是好玩。

more.en: The seller kept an eye on Tom, who was trying the horn for fun.
more.szh: 卖家一直盯着 Tom，因为他在那儿按喇叭玩。

get-hooked-on-sth.note: to start to enjoy something so much that you want to do it all the time
get-hooked-on-sth.tip: on 是介词，后面接名词或 doing；比 get into 程度更深，有点「停不下来」。
get-hooked-on-sth.example: I got hooked on that TV series and watched it all in a week.
get-hooked-on-sth.en: At thirteen, I got hooked on building things from scratch.
get-hooked-on-sth.szh: 十三岁的时候，我迷上了从零开始做东西。

more.en: So, Tom's got hooked on Chinese films lately, and I tend to leave my laptop lying around.
more.szh: Tom 最近迷上了中国电影，而我又总爱把笔记本电脑随手一放。

from-scratch.note: from the very beginning, without using anything that already exists
from-scratch.tip: 程序员常说 build / write sth from scratch；start from scratch 是「推倒重来」。
from-scratch.example: We decided to rewrite the app from scratch.
from-scratch.en: At thirteen, I got hooked on building things from scratch.
from-scratch.szh: 十三岁的时候，我迷上了从零开始做东西。

more.en: The school was on a budget, so she wrote her own listening tests from scratch.
more.szh: 学校经费紧张，她就自己从头编听力题。

w-calculator.note: calculate 计算；calculator 就是「算的东西」。
w-calculator.en: I built a calculator that got every answer slightly wrong.
w-calculator.szh: 我做了个计算器，每个答案都差那么一点点。

more.en: For forty years, she got by with a calculator and a good memory.
more.szh: 四十年来，她就靠一个计算器和一副好记性对付过来。

w-maths.note: 英式说 maths，美式说 math；虽然有 s，但当单数用。
w-maths.en: My maths teacher pointed out that seven times eight isn't fifty-four.
w-maths.szh: 数学老师指出来，七乘八不等于五十四。

w-one-page.note: 数字 + 名词用连字符做形容词，名词不加 s：a one-page guide、a two-hour meeting。
w-one-page.en: Rachel asked us to write a one-page guide to help Ollie settle in.
w-one-page.szh: Rachel 让我们写一页纸的指南，帮 Ollie 尽快适应。

w-guide.note: a guide to sth 关于……的指南；也指导游：a tour guide。
w-guide.en: Rachel asked us to write a one-page guide to help Ollie settle in.
w-guide.szh: Rachel 让我们写一页纸的指南，帮 Ollie 尽快适应。

settle-in.zh: （在新地方、新工作）安顿下来；适应
settle-in.note: to start to feel happy and relaxed in a new home, job or school
settle-in.tip: 常用进行时问候新人：Are you settling in OK?；后面可接 at / to：settle in to a new job。
settle-in.example: How are you settling in at your new school?
settle-in.en: Rachel asked us to write a one-page guide to help Ollie settle in.
settle-in.szh: Rachel 让我们写一页纸的指南，帮 Ollie 尽快适应。

more.en: He gave it to me when I moved to the UK, to help me settle in.
more.szh: 我来英国的时候，他把相机送给了我，好让我早点适应这边的生活。

more.en: If you join a running club, give yourself a month to settle in.
more.szh: 要是加入了跑步俱乐部，给自己一个月慢慢适应。

keep-in-mind.note: to remember a fact when you are thinking or making a decision
keep-in-mind.tip: 后面接 that 从句，或者把东西放中间：keep it in mind。比 remember 多一层「做决定时要考虑到」。
keep-in-mind.example: Keep in mind that the shop closes early on Sundays.
keep-in-mind.en: Keep in mind that Ollie's a developer, not a tester.
keep-in-mind.szh: 别忘了，Ollie 是开发，不是测试。

more.en: So keep in mind that a lot of this is a good guess.
more.szh: 所以大家要记住，这里面很多都是有根据的猜测。

more.en: Keep in mind that most people tend to give up after three weeks.
more.szh: 别忘了，大多数人坚持三个星期就放弃了。

w-book.note: book a meeting / a room / a table；美式也常说 schedule a meeting。
w-book.en: Number two: avoid booking meetings on Wednesdays.
w-book.szh: 第二条：星期三别约会议。

get-sb-up-to-speed.zh: 让某人跟上进度；让某人了解最新情况
get-sb-up-to-speed.note: to give someone all the information they need so they can work like everyone else
get-sb-up-to-speed.tip: 人放在 get 和 up 中间；自己「跟上了」说 be up to speed。
get-sb-up-to-speed.example: I'll spend the first morning getting you up to speed on the project.
get-sb-up-to-speed.en: Number four: nobody can get you up to speed in a week.
get-sb-up-to-speed.szh: 第四条：谁也没法让你一个星期就跟上节奏。

more.en: Margaret's got me up to speed on York's drainpipes — and I never expected to say that.
more.szh: Margaret 让我把约克的排水管摸了个门儿清——这话我做梦都没想到自己会说。

more.en: That evening, Priya got us up to speed on the costs nobody talks about.
more.szh: 那天晚上，Priya 把那些没人提的开销给我们讲了个明白。

it-s-no-big-deal.note: used to say that something is not important or not a problem
it-s-no-big-deal.tip: 口语；安慰别人或回应道歉时常用。反过来说 It's a big deal. 是「这可是件大事」。
it-s-no-big-deal.en: It's no big deal if you can't figure everything out at once.
it-s-no-big-deal.szh: 一下子弄不明白所有事，没什么大不了的。

more.en: I felt a bit out of place, but I told myself it was no big deal.
more.szh: 我觉得自己有点格格不入，但我跟自己说，没什么大不了的。

at-your-own-pace.note: at the speed that is right for you, not the speed of other people
at-your-own-pace.tip: your 跟着主语变：at his own pace；pace 是「步调、速度」。
at-your-own-pace.example: This online course lets you study at your own pace.
at-your-own-pace.en: Just learn at your own pace.
at-your-own-pace.szh: 按自己的节奏慢慢学就行。

more.en: On the day, his hands were shaking, and she whispered, "Read at your own pace. Nobody's going anywhere."
more.szh: 到了那天，他的手一直在抖，她小声跟他说：「按你自己的节奏读，没人会走的。」

w-build.note: 程序员说的 build 是编译打包出来的一个版本；动词 build 是「建造、构建」。
w-build.en: You got that old build working on your own.
w-build.szh: 那个旧版本是你一个人弄好的。

w-kitchen-rules.note: 办公室的 kitchen 是茶水间；英国办公室常见的规矩：自己的杯子自己洗，别拿别人的牛奶。
w-kitchen-rules.en: And someone needs to fill him in on the kitchen rules, so he doesn't take anyone's milk.
w-kitchen-rules.szh: 还得有人跟他讲讲茶水间的规矩，免得他拿了别人的牛奶。

don-t-hesitate-to-do.note: used to tell someone they should feel free to do something
don-t-hesitate-to-do.tip: 邮件结尾常见：Please don't hesitate to contact me. 后面接 to do；比 feel free to do 正式一点。
don-t-hesitate-to-do.example: If you need anything, don't hesitate to call me.
don-t-hesitate-to-do.en: OK. "Don't hesitate to ask questions instead of guessing."
don-t-hesitate-to-do.szh: 好。「有问题尽管问，别自己瞎猜。」

more.en: If a bowl starts to wobble, don't hesitate to stop.
more.szh: 碗一开始晃，就别犹豫，马上停。

be-fully-booked.note: if a train, hotel or restaurant is fully booked, there are no seats or rooms left
be-fully-booked.tip: 说「订满了」不用 full booked；也可以只说 booked up。主语是火车、酒店、餐厅，不是人。
be-fully-booked.example: Every hotel near the station is fully booked this weekend.
be-fully-booked.en: The train was fully booked, but luckily Tom had reserved two seats in coach C.
be-fully-booked.szh: 车票全卖光了，好在 Tom 提前在 C 车厢订了两个座位。

more.en: Today's tour is fully booked, so let's get started.
more.szh: 今天的导览名额全满了，我们这就开始吧。

more.en: Oh, and Dan's Monday class is fully booked now, because I made half the hospital sign up.
more.szh: 对了，Dan 周一那节课现在都约满了，因为我把半个医院的人都拉去报名了。

w-coach.note: 英式英语里 coach 还指长途大巴；火车车厢也可以说 carriage。
w-coach.en: The train was fully booked, but luckily Tom had reserved two seats in coach C.
w-coach.szh: 车票全卖光了，好在 Tom 提前在 C 车厢订了两个座位。

on-board.zh: 在车上；在船上；在飞机上
on-board.note: on or onto a train, ship or plane
on-board.tip: get on board 上车，be on board 在车上；后面要接交通工具时用 on board the train。
on-board.example: There's no food on board, so bring something to eat.
on-board.en: We jumped on board at the back just as the doors closed.
on-board.szh: 车门关上的那一刻，我们从车尾跳了上去。

more.en: Now I'm on board the four o'clock to London, in a seat that's actually mine.
more.szh: 现在我坐上了四点回伦敦的火车，这回坐的还真是我自己的座位。

more.en: The number 73 finally turned up, and as I stepped on board, the sole split in two.
more.szh: 73 路总算来了，我一脚迈上车，鞋底裂成了两半。

w-rack.note: 全称 luggage rack；放东西用 on the rack。
w-rack.en: I put my backpack on the rack above them, and Tom had a quick look at the little screen.
w-rack.szh: 我把背包放到他们头顶的行李架上，Tom 凑过去看了一眼座位上方的小屏幕。

w-reservation.note: 动词是 reserve：reserve a seat；订餐厅也说 make a reservation。
w-reservation.en: "Reservations are only kept until the train leaves," he read.
w-reservation.szh: 「订座只保留到开车为止，」他念道。

keep-an-eye-on-sth.note: to watch something or someone carefully so that nothing bad happens
keep-an-eye-on-sth.tip: eye 用单数，不说 keep eyes on；也可以说 keep an eye on the time（留意时间）。
keep-an-eye-on-sth.example: Could you keep an eye on my laptop while I get a coffee?
keep-an-eye-on-sth.en: "Oh, and always keep an eye on your bag."

more.en: Did you keep an eye on your bag, like I told you?
more.szh: 你看好包了吗？我可跟你说过。

more.en: He lies there, keeping an eye on the red hand.
more.szh: 他就那么躺着，盯着那根红色的秒针。

more.en: The seller kept an eye on Tom, who was trying the horn for fun.
more.szh: 卖家一直盯着 Tom，因为他在那儿按喇叭玩。

w-guard.note: 英国火车上查票、管车门的工作人员；guard 还有「警卫」的意思。
w-guard.en: Then the wifi went down, and a guard came along and looked over our tickets.
w-guard.szh: 后来车上的 Wi-Fi 断了，一位列车员过来把我们的票查了一遍。

leave-sth-behind.note: to forget to take something with you when you leave a place
leave-sth-behind.tip: 东西放在 leave 和 behind 中间：leave my bag behind；落在哪里用 in / at：behind in the car。
leave-sth-behind.example: I left my umbrella behind at the restaurant again.
leave-sth-behind.en: Somewhere near Peterborough, I suddenly realised I'd left my backpack behind in coach C.
leave-sth-behind.szh: 快到彼得伯勒的时候，我突然反应过来：背包落在 C 车厢了。

more.en: Just leave it behind and start from scratch.
more.szh: 扔一边，从头再来。

go-missing.note: to disappear, so that nobody knows where something or someone is
go-missing.tip: 主语是丢的东西：My phone went missing，不说 I went missing my phone。英式英语常用。
go-missing.example: My keys went missing last week, and I still haven't found them.
go-missing.en: "Bags go missing on this line all the time," Tom said.
go-missing.szh: 「这条线上丢包是常事，」Tom 说。

more.en: It went missing in our final year, just after I'd lent it to someone in the class.
more.szh: 毕业那年它不见了，就在我把它借给班上某个人之后。

hand-sth-in.zh: 上交；交给（失物招领、老师、前台）
hand-sth-in.note: to give something to a person in charge, for example something you found or a piece of work
hand-sth-in.tip: 被动 be handed in 很常用：丢的东西「被交上来」；交作业也说 hand in your homework。
hand-sth-in.example: Someone handed my wallet in at the front desk.

more.en: So, in seven days, my backpack was handed in without its sandwich.
more.szh: 七天里，我的背包被人交了回来，只是三明治没了。

more.en: The day after I'd handed in my last homework of the year, Dad took a small red bike out of the shed.
more.szh: 交完那学年最后一份作业的第二天，爸爸从棚子里推出一辆小红车。

w-platform.en: At York, the guard was waiting on the platform with my backpack.
w-platform.szh: 到了约克，列车员拿着我的背包在站台上等着。

w-charger.note: 动词 charge 充电：My phone is charging.
w-charger.en: Everything was still there — laptop, passport, charger — except my sandwich.
w-charger.szh: 东西都在——电脑、护照、充电器——就是三明治没了。

w-pickle.note: 英国的 pickle 常指一种褐色的酸甜蔬菜酱，和奶酪一起夹三明治；美式英语里 pickle 多指腌黄瓜。

w-stall.note: 摆摊的人叫 stallholder；market stall、food stall 都很常见。
w-stall.en: In a supermarket, the price is the price, but at a market stall, nothing is sold at the first price.
w-stall.szh: 在超市，标多少就是多少；可在市场的摊位上，没有东西是按开价卖的。

more.en: The bike shed, and that noodle stall outside the gate.
more.szh: 车棚，还有校门外那个面摊。

w-pretend.note: 后面接 to do 或 that 从句：pretend to be busy / pretend that you're busy。
w-pretend.en: At least pretend to think about it for a while.
w-pretend.szh: 至少也要装模作样想一会儿。

w-brass.note: 放在名词前当形容词用：a brass clock、brass buttons。
w-brass.en: Oh wow, look at that brass clock!

w-farmhouse.note: farm + house；英国乡下很多老农舍有几百年历史。
w-farmhouse.en: It was made in Sheffield in 1920, and it was found in a farmhouse near Whitby.
w-farmhouse.szh: 它是 1920 年在谢菲尔德造的，是在惠特比附近的一座农舍里找到的。

how-much-do-you-want-for-sth.text: how much do you want for sth?
how-much-do-you-want-for-sth.note: a question you ask a seller when you want to know the price and maybe pay less
how-much-do-you-want-for-sth.tip: 比 How much is it? 多一层「价钱可以谈」的意思，在市场、二手买卖里常用；问的是卖家心里的价。
how-much-do-you-want-for-sth.example: How much do you want for the bike? It looks a bit old.
how-much-do-you-want-for-sth.en: How much do you want for it?

more.en: Honestly, I should never have asked, "How much do you want for it?"
more.szh: 说真的，我当初就不该问那句「这个您想卖多少？」

more.en: How much do you want for tonight's password?
more.szh: 今晚的密码，你开个价吧。

a-rip-off.note: something that costs much more than it should
a-rip-off.tip: 口语，常说 That's a rip-off 或 What a rip-off!；动词说法是 rip sb off（宰某人）。
a-rip-off.example: Eight pounds for a coffee? That's a rip-off.

more.en: Six pounds for a clock that must be thirty years old is a bit of a rip-off.
more.szh: 一个少说也有三十年的旧钟卖 6 英镑，有点坑。

more.en: "Chen, that's a rip-off," he said.
more.szh: 「小陈，你这是被宰了，」他说。

meet-sb-halfway.note: to agree to some of what another person wants so that you can both agree
meet-sb-halfway.tip: 不只用于讲价，开会、商量计划都能用；meet halfway 是双方各退一步，不是只有一方让。
meet-sb-halfway.example: You want Friday and I want Monday, so let's meet halfway and say Wednesday.

more.en: Can you meet me halfway?
more.szh: 咱们各让一步，行不行？

more.en: Fine, I'll meet you halfway.
more.szh: 好吧，咱们各让一步。

w-halfway.note: 也能放在名词前：the halfway point（中点）；halfway through the film 电影看到一半。

take-it-or-leave-it.note: said when you will not change an offer and the other person must accept it or refuse it
take-it-or-leave-it.tip: 语气很硬，是在说「不再让价了」；对上司、客户说会显得没礼貌。
take-it-or-leave-it.example: This is my last offer — take it or leave it.
take-it-or-leave-it.en: Thirty-two pounds, take it or leave it.

more.en: It's my only offer — take it or leave it.
more.szh: 我就这一个提议——要不要随你。

knock-sth-off.note: to take an amount away from a price
knock-sth-off.tip: 钱数放在中间：knock £5 off；也可以说 knock £5 off the price。
knock-sth-off.example: The shop knocked ten pounds off because the box was damaged.

more.en: The shop knocked twenty pounds off mine because the bell didn't work.
more.szh: 因为我那辆车铃不响，店里便宜了 20 英镑。

be-a-bargain.note: to be sold for less than its real value
be-a-bargain.tip: bargain 是名词，前面要有 a：It's a bargain；不说 It's very bargain。
be-a-bargain.example: These boots were a bargain — I paid half the normal price.
be-a-bargain.en: And for a clock that old, thirty-two pounds is a bargain.
be-a-bargain.szh: 这么老的钟，32 英镑算捡了个便宜。

more.en: This arch dates back to 1870, and the rent was a bargain.
more.szh: 这间桥洞工作室是 1870 年建的，房租便宜得很。

w-sticker.note: 动词 stick 是「粘贴」；price sticker 价格标签。
w-sticker.en: There's a tiny sticker on the bottom.

come-across-sth.note: to find something or meet someone when you are not looking for them
come-across-sth.tip: come 的过去式是 came；碰到的东西放在后面：come across a problem，不拆开说 come it across。
come-across-sth.example: I came across some old photos while I was cleaning the flat.
come-across-sth.en: On Sunday afternoon, nine-year-old Isla Walsh came across a Roman coin while she was walking her dog, Biscuit.
come-across-sth.szh: 周日下午，九岁的 Isla Walsh 遛狗 Biscuit 的时候，发现了一枚罗马硬币。

more.en: Then he comes across a video of a man cleaning old trainers, then another.
more.szh: 结果刷到一个男的洗旧球鞋的视频，接着又是一个。

more.en: I've just come across a message from Lily, from three weeks ago.
more.szh: 我刚翻到 Lily 三个星期前发的一条消息。

by-chance.note: in a way that was not planned
by-chance.tip: 和第 19 课的 by coincidence 意思接近；by chance 更常用，放在句末最自然。
by-chance.example: We met by chance at the airport.
by-chance.en: I wasn't looking for anything — it was completely by chance.
by-chance.szh: 我根本没在找东西——完全是碰巧。

more.en: And yesterday I found your gas bill under a pizza box, completely by chance.
more.szh: 昨天我还在一个披萨盒底下翻出了你的煤气账单，纯属碰巧。

more.en: Then, by chance, she spotted a wool coat for £8 while she was looking for boots.
more.szh: 后来她找靴子的时候，碰巧看到一件羊毛大衣，只要 8 英镑。

w-button.note: 衣服上的扣子和机器、App 上的按钮都叫 button。
w-button.en: I saw something small and green, and I thought it was an old brass button.
w-button.szh: 我看见一个绿色的小东西，还以为是颗旧铜扣子。

can-t-believe-your-eyes.note: to be very surprised by something you see
can-t-believe-your-eyes.tip: your 要换成对应的人：I couldn't believe my eyes / She couldn't believe her eyes；讲过去的事用 couldn't。
can-t-believe-your-eyes.example: When I saw the bill, I couldn't believe my eyes.
can-t-believe-your-eyes.en: Then I had a closer look, and I couldn't believe my eyes.
can-t-believe-your-eyes.szh: 再仔细一看，简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。

more.en: It didn't go as described in the textbook, and we couldn't believe our eyes.
more.szh: 实验完全没按课本上写的来，我们都看傻了眼。

w-identify.note: identify sth as … 认定某物是……；名词 identification，简称 ID。
w-identify.en: The coin has now been identified as Roman.
w-identify.szh: 这枚硬币现在已经确认是罗马时期的。

date-back-to.note: to have existed since a particular time in the past
date-back-to.tip: 说东西本身的年代，用一般现在时：It dates back to 1920，不说 It dated back。
date-back-to.example: This pub dates back to the 16th century.
date-back-to.en: Well, it dates back to around AD 210.
date-back-to.szh: 嗯，大约可以追溯到公元 210 年。

more.en: Actually, my whole career dates back to those poems.
more.szh: 说起来，我这一行能干到今天，就是从那些诗开始的。

more.en: This arch dates back to 1870, and the rent was a bargain.
more.szh: 这间桥洞工作室是 1870 年建的，房租便宜得很。

w-emperor.note: 放在名字前面时首字母大写：the Emperor Augustus。
w-emperor.en: At that time, the Emperor Septimius Severus was actually living here in York.
w-emperor.szh: 那时候，罗马皇帝塞普蒂米乌斯·塞维鲁其实就住在约克。

w-rarely.note: rare（稀有的）的副词；本身带否定意思，不再加 not。
w-rarely.en: There's plenty of Roman history under our streets, but coins like this are rarely found by members of the public.
w-rarely.szh: 我们的街道底下埋着大量罗马时期的历史，可这样的硬币很少被普通人找到。

w-the-public.note: 和专家、工作人员相对的「普通人」；open to the public 对公众开放。
w-the-public.en: There's plenty of Roman history under our streets, but coins like this are rarely found by members of the public.
w-the-public.szh: 我们的街道底下埋着大量罗马时期的历史，可这样的硬币很少被普通人找到。

w-worth.note: 后面直接接钱数，不加 of：worth £300；问值不值钱就说 Is it worth much?

be-thrilled.note: to be very happy and excited about something
be-thrilled.tip: 比 happy 强得多；对什么高兴用 about / with，或接 to do：I'm thrilled to be here。英式英语里 family 后面动词可用复数。
be-thrilled.example: We were thrilled when we heard the news.

more.en: If it had survived, Tom would have been thrilled.
more.szh: 它要是没裂，Tom 肯定高兴坏了。

on-display.note: put in a public place so that people can see it
on-display.tip: be on display 在展出（状态），go on display 开始展出（变化）；put sth on display 把某物拿出来展示。
on-display.example: Her paintings are on display at the library this month.
on-display.en: The coin will go on display at the Yorkshire Museum next spring.
on-display.szh: 这枚硬币明年春天将在约克郡博物馆展出。

more.en: Her test paper is now on display on the fridge.
more.szh: 她的试卷现在正贴在冰箱上，供全家参观。

w-listed.note: listed building 是英国受法律保护的历史建筑，改动要先申请；分 Grade I、II* 和 II 三级。
w-listed.szh: 这是一栋受保护的历史建筑。

be-allowed-to-do.note: to have permission to do something
be-allowed-to-do.tip: 否定 aren't allowed to 是「不许」，比 can't 更强调规定；后面接动词原形。
be-allowed-to-do.example: Visitors aren't allowed to take photos inside the museum.
be-allowed-to-do.en: It means you aren't allowed to just do what you like.
be-allowed-to-do.szh: 意思就是，你不能想怎么弄就怎么弄。

more.en: But am I allowed to keep one mug on my desk?
more.szh: 那我桌上能留一个杯子吗？

more.en: On the app, sellers are allowed to set their own prices.
more.szh: 在这个 App 上，卖家可以自己定价。

make-changes-to-sth.tip: 介词用 to，不用 on / for：make changes to the code。小改动说 make small changes。
make-changes-to-sth.example: I've made a few changes to the design — can you have a look?
make-changes-to-sth.en: If you want to make changes to the house, you have to ask the council first.
make-changes-to-sth.szh: 想对房子做任何改动，都得先问市政厅。

more.en: Ring back in three months and tell me what changes you've made to your evenings.
more.szh: 三个月后再打进来，告诉我你的晚上有了哪些变化。

more.en: We need to make changes to how we use energy, then.
more.szh: 那咱们用电的习惯得改改了。

w-council.note: 英国的城市、郡由 council 管理，收垃圾、批建房都归它管。
w-council.en: If you want to make changes to the house, you have to ask the council first.
w-council.szh: 想对房子做任何改动，都得先问市政厅。

w-knocker.note: 动词 knock 敲门；英国老房子的前门上常装一个金属门环。
w-knocker.en: Even for a brass door knocker.
w-knocker.szh: 连换个黄铜门环都要问。

w-traditional.note: 名词 tradition；traditional food 传统食物。
w-traditional.en: Repairs should be done with traditional materials, and plastic windows usually can't be fitted.
w-traditional.szh: 修缮要用传统材料，塑料窗一般不让装。

w-fine.note: 当名词也是「罚款」：pay a fine；和形容词 fine（好的）是同一个拼写。
w-fine.en: According to the council's website, owners who ignore the rules can be fined thousands of pounds.
w-fine.szh: 据市政厅网站说，不守规矩的房主可能被罚好几千英镑。

get-permission-to-do.note: to be told officially that you can do something
get-permission-to-do.tip: permission 不可数，不说 a permission；向谁要许可是 from sb：get permission from the council。
get-permission-to-do.example: We need to get permission to use their photos.
get-permission-to-do.en: How long does it take to get permission to do the work?
get-permission-to-do.szh: 那拿到施工许可要多久？

more.en: The manager, Gary Pike, got permission to spend fifteen pounds a week on fruit.
more.szh: 经理 Gary Pike 申请到了每周 15 英镑的水果钱。

more.en: Years later, I found out he hadn't got permission to do it.
more.szh: 很多年后我才知道，那个实验他根本没得到批准。

w-strict.note: a strict teacher 严厉的老师；strict rules 严格的规定。
w-strict.en: To be honest, it all sounds a bit strict.
w-strict.szh: 说实话，听着有点太严了。

fall-apart.note: to break into pieces because it is old or badly made
fall-apart.tip: fall 的过去式 fell，过去分词 fallen；人也能 fall apart，是「崩溃」。
fall-apart.example: My old trainers are falling apart.
fall-apart.en: Maybe, but in the 1960s, lots of old houses had fallen apart, or were knocked down for roads and car parks.
fall-apart.szh: 也许吧，可在六十年代，好多老房子要么已经破败不堪，要么被拆掉修了马路和停车场。

more.en: Can I just glue the crack, or will it fall apart?
more.szh: 我拿胶把裂缝粘上行吗？还是会散架？

in-the-long-run.note: after a long period of time, in the future
in-the-long-run.tip: 常放在句首或句末；反义是 in the short run / in the short term。
in-the-long-run.example: Writing tests takes time, but it saves time in the long run.
in-the-long-run.en: And in the long run, the rules are good for the city.
in-the-long-run.szh: 从长远看，这些规定对城市是好事。

more.en: "But in the long run, a lot of them get both.
more.szh: 「不过从长远看，很多人两样都拿到了。

in-good-condition.note: not damaged, and working or looking as it should
in-good-condition.tip: condition 前不加 a：in good condition / in poor condition；二手买卖常用。
in-good-condition.example: The car is ten years old, but it's still in good condition.
in-good-condition.en: They keep the old streets in good condition, and they bring in eight million tourists a year.
in-good-condition.szh: 老街能一直保持得好好的，每年还能招来八百万游客。

more.en: He'll keep it in good condition for fifteen years — he just won't finish it.
more.szh: 他会替你好好保存十五年——就是一直看不完。

w-roast.note: Sunday roast 是英国传统的周日午餐：烤肉、烤土豆和蔬菜，配肉汁。
w-roast.en: Right, everyone: lunch is served at one on Sunday, and roast beef is on the menu.
w-roast.szh: 好了各位：周日一点开饭，主菜是烤牛肉。

on-the-menu.note: available to eat at a meal or in a restaurant
on-the-menu.tip: 也能用来比喻「在计划里」：A trip to Paris isn't on the menu this year.
on-the-menu.example: Fish and chips is always on the menu on Fridays.
on-the-menu.en: Right, everyone: lunch is served at one on Sunday, and roast beef is on the menu.
on-the-menu.szh: 好了各位：周日一点开饭，主菜是烤牛肉。

more.en: Pottery and salsa are both on the menu at your local college.
more.szh: 你们那儿的成人学院就开着陶艺课和萨尔萨舞课。

more.en: Cold ones aren't on the menu.
more.szh: 冷水澡？我这儿可没这道菜。

count-me-in.note: used to say that you want to join an activity or plan
count-me-in.tip: 反过来说「别算我」是 count me out；只用 me，一般不说 count him in。
count-me-in.example: Pizza after work? Count me in!
count-me-in.en: If you need a hand in the kitchen, count me in.
count-me-in.szh: 厨房要是缺人手，算我一个。

more.en: Count me in.
more.szh: 算我一个。

more.en: When Liu Yang starts a school team, say "Count me in" — but don't give up computers.
more.szh: 刘洋组校队的时候，你就说「算我一个」——不过电脑可别丢下。

bring-sb-sth-along.note: to take someone or something with you when you go somewhere
bring-sb-sth-along.tip: 人或东西放在 bring 和 along 中间：bring Jake along；短的代词一定放中间：bring him along。
bring-sb-sth-along.example: Feel free to bring your partner along to the party.
bring-sb-sth-along.szh: 我能带 Jake 一起来吗？

more.en: Some people even bring fruit along from their own gardens.
more.szh: 有人还从自家园子里带水果过来。

more.en: Last month, my sister brought me along to a sale in Hove.
more.szh: 上个月，我妹妹拉我去霍夫逛一场促销。

w-vegetarian.note: 口语常简称 veggie；完全不吃动物制品的是 vegan。

w-easter.note: 每年三四月间的节日，英国学校会放两周假；首字母大写。
w-easter.en: My oven hasn't been used since Easter, so the beef can be cooked at mine.
w-easter.szh: 我的烤箱从复活节起就没用过，牛肉拿到我家烤吧。

help-out.note: to help someone, especially when they are busy
help-out.tip: 比 help 更口语，常不带宾语；要说帮谁可以 help sb out。
help-out.example: My sister sometimes helps out at the café on Saturdays.
help-out.en: And Chen can come round and help out.

more.en: Tom offered to help out.
more.szh: Tom 主动说要来搭把手。

w-dumpling.note: 包饺子说 make dumplings；英国菜里也有一种 dumpling，是面团做的团子。
w-dumpling.en: Shall I make some vegetable dumplings for Jake?
w-dumpling.szh: 要不我给 Jake 包点素饺子？

w-potato.note: 复数加 es：potatoes；烤土豆 roast potatoes 是周日午餐的标配。
w-potato.en: We haven't got enough potatoes for ten, so I'm just popping out to the shop.
w-potato.szh: 土豆不够十个人吃，我这就去趟商店。

pop-out.note: to leave a place for a short time
pop-out.tip: 英式口语，常和 just 连用；去哪里用 to，为了什么用 for：pop out for some milk。
pop-out.example: I'm just popping out for a coffee — back in ten minutes.
pop-out.en: We haven't got enough potatoes for ten, so I'm just popping out to the shop.
pop-out.szh: 土豆不够十个人吃，我这就去趟商店。

more.en: I'm just popping out for a coffee and a think.
more.szh: 我出去买杯咖啡，顺便想一想。

no-worries.note: used to say that something is not a problem, or as a reply to thanks
no-worries.tip: 非常口语，英国、澳大利亚常用；回答 Thank you 时也能说，相当于 You're welcome。
no-worries.example: "Sorry I'm late." "No worries — we haven't started yet."

w-switch-off.note: at the wall 指墙上的电源插座开关；英国插座多数自带开关。
w-switch-off.en: It was switched off at the wall.
w-switch-off.szh: 是墙上的电源开关被关掉了。

go-on-about-sth.note: to talk about something for a long time, often in a way that is boring for other people
go-on-about-sth.tip: 带一点抱怨或调侃；后面接 about：go on about work。和 go on（继续）不是一回事。
go-on-about-sth.example: He keeps going on about his new car.
go-on-about-sth.en: She's 82 now, and she still can't walk past an old building without going on about it for ten minutes.
go-on-about-sth.szh: 如今她 82 岁了，路过一栋老房子，还是忍不住要讲上十分钟。

more.en: "People go on about expensive superfoods, but frozen peas are just as good for you," she says.
more.szh: 「大家老念叨那些贵得要命的超级食物，其实冷冻豌豆对身体一样好，」她说。

more.en: My partner says I go on about this too much, and he's probably right.
more.szh: 我家那位说我在这件事上唠叨个没完，他大概说得没错。

w-knock-down.note: knock down a wall / a house；也能说「撞倒」：He was knocked down by a bike。
w-knock-down.en: And why wasn't it knocked down?

w-teenager.note: 指 13 到 19 岁（thirteen 到 nineteen 都带 teen）的人。
w-teenager.en: "Teenagers don't care about kings," she says.
w-teenager.szh: 「十几岁的孩子才不在乎国王呢，」她说。

w-sweet-shop.note: 英式说法，sweets 是糖果；美式说 candy store。
w-sweet-shop.en: "And to my surprise, my house turned out to be an old sweet shop."
w-sweet-shop.szh: 「结果没想到，我家以前居然是一家糖果店。」

take-an-interest-in-sth.note: to start to be interested in something and want to learn about it
take-an-interest-in-sth.tip: 介词用 in；说「开始感兴趣」这个变化。比较 be interested in（状态）。
take-an-interest-in-sth.example: My son has started to take an interest in cooking.
take-an-interest-in-sth.en: "I've taken an interest in old buildings ever since."
take-an-interest-in-sth.szh: 「从那以后，我就对老房子感兴趣了。」

more.en: Our investors have taken a real interest in it, too, so dark mode can wait.
more.szh: 投资人对这个也特别感兴趣，所以深色模式可以往后放。

know-sth-inside-out.tip: 东西放在 know 和 inside out 中间；inside out 单独用是「里朝外」：wear a T-shirt inside out。
know-sth-inside-out.example: She knows the codebase inside out, so ask her first.
know-sth-inside-out.en: Margaret knows the city inside out.
know-sth-inside-out.szh: Margaret 对这座城市了如指掌。

more.en: I know that guy's recipes inside out now, if that helps.
more.szh: 那个人的菜谱我现在倒背如流，要是这能算点什么的话。

more.en: Now she knows the history of Indian stamps inside out.
more.szh: 现在她对印度邮票的历史了如指掌。

bring-sth-to-life.note: to make something more interesting or exciting
bring-sth-to-life.tip: 常说讲故事、讲课、表演把东西讲「活」了；不及物的说法是 come to life。
bring-sth-to-life.example: Good examples bring a talk to life.
bring-sth-to-life.en: And when she talks about it, she really brings it to life.
bring-sth-to-life.szh: 她一讲起来，老城就活了。

more.en: At nine in the morning, that first cup brings the whole office to life.
more.szh: 早上九点，就是这第一杯，让整个办公室都活过来了。

more.en: They'll bring English to life about a week later.
more.szh: 大概一个星期以后，那些笑话会让英语真正鲜活起来。

w-lead.note: 过去式 led；lead a tour 带团参观，lead a team 带团队。
w-lead.en: Every Thursday, she leads a free walking tour of the city walls for members of the public.
w-lead.szh: 每周四，她都为普通游客带一次免费的城墙徒步游。

w-cancel.note: 英式拼写双写 l：cancelled、cancelling；美式常写 canceled。
w-cancel.en: Tours are rarely cancelled at short notice.

w-route.note: 英式读音像 root；bus route 公交线路。
w-route.en: This month, part of the wall is being repaired, so the group's taking a longer route.
w-route.szh: 这个月，有一段城墙正在维修，所以大家得绕远路走。

be-passionate-about-sth.note: to have very strong feelings of love or interest for something
be-passionate-about-sth.tip: 介词用 about，后面接名词或 doing：passionate about teaching；比 like 强得多。
be-passionate-about-sth.example: Our team is passionate about good design.
be-passionate-about-sth.en: She's always been passionate about the history of ordinary people.
be-passionate-about-sth.szh: 她一直对普通人的历史特别着迷。

more.en: He was so passionate about the project that he forgot to eat lunch.
more.szh: 他干得太投入，连午饭都忘了吃。

w-ordinary.note: ordinary people 普通人，和国王、名人相对。
w-ordinary.en: She's always been passionate about the history of ordinary people.
w-ordinary.szh: 她一直对普通人的历史特别着迷。

pass-sth-on.note: to give something to another person, for example knowledge or a message
pass-sth-on.tip: 代词放中间：pass it on；给谁用 to：pass it on to your children。
pass-sth-on.example: Could you pass this message on to Tom?
pass-sth-on.en: "Make them ask why, and make sure they pass it on."
pass-sth-on.szh: 「让学生学会问为什么，还要让他们把这份好奇传下去。」

more.en: The chip passes this new sound on to the speakers by your ears.
more.szh: 芯片再把这个新声音传给你耳边的扬声器。

introduce-yourself.note: to tell someone your name when you meet them for the first time
introduce-yourself.tip: yourself 要随人变：introduce myself / ourselves；向谁介绍用 to：introduce yourself to the team。
introduce-yourself.example: Let's go round the table and introduce ourselves.
introduce-yourself.en: The pub was so loud that when I introduced myself to the barman, my name got misheard.
introduce-yourself.szh: 酒吧里吵得要命，我跟酒保自我介绍时，他把我的名字听错了。

more.en: I used your guest pass and introduced myself to Dan.
more.szh: 我用了你的访客卡，还跟 Dan 做了自我介绍。

more.en: At her first stamp fair, she was too shy to introduce herself.
more.szh: 第一次去邮票展会时，她害羞得连自我介绍都不敢。

w-barman.note: 女性是 barmaid；现在也常说中性的 bartender 或 bar staff。
w-barman.en: The pub was so loud that when I introduced myself to the barman, my name got misheard.
w-barman.szh: 酒吧里吵得要命，我跟酒保自我介绍时，他把我的名字听错了。

w-mishear.note: mis- 表示「错」：misread 看错、misunderstand 误解；过去式和过去分词是 misheard。
w-mishear.en: The pub was so loud that when I introduced myself to the barman, my name got misheard.
w-mishear.szh: 酒吧里吵得要命，我跟酒保自我介绍时，他把我的名字听错了。

w-register.note: register for a course 报名上课；名词 registration。
w-register.en: Before I could make it clear that my name was Chen, our team got registered as "Shane and the Taylors".
w-register.szh: 我还没来得及说清楚我叫小陈，我们队就被登记成了「Shane 和 Taylor 一家」。

more.en: My class was in Room 304 of Building B, where I'd already been marked absent on the register.
more.szh: 我的班在 B 栋的 304，那边的点名册上已经把我记成缺课了。

it-s-a-long-story.note: said when something is too complicated to explain now, or you do not want to explain it
it-s-a-long-story.tip: 常常是不想解释的客气说法；讲过去的事也能说 It was a long story。
it-s-a-long-story.example: "Why are you wearing two different shoes?" "It's a long story."
it-s-a-long-story.en: When Uncle Mike asked about the new name, Tom just said, "It's a long story."
it-s-a-long-story.szh: Mike 叔叔问起这个新队名，Tom 只说了一句：「说来话长。」

more.en: It's a long story, but here's the short version.
more.szh: 说来话长，我给你讲个简短版。

more.en: When Tom asked why I kept walking past the shop, I just said, "It's a long story."
more.szh: Tom 问我为什么老在那家店门口转悠，我只说了句：「说来话长。」

go-along-with-sth.note: to accept something or agree with someone, often without saying what you really think
go-along-with-sth.tip: 后面接想法、计划或人：go along with the idea / with Tom；常带「其实不太情愿」的意思。
go-along-with-sth.example: I didn't love the plan, but I went along with it.
go-along-with-sth.en: So I went along with it, and I got called Shane all night.
go-along-with-sth.szh: 于是我就将错就错，被人叫了一晚上 Shane。

more.en: But he usually goes along with Chen's experiments.
more.szh: 不过小陈的各种实验，他通常都肯配合。

more.en: Whatever you two decide, I'll go along with it.
more.szh: 你们俩怎么定，我都照办。

mistake-sb-for-sb.zh: 把某人错当成另一个人
mistake-sb-for-sb.note: to think wrongly that one person or thing is another
mistake-sb-for-sb.tip: mistake 的过去式是 mistook，过去分词 mistaken；介词用 for，不用 as。
mistake-sb-for-sb.example: People often mistake me for my brother.
mistake-sb-for-sb.en: Later, Uncle Mike mistook me for one of Rosie's friends and asked how my sister's wedding went.
mistake-sb-for-sb.szh: 后来，Mike 叔叔把我当成了 Rosie 的朋友，还问我姐姐的婚礼办得怎么样。

more.en: Her watch has even mistaken her for someone asleep while she was watching a long film.
more.szh: 有一次她在看一部很长的电影，手表居然把她当成了睡着的人。

be-named-after-sb-sth.note: to be given the same name as someone or something
be-named-after-sb-sth.tip: 英式用 named after，美式也说 named for；人、街道、城市、船都能用。
be-named-after-sb-sth.example: The street was named after a famous doctor.
be-named-after-sb-sth.en: Then a woman at the bar asked, "Were you named after the old cowboy film?"
be-named-after-sb-sth.szh: 接着，吧台边一位女士问：「你的名字是照那部老西部片起的吗？」

more.en: My team's just launched Rota, an app named after the chore list on my fridge.
more.szh: 我的团队刚上线了 Rota，名字就来自我家冰箱上那张家务表。

w-cowboy.note: Shane 是 1953 年一部很有名的美国西部片；英式口语里 cowboy 还指「不靠谱的工人」。
w-cowboy.en: Then a woman at the bar asked, "Were you named after the old cowboy film?"
w-cowboy.szh: 接着，吧台边一位女士问：「你的名字是照那部老西部片起的吗？」

laugh-sth-off.note: to laugh about something to show that it does not worry or upset you
laugh-sth-off.tip: 代词放中间：laugh it off；常用于尴尬、出错、被批评的场合。
laugh-sth-off.example: She fell over on stage, but she laughed it off.
laugh-sth-off.en: I laughed it off and told her my parents loved horses.
laugh-sth-off.szh: 我打了个哈哈，说我爸妈特别喜欢马。

more.en: Mum said he was only showing off, but he just laughed it off.
more.szh: 妈妈说他就是在显摆，他笑笑没当回事。

w-badge.note: 开会、活动时别在胸前写名字的牌子叫 name badge。
w-badge.en: Tom's mum even went out of her way to make me a name badge.
w-badge.szh: Tom 的妈妈甚至还特意给我做了个名牌。

w-beer-mat.note: 英国酒吧桌上的纸板杯垫，紧张时有人会把它撕碎。
w-beer-mat.en: Pete got so stressed that he took a beer mat apart.
w-beer-mat.szh: Pete 急得把一张啤酒杯垫拆得七零八落。

w-dynasty.note: the Ming dynasty 明朝，the Tang dynasty 唐朝；dynasty 小写，朝代名大写。
w-dynasty.en: It was about the Ming dynasty, and everyone turned to me.
w-dynasty.szh: 那道题问的是明朝，大家齐刷刷看向我。

i-m-writing-to.zh: 来信是想……（邮件开头说明目的）
i-m-writing-to.note: used at the start of an email or letter to say why you are writing
i-m-writing-to.tip: 后面接动词原形：I'm writing to ask / to apologise / to confirm；比 I want to … 正式、礼貌。
i-m-writing-to.example: I'm writing to complain about my last order.
i-m-writing-to.en: "I'm writing to ask about a camera I lost at the museum on Thursday afternoon."
i-m-writing-to.szh: 「来信是想询问一台相机，我周四下午把它落在了贵馆。」

more.en: "I'm writing to ask a simple question," she said in her email.
more.szh: 她在邮件里说：「我写信是想问个简单的问题。」

more.en: I even started an email to the shop: "I'm writing to ask if the green band is still in stock."
more.szh: 我甚至给店里写了半封邮件：「我写信是想问一下，绿表带那款还有没有货。」

w-entrance.note: 出口是 exit；at the main entrance 在正门。
w-entrance.en: Well, I had my bag checked at the entrance at about two.
w-entrance.szh: 嗯，两点左右我在入口让人查过包。

as-far-as-i-know.note: used to say that you think something is true, but you are not completely sure
as-far-as-i-know.tip: 说的是自己的了解有限；不说 as far as I knew it，也不说 as long as I know。
as-far-as-i-know.example: As far as I know, the meeting is still at three.
as-far-as-i-know.en: As far as I know, the camera was still in it then.
as-far-as-i-know.szh: 据我所知，那时相机还在包里。

more.en: "As far as I know, nobody in our family likes it except Grandma," Chen said.
more.szh: 「据我所知，咱家除了奶奶，没人爱吃这个，」小陈说。

more.en: And as far as I know, I chose the right size — I checked your size guide twice.
more.szh: 而且据我所知，我选的尺码没错，你们的尺码表我看了两遍。

w-mallard.note: mallard 本义是绿头野鸭；作火车名时首字母大写，不加 the。
w-mallard.en: Then I had my photo taken next to Mallard.
w-mallard.szh: 然后请人给我在「野鸭号」旁边拍了张照。

w-bench.note: 公园、车站、博物馆里供人坐的长凳。
w-bench.en: I think the camera got left on a bench in the Great Hall.
w-bench.szh: 我觉得相机是落在大厅的长椅上了。

more.en: In 1994, he was showing us an experiment when he accidentally set fire to a bench.
more.szh: 1994 年，他给我们做一个实验，结果不小心把实验台点着了。

w-band.note: band 常见的意思是「乐队」，这里指一圈带子；橡皮筋叫 rubber band。
w-band.en: It's an old black Fujifilm with a red band, and it isn't worth much.
w-band.szh: 是一台黑色的老富士相机，背带是红色的，不值什么钱。

more.en: It was a £240 watch with a plain white face and a dark green leather band.
more.szh: 一块 240 英镑的手表，白色素表盘，墨绿色皮表带。

mean-the-world-to-sb.zh: 对某人来说无比重要；是某人的宝贝
mean-the-world-to-sb.note: to be extremely important to someone, usually because of feelings or memories
mean-the-world-to-sb.tip: 比第 12 课的 mean a lot to sb 语气更重；主语是东西或人，to 后面接人：She means the world to me。
mean-the-world-to-sb.example: This old watch isn't expensive, but it means the world to my dad.
mean-the-world-to-sb.en: But it means the world to me.
mean-the-world-to-sb.szh: 可它对我来说太重要了。

more.en: This launch means the world to me.
more.szh: 这次上线对我太重要了。

look-out-for-sth.note: to watch carefully so that you will notice something or someone
look-out-for-sth.tip: 和第 41 课的 keep an eye on 比：look out for 是「留意着找」，keep an eye on 是「看着别出事」；单说 Look out! 是「小心！」。
look-out-for-sth.example: Look out for a blue door on the left.
look-out-for-sth.en: Right. Now ask them to look out for it, but politely.
look-out-for-sth.szh: 好。现在请他们帮忙留意一下，不过要客气点。

more.en: Look out for the red dots in your own work, because most of them can be removed.
more.szh: 留意一下你们自己产品里的小红点，大部分其实都可以去掉。

i-d-be-grateful-if.zh: 如果……我将不胜感激（礼貌请求）
i-d-be-grateful-if.note: a polite way to ask someone to do something, often used in formal emails
i-d-be-grateful-if.tip: if 后面常用 you could …；比 Please … 客气得多，正式邮件常用。
i-d-be-grateful-if.example: I'd be grateful if you could reply by Friday.
i-d-be-grateful-if.en: "I'd be grateful if your staff could check the Great Hall."
i-d-be-grateful-if.szh: 「如贵馆工作人员能帮忙查看一下大厅，我将不胜感激。」

more.en: Anyway, I'd be grateful if someone could send me the new rota for June.
more.szh: 好了，要是谁能把六月的新排班表发我一份，我就太感谢了。

more.en: I'd be grateful if people listened to their bodies instead of checking their wrists."
more.szh: 我希望大家多听听自己身体的感觉，别老盯着手腕。」

get-sth-back.note: to have something again after you lost it or gave it to someone
get-sth-back.tip: 东西放在 get 和 back 中间：get it back；借出去的东西要回来也用它。
get-sth-back.example: Did you ever get your money back?
get-sth-back.en: "I'm staying in York until Sunday, and I'd love to get it back before then."
get-sth-back.szh: 「我在约克待到周日，很希望在那之前能拿回相机。」

more.en: He's lost three umbrellas on that bus, and he's never got one back.
more.szh: 他在那趟车上丢过三把伞，一把都没找回来。

w-postage.note: post 是邮寄（英式），postage 是邮寄的费用；美式多说 shipping。

more.en: Who'll deal with my return, and do I have to pay for postage?
more.szh: 退货由谁来处理？邮费要我自己出吗？

w-battery.note: 换电池是 replace the battery，充电是 charge the battery；电量低说 The battery is low。
w-battery.en: Look, I've had the battery replaced at the shop on Gillygate.
w-battery.szh: 瞧，我在吉利盖特街那家店给它换了块电池。

w-drainpipe.note: 英国老房子外墙上竖着的铁管，把屋顶的雨水排下来。
w-drainpipe.en: I've taken 212 photos of drainpipes on listed buildings.
w-drainpipe.szh: 我拍了 212 张受保护老建筑上的排水管。

w-viking.note: 八到十一世纪从北欧来的人，曾占领约克，叫它 Jorvik；放在名词前也当形容词用。
w-viking.en: So, first I'll tell you where this shoe was found, and then what it tells us about life in Viking York.
w-viking.szh: 我先讲这只鞋是在哪儿发现的，再讲它能告诉我们维京时代的约克人怎么过日子。

w-leather.note: 放在名词前当形容词：a leather bag、leather shoes。
w-leather.en: Now, this is a copy of a small leather shoe, and the real one is kept upstairs.
w-leather.szh: 来，这是一只小皮鞋的复制品，真品放在楼上。

more.en: In a shop near Bond Street, I tried on a pair of white leather trainers.
more.szh: 在邦德街附近的一家店里，我试穿了一双白色皮运动鞋。

in-one-piece.tip: 也常用来说人「平安无事」：They got home in one piece.
in-one-piece.example: The package arrived in one piece.
in-one-piece.en: It was found in one piece in the 1970s, about six metres under the street we're standing on.
in-one-piece.szh: 它是上世纪七十年代出土的，完完整整，就在我们脚下这条街大约六米深的地方。

more.en: But somehow, they got home in one piece.
more.szh: 可不知怎么的，鸡蛋一个都没碎，平平安安到了家。

more.en: To be fair, the parcel arrived in one piece, and the wool feels lovely.
more.szh: 说句公道话，包裹送到时完好无损，羊毛摸着也挺舒服。

be-made-of-sth.note: to have something as its material
be-made-of-sth.tip: 看得出原材料用 made of（皮鞋、木桌）；看不出了用 made from：Paper is made from wood。
be-made-of-sth.example: The table is made of old wood from a farmhouse.
be-made-of-sth.en: It's made of goat leather, and it's a size four.

more.en: He was building a little tower made of pens.
more.szh: 他在用笔搭一座小塔。

more.en: It's made of iron, and it's older than me.
more.szh: 是口铁锅，岁数比我还大。

w-goat.note: 绵羊是 sheep；goat leather 就是山羊皮。
w-goat.en: It's made of goat leather, and it's a size four.

more.en: And I'd write terrible poems about the farmer's goat.
more.szh: 我还会给农场主家的山羊写特别烂的诗。

w-belong-to.note: 不用进行时：不说 It is belonging to me。
w-belong-to.en: That's why it's thought that it belonged to a teenager.
w-belong-to.szh: 正因为这样，人们认为它的主人是个十几岁的孩子。

in-those-days.note: at a time in the past
in-those-days.tip: 和第 4 课的 these days（如今）相对；说过去的情况，动词用过去时。
in-those-days.example: In those days, nobody had a mobile phone.
in-those-days.en: In those days, hardly anyone wrote anything down.
in-those-days.szh: 那个年代，几乎没人会把事情记下来。

more.en: In those days, nobody did running tests — you just ran.
more.szh: 那时候没人做什么跑步测试，跑就完了。

more.en: In those days, our chore list was a sheet of paper on the wall, and I was almost sorry to leave it.
more.szh: 那时候我们的值日表就是墙上的一张纸，毕业离开时，我差点还舍不得它。

w-comb.note: b 不发音，读作 /kəʊm/；当动词是「梳」：comb your hair。
w-comb.en: But actually, hundreds of combs were found here at Coppergate.
w-comb.szh: 可实际上，在铜门街这儿出土了好几百把梳子。

make-do-with-sth.note: to manage with something that is not as good as you want, because there is nothing better
make-do-with-sth.tip: 后面接名词；make 的过去式 made：made do with。没有宾语时可以只说 make do。
make-do-with-sth.example: There's no milk, so we'll have to make do with black coffee.
make-do-with-sth.en: So they made do with what they had.
make-do-with-sth.szh: 所以只能有什么将就着用什么。

more.en: Then we tried to make do with a group chat, which was even worse.
more.szh: 后来我们只好凑合着用群聊，结果更糟。

believe-it-or-not.zh: 信不信由你；说来你可能不信
believe-it-or-not.note: used before saying something surprising but true
believe-it-or-not.tip: 常放在句首，后面加逗号；讲解、讲故事时用来抓住听众。
believe-it-or-not.example: Believe it or not, I've never seen the sea.
believe-it-or-not.en: Believe it or not, the owner had this one mended at least three times.
believe-it-or-not.szh: 说出来你们可能不信，这只鞋的主人至少找人补过三次。

more.en: Believe it or not, it'll all be for the best.
more.szh: 信不信由你，这一切到头来都是好事。

more.en: Believe it or not, most people don't even mention it.
more.szh: 说来你可能不信，大多数人提都没提。

w-mend.note: 多用于衣服、鞋这类东西；修机器、电器常说 fix 或 repair。
w-mend.en: Believe it or not, the owner had this one mended at least three times.
w-mend.szh: 说出来你们可能不信，这只鞋的主人至少找人补过三次。

wear-out.note: to become thin or damaged after being used a lot
wear-out.tip: wear 的过去式 wore，过去分词 worn：worn out。人也可以 be worn out（累坏了）。
wear-out.example: My running shoes wore out after six months.
wear-out.en: It was only thrown away when it finally wore out.
wear-out.szh: 直到彻底穿坏了，才被扔掉。

set-off.tip: set 的过去式和过去分词都是 set；从哪里出发用 from，去哪里用 for：set off for London。
set-off.example: We set off early to miss the traffic.
set-off.en: We set off from Tom's parents' at three.
set-off.szh: 我们三点从 Tom 爸妈家出发。

more.en: I set off at a quarter past six every morning, and the bus is always full of nurses.
more.szh: 我每天早上六点一刻出门，车上总是挤满了护士。

more.en: And on New Year's Day, I set off along the river on it.
more.szh: 元旦那天，我骑着它沿着河出发了。

w-rename.note: re- 表示「重新」：rewrite 重写、rebuild 重建；程序员常说 rename a file。
w-rename.en: At the quiz, I got renamed Shane.
w-rename.szh: 问答之夜，我被改名叫了 Shane。

w-photograph.note: 当动词比 take a photo of 正式；重音在第一个音节。
w-photograph.en: And thanks to Margaret, 212 drainpipes have been photographed.
w-photograph.szh: 多亏了 Margaret，足足拍了 212 根排水管。

make-the-most-of-sth.note: to use or enjoy something as much as possible while you can
make-the-most-of-sth.tip: 常用于时间、机会、好天气；most 前面一定有 the。
make-the-most-of-sth.example: It's sunny today, so let's make the most of it.
make-the-most-of-sth.en: But I made the most of every day.
make-the-most-of-sth.szh: 不过，我每一天都过得很充实。

more.en: Make the most of the light evenings.
more.szh: 趁着傍晚天还亮，多出去跑跑。

more.en: So, Tom and I wanted a second-hand car, to make the most of our weekends.
more.szh: 我跟 Tom 想买辆二手车，好好利用周末出去玩。

be-sorry-to-leave.note: to feel sad because you have to go away from a place or people you like
be-sorry-to-leave.tip: 这里的 sorry 是「难过、遗憾」，不是道歉；be sorry to hear sth 是「听到……很难过」。
be-sorry-to-leave.example: We had a great time here, and we're sorry to leave.
be-sorry-to-leave.en: I'm tired but happy, and really sorry to leave.
be-sorry-to-leave.szh: 我累是累，但很开心，真舍不得走。

more.en: I'll be sorry to leave in June, you know.
more.szh: 跟你说，六月要走了，我还真有点舍不得。

more.en: In those days, our chore list was a sheet of paper on the wall, and I was almost sorry to leave it.
more.szh: 那时候我们的值日表就是墙上的一张纸，毕业离开时，我差点还舍不得它。

can-t-get-over-sth.zh: （惊讶得）想不通；还没回过神来
can-t-get-over-sth.note: to be very surprised by something and keep thinking about it
can-t-get-over-sth.tip: 后面常接 how 从句或名词：I can't get over the view；get over sth 单用是「从（病、失恋）中恢复」。
can-t-get-over-sth.example: I can't get over how cheap the flat was.
can-t-get-over-sth.en: I can't get over how much history fits into one small city.
can-t-get-over-sth.szh: 一座小城装得下这么多历史，我到现在都觉得不可思议。

more.en: We couldn't get over how quickly it disappeared under pizza menus.
more.szh: 没想到它那么快就被一堆披萨菜单盖住了。

take-sth-for-granted.zh: 认为……理所当然（因而不在意）
take-sth-for-granted.note: to not notice or value something because it is always there
take-sth-for-granted.tip: 东西放在 take 和 for granted 中间；take 的过去分词 taken：have taken it for granted。
take-sth-for-granted.example: We often take clean water for granted.
take-sth-for-granted.en: In London, I walk past old buildings every day, and I've always taken them for granted.
take-sth-for-granted.szh: 在伦敦，我每天从老房子旁边走过，一直觉得理所当然。

more.en: That means they take it for granted.
more.szh: 这说明他们已经觉得理所当然了。

w-upload.note: 反义词 download（下载）；名词也是 upload。
w-upload.en: My photos are being uploaded right now, so you'll see them on Monday.
w-upload.szh: 照片现在正在上传，周一你们就能看到。

have-the-time-of-your-life.text: have the time of your life
have-the-time-of-your-life.zh: 过得特别开心；度过最快乐的时光
have-the-time-of-your-life.tip: your 要随人变：my / their life；常用现在完成时或过去时说一段经历。
have-the-time-of-your-life.example: The kids had the time of their lives at the beach.
have-the-time-of-your-life.en: All in all, I've had the time of my life.
have-the-time-of-your-life.szh: 总之，这一周是我过得最开心的日子。

w-announcement.note: 动词 announce；车站、机场的广播都叫 announcement。
w-announcement.en: As we got off, there was an announcement.
w-announcement.szh: 我们刚下车，就听到一条广播。

more.en: Some models even have a "listen" button, so you can still hear the driver's announcements.
more.szh: 有些型号还带一个「收听」按钮，好让你还能听见司机的广播。

w-passenger.note: 广播里常把 passenger 直接放在名字前面，像头衔一样。
w-passenger.en: "Would passenger Shane Taylor please come to the information desk?"
w-passenger.szh: 「请乘客 Shane Taylor 到问讯处来一下。」

w-luggage.note: 不可数，不说 a luggage；一件行李是 a piece of luggage。
w-luggage.en: Tom had written that name on my luggage label as a joke.
w-luggage.szh: 原来 Tom 开玩笑，在我的行李牌上写了这个名字。

w-label.note: 英式读音 /ˈleɪbl/；衣服上的标签、文件夹上的标签都叫 label。
w-label.en: Tom had written that name on my luggage label as a joke.
w-label.szh: 原来 Tom 开玩笑，在我的行李牌上写了这个名字。

w-trainers.note: 英式说法，常用复数；美式说 sneakers。
w-trainers.en: Then he comes across a video of a man cleaning old trainers, then another.
w-trainers.szh: 结果刷到一个男的洗旧球鞋的视频，接着又是一个。

can-t-put-sth-down.note: to find something so interesting that you cannot stop reading, watching or using it
can-t-put-sth-down.tip: 常说书好看：I couldn't put it down。代词要放中间：put it down，不说 put down it。
can-t-put-sth-down.example: The book was so good that I couldn't put it down.
can-t-put-sth-down.en: Honestly, he can't put the phone down until one.
can-t-put-sth-down.szh: 说真的，不到一点，他根本放不下手机。

more.en: Honestly, I just couldn't put my phone down at night.
more.szh: 说真的，我以前一到晚上就是放不下手机。

more.en: Dad had given me a Harry Potter book, and I couldn't put it down.
more.szh: 是爸爸给了我一本《哈利·波特》，我一拿起来就放不下。

stay-up-late.note: to go to bed much later than usual
stay-up-late.tip: stay up 是「不去睡」，late 可以换成具体时间：stay up until two。别和 get up late（起得晚）混。
stay-up-late.example: We stayed up late talking about the trip.
stay-up-late.en: And every night, he says it's the last time he'll stay up late.
stay-up-late.szh: 每天晚上他都说，这是最后一次熬夜。

more.en: Don't stay up late the night before a run.
more.szh: 跑步前一晚别熬夜。

more.en: I stayed up late three nights in a row, reading adverts.
more.szh: 我一连三个晚上熬夜看卖车广告。

w-impressed.note: not impressed 常是委婉的「不满意、不以为然」。
w-impressed.en: When he told her about his evenings, she wasn't impressed.
w-impressed.szh: 他跟她说了自己晚上的情况，她听了直摇头。

more.en: Tom wasn't impressed.
more.szh: Tom 可一点都不买账。

wind-down.note: to relax after a busy or exciting time, especially before sleep
wind-down.tip: 这里的 wind 读 /waɪnd/，过去式 wound 读 /waʊnd/；和「风」wind /wɪnd/ 不是一个词。
wind-down.example: I usually read for half an hour to wind down after work.
wind-down.en: "Your brain needs time to wind down."
wind-down.szh: 「你的大脑得有时间慢慢静下来。」

more.en: It'd been a long week at work, and a walk down Oxford Street is my way of winding down.
more.szh: 上了一周累人的班，去牛津街走一走，是我放松的法子。

more.en: I'm going to order another coffee and wind down instead of opening my laptop.
more.szh: 我再点一杯咖啡放松一下，不开电脑了。

w-insist.note: 后面接 on doing：insist on paying（非要付钱）。
w-insist.en: The owner insists on showing him the ropes, even though it's only got two buttons.
w-insist.szh: 店老板非要手把手教他怎么用，虽然那闹钟一共就两个按钮。

set-an-alarm.note: to make a clock or phone ring at a certain time
set-an-alarm.tip: 定在几点用 for：set an alarm for six；闹钟响了说 the alarm goes off。set 的过去式、过去分词都是 set。
set-an-alarm.example: Can you set an alarm for half past five?
set-an-alarm.en: "This one sets the alarm, and this one turns it off."

switch-off.note: to turn off a light or machine; also, to stop thinking about work and relax
switch-off.tip: 英式更常说 switch off，美式多说 turn off；人当主语时是「放空、不想事」。
switch-off.example: I can't switch off when I'm on holiday — I keep checking emails.
switch-off.en: By half past ten, he's switched off the light and feels he's making progress.
switch-off.szh: 十点半，他已经关了灯，觉得自己总算有进步了。

w-tick.note: 也指打勾：tick the box（在方框里打勾）。
w-tick.en: Then he hears it: tick, tick, tick.
w-tick.szh: 然后他听见了：嘀嗒，嘀嗒，嘀嗒。

be-wide-awake.zh: 完全清醒；一点睡意都没有
be-wide-awake.note: to be completely awake, often when you want to be asleep
be-wide-awake.tip: wide 在这里是「完全」，只和 awake、open 这几个词连用：wide open。反义是 fast asleep（第 1 课）。
be-wide-awake.example: It was three in the morning and the baby was wide awake.
be-wide-awake.en: The clock is so loud that at twenty to one, he's still wide awake.
be-wide-awake.szh: 钟走得太响了，到了十二点四十，他还是一点睡意都没有。

w-hand.note: 时针 hour hand，分针 minute hand，秒针 second hand。
w-hand.en: He lies there, keeping an eye on the red hand.
w-hand.szh: 他就那么躺着，盯着那根红色的秒针。

w-pillow.en: He goes through his options: a pillow, a drawer, the window.
w-pillow.szh: 他把办法挨个想了一遍：拿枕头捂上、塞进抽屉、扔出窗外。

w-drawer.note: 读 /drɔː/，w 和 er 基本不发音。
w-drawer.en: He goes through his options: a pillow, a drawer, the window.
w-drawer.szh: 他把办法挨个想了一遍：拿枕头捂上、塞进抽屉、扔出窗外。

more.en: And the watch, sitting in a drawer, still sends her a message every morning: "We missed you last night."
more.szh: 而那块躺在抽屉里的手表，每天早上还是会给她发一条消息：「昨晚我们想你了。」

leave-sth-lying-around.note: to leave things in places where they should not be, instead of putting them away
leave-sth-lying-around.tip: lying 是 lie（躺、放着）的 -ing，不是「说谎」；英式也说 lying about。
leave-sth-lying-around.example: Don't leave your keys lying around — you'll lose them again.
leave-sth-lying-around.en: Chen, you leave mugs lying around everywhere.

more.en: And I never left them lying around in the hall like my other shoes.
more.szh: 也从来不像别的鞋那样，随手扔在门厅里。

more.en: So, Tom's got hooked on Chinese films lately, and I tend to leave my laptop lying around.
more.szh: Tom 最近迷上了中国电影，而我又总爱把笔记本电脑随手一放。

pile-up.note: to become a large amount, often because you have not dealt with it
pile-up.tip: 可以说东西，也可以说事情：The work is piling up。名词是 a pile of（一堆）。
pile-up.example: My emails always pile up when I'm on holiday.
pile-up.en: The post has been piling up by the door since I arrived.
pile-up.szh: 我来了以后，门口的信就越堆越多。

more.en: She sends about forty a day, so they just pile up.
more.szh: 她一天发四十来条，消息全堆在那儿没看。

more.en: Every night the marking piled up.
more.szh: 每天晚上，要批的作业都堆成山。

w-gas-bill.note: 英国的水、电、煤气分开收费，统称 bills：pay the bills。
w-gas-bill.en: And yesterday I found your gas bill under a pizza box, completely by chance.
w-gas-bill.szh: 昨天我还在一个披萨盒底下翻出了你的煤气账单，纯属碰巧。

do-the-washing-up.note: to wash the plates, cups and pans after a meal
do-the-washing-up.tip: 英式说法，固定用 do，不说 make the washing-up；美式说 do the dishes。洗衣服是 do the washing。
do-the-washing-up.example: You cooked, so I'll do the washing-up.
do-the-washing-up.en: I usually do the washing-up on Sundays.

w-fold.note: 叠衣服：fold the washing；反义 unfold。
w-fold.en: When you were ten, you used to fold your socks and line up your pencils by colour.
w-fold.szh: 你十岁那会儿，袜子都叠得整整齐齐，铅笔还按颜色排好。

w-unmade.note: un- 表示「没」：made 是铺好的，unmade 是乱着的。
w-unmade.en: Nurses hardly ever leave a bed unmade.

drive-sb-mad.zh: 快把某人逼疯；让人受不了
drive-sb-mad.tip: 英式口语；mad 在这里是「疯」不是「生气」。也说 drive sb crazy。
drive-sb-mad.example: The noise from the building site is driving me mad.
drive-sb-mad.en: Look, the mugs drive me mad, but I'm not trying to change your whole life.
drive-sb-mad.szh: 听着，那些杯子快把我逼疯了，但我也没想改造你整个人生。

w-standards.note: 常用复数：have high standards（要求高）。
w-standards.en: To be honest, my standards went down a bit when I moved in with Tom.
w-standards.szh: 说实话，跟 Tom 合租以后，我的标准是降了点。

put-sth-away.note: to put something back in the place where it is usually kept
put-sth-away.tip: 代词放中间：put it away，不说 put away it；put 的三种形式都是 put。
put-sth-away.example: Can you put the shopping away while I make tea?
put-sth-away.en: And here's the rule: everything gets put away before bed.
put-sth-away.szh: 规矩是：睡觉前所有东西都得收好。

more.en: You even put your mugs away now.
more.szh: 你现在连杯子都会收好了。

more.en: And we'd get more done if you put your phone away.
more.szh: 还有，你把手机收起来，咱们效率能高点。

more.en: On Sunday, Priya came round and told us to put our phones away.
more.szh: 周日 Priya 过来了，让我俩先把手机收起来。

clear-out.zh: 清理（把不要的东西清出去）
clear-out.note: to make a place tidy by removing things you do not want
clear-out.tip: 比 tidy up 动静大：tidy up 是收拾整齐，clear out 是把东西搬出来、扔掉一批。
clear-out.example: We cleared out the garage and found three old bikes.
clear-out.en: On Saturday, we're clearing out the hall cupboard together, because I can't even open it.
clear-out.szh: 周六咱俩一起把门厅那个柜子清一清，我连柜门都打不开。

w-racket.note: 网球、羽毛球拍用 racket；乒乓球拍是 bat。
w-racket.en: An umbrella, a tennis racket, two old trainers and about forty plastic bags have just fallen on my head!
w-racket.szh: 一把伞、一个网球拍、两只旧球鞋，还有差不多四十个塑料袋，全砸我头上了！

w-caller.note: 电台、电视的热线节目里打电话进来的人；打进节目说 call in / ring in。
w-caller.en: You're listening to Dear Helen, and our first caller is Matt from Bristol.
w-caller.szh: 这里是《亲爱的 Helen》，第一位打进电话的是布里斯托尔的 Matt。

w-insurance.note: 买保险是 take out insurance；重音在第二个音节 in-SUR-ance。
w-insurance.en: Well, I'm thirty-four, and I work in an insurance office.
w-insurance.szh: 是这样，我今年三十四，在一家保险公司上班。

more.en: She added up insurance, road tax, parking and petrol, and it came to £2,400 a year.
more.szh: 她把保险、路税、停车费和油钱加起来，一年要 2400 英镑。

kill-time.note: to do something unimportant while you are waiting or have nothing to do
kill-time.tip: 常带「没什么意义」的意思；花时间做正经事用 spend time doing。
kill-time.example: We killed time in a café until the train came.
kill-time.en: Even when I'm out of the office on holiday, I just kill time on my phone.
kill-time.szh: 就连休假不用上班的时候，我也就是拿着手机打发时间。

more.en: One rainy morning, I was killing time at the bus stop when I felt cold water in my sock.
more.szh: 一个下雨的早上，我在公交站干等着，忽然觉得袜子里进了冷水。

more.en: For two weeks he'd been practising in the bike shed at lunchtime, while his friends killed time playing cards.
more.szh: 那两个星期，他每天中午都躲在车棚里练，朋友们就在一旁打牌打发时间。

be-stuck-in-a-rut.zh: 陷入一成不变的日子；困在老套路里
be-stuck-in-a-rut.note: to be in a boring situation where you do the same things every day and nothing changes
be-stuck-in-a-rut.tip: rut 原指车轮压出来的沟，车陷进去就出不来；也说 get stuck in a rut。
be-stuck-in-a-rut.example: After ten years in the same job, she felt stuck in a rut.
be-stuck-in-a-rut.en: You're stuck in a rut, and that's a different thing.
be-stuck-in-a-rut.szh: 你只是陷进一成不变的日子里了，这是两码事。

no-wonder.note: used to say that something is not surprising
no-wonder.tip: 后面直接接句子；单独说也行：No wonder!（怪不得！）
no-wonder.example: You didn't eat lunch? No wonder you're hungry.
no-wonder.en: No wonder the evenings feel long — they're all the same evening.
no-wonder.szh: 难怪晚上显得那么长——每个晚上都是同一个晚上。

more.en: No wonder he looked so tired at his talk.
more.szh: 难怪他讲座那天看着那么累。

w-boredom.note: bored（人觉得无聊）的名词；boring 是「事情让人无聊」。
w-boredom.en: Believe me, I know all about boredom.
w-boredom.szh: 相信我，无聊是什么滋味，我太清楚了。

get-out-of-the-house.zh: 出门走走；别老待在家里
get-out-of-the-house.note: to go out, especially when you have been at home for too long
get-out-of-the-house.tip: 重点不是去哪儿，而是「离开家」；比 go out 更强调在家闷太久了。
get-out-of-the-house.example: I work from home, so I go to the gym just to get out of the house.
get-out-of-the-house.en: First, get out of the house twice a week, even if it's only to the library.
get-out-of-the-house.szh: 第一，每周出门两次，哪怕只是去趟图书馆。

take-up-sth.note: to start doing a new activity, especially for fun
take-up-sth.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：take up yoga、take up painting；不接 to do。
take-up-sth.example: My dad took up running when he was sixty.
take-up-sth.en: Second, take up something you'll probably be bad at.
take-up-sth.szh: 第二，学一样你多半学不好的东西。

more.en: And a few have even taken up mending as a hobby.
more.szh: 还有少数人干脆把缝缝补补当成了爱好。

w-pottery.note: 做陶艺的课叫 a pottery class。
w-pottery.en: Pottery and salsa are both on the menu at your local college.
w-pottery.szh: 你们那儿的成人学院就开着陶艺课和萨尔萨舞课。

w-salsa.note: 拉丁舞的一种；也是一种番茄辣酱。
w-salsa.en: Pottery and salsa are both on the menu at your local college.
w-salsa.szh: 你们那儿的成人学院就开着陶艺课和萨尔萨舞课。

have-time-on-your-hands.zh: 闲着没事；有大把空闲时间
have-time-on-your-hands.note: to have a lot of free time and not much to do
have-time-on-your-hands.tip: your 要跟着主语换：I have time on my hands / she has time on her hands。
have-time-on-your-hands.example: Now that the kids have left home, I have more time on my hands.
have-time-on-your-hands.en: I've had a lot of time on my hands, so thanks.
have-time-on-your-hands.szh: 我闲了一晚上，所以真得谢谢你。

more.en: And reading, when she has time on her hands.
more.szh: 还有看书，前提是她闲下来。

more.en: Tom says I've got too much time on my hands at weekends anyway.
more.szh: 反正 Tom 说我周末闲得发慌。

w-portion.note: 英国的 five a day 指每天五份蔬果，一份大约 80 克，比如一个苹果。
w-portion.en: Here's a question for you: how many portions of fruit and veg did you eat yesterday?
w-portion.szh: 先问大家一个问题：你昨天吃了几份水果蔬菜？

fall-short-of-sth.zh: 没达到（目标、要求）；差一截
fall-short-of-sth.note: to fail to reach a target or the amount you need
fall-short-of-sth.tip: 中间可以加 well、just 说差多少：fall just short（差一点）。fall 的过去式 fell，过去分词 fallen。
fall-short-of-sth.example: Sales fell short of what we expected this year.
fall-short-of-sth.en: The typical adult manages 3.7, and lots of people fall well short of the target.
fall-short-of-sth.szh: 普通成年人每天吃 3.7 份，很多人离这个目标还差得远。

a-balanced-diet.note: a way of eating that includes the right amounts of different kinds of food
a-balanced-diet.tip: diet 在这里是「日常饮食」，不一定是减肥；「在节食」才是 be on a diet。
a-balanced-diet.example: A balanced diet doesn't mean you can never eat chocolate.
a-balanced-diet.en: She says people do know what a balanced diet looks like.
a-balanced-diet.szh: 她说，大家其实知道均衡饮食是什么样的。

more.en: After a twelve-hour shift, a hot shower is part of a balanced diet.
more.szh: 干完十二个小时的班，洗个热水澡就是均衡饮食的一部分。

be-high-in-sth.note: to contain a lot of something, such as sugar, fat or salt
be-high-in-sth.tip: 反义是 be low in sth；介词用 in，不用 of。
be-high-in-sth.example: These crisps are very high in salt.
be-high-in-sth.en: "On top of that, a lot of the snacks we reach for at work are high in sugar."
be-high-in-sth.szh: 「再加上，我们上班时随手拿的零食，很多含糖量都很高。」

more.en: "Most cheap new clothes are high in plastic, and they don't last as long as wool or cotton," she said.
more.szh: 「便宜的新衣服大多塑料成分很高，没有羊毛、棉的经穿，」她说。

more.en: Mind you, it was very high in salt.
more.szh: 不过话说回来，咸得要命。

w-pear.en: Every Monday, he puts a big bowl of apples, pears and bananas next to the kettle.
w-pear.szh: 每周一，他都在烧水壶旁边摆上一大碗苹果、梨和香蕉。

snack-on-sth.note: to eat small amounts of a particular food between meals
snack-on-sth.tip: snack 可以当动词；不说 eat snack on。
snack-on-sth.example: I try to snack on nuts instead of crisps.
snack-on-sth.en: "Before, we'd snack on biscuits all afternoon," he says.
snack-on-sth.szh: 「以前我们一下午都在吃饼干，」他说。

more.en: She snacks on biscuits all through her night shifts.
more.szh: 她上夜班的时候，饼干一直没离过嘴。

more.en: And you'd better not snack on those biscuits with clay on your fingers.
more.szh: 还有，手上沾着泥，可别去拿那些饼干吃。

go-a-long-way.note: to be very helpful in improving a situation
go-a-long-way.tip: 也说钱「很经花」：Ten pounds goes a long way here。别按字面理解成「走很远」。
go-a-long-way.example: A quick thank-you email goes a long way.
go-a-long-way.en: Dr Webster says small changes like this go a long way.
go-a-long-way.szh: Webster 博士说，这样的小改变作用很大。

w-superfood.zh: 超级食物（据说特别有营养的食物）
w-superfood.note: 广告里常见，比如牛油果、奇亚籽，带点营销味。
w-superfood.en: "People go on about expensive superfoods, but frozen peas are just as good for you," she says.
w-superfood.szh: 「大家老念叨那些贵得要命的超级食物，其实冷冻豌豆对身体一样好，」她说。

w-peas.note: 单数 pea；英国人家里冰箱几乎都有一袋冻豌豆。
w-peas.en: "People go on about expensive superfoods, but frozen peas are just as good for you," she says.
w-peas.szh: 「大家老念叨那些贵得要命的超级食物，其实冷冻豌豆对身体一样好，」她说。

be-good-for-you.note: to be healthy for you to eat or do
be-good-for-you.tip: 对身体不好是 be bad for you；注意介词 for，不说 good to you（那是「对你好、待你好」）。
be-good-for-you.example: Walking to work is good for you and saves money.
be-good-for-you.en: "People go on about expensive superfoods, but frozen peas are just as good for you," she says.
be-good-for-you.szh: 「大家老念叨那些贵得要命的超级食物，其实冷冻豌豆对身体一样好，」她说。

w-ketchup.note: 英国人也常说 tomato sauce。

work-out.note: to do exercise to make your body stronger and fitter
work-out.tip: 名词连写：a workout（一次锻炼）。work out 还有「算出来、想明白」的意思，看上下文。
work-out.example: She works out three times a week before work.
work-out.en: I'm just not used to telling you every time I work out.
work-out.szh: 我只是不习惯每次健身都跟你报备。

more.en: Ella worked out that her whole winter outfit cost less than one new pair of jeans.
more.szh: Ella 算了算，她一整套冬装加起来，比一条新牛仔裤还便宜。

more.en: I'd love to come on 19 December, but I've worked out the flight would cost more than two months' rent.
more.szh: 我很想 12 月 19 号回去，可我算了一下，机票比我两个月的房租还贵。

w-session.note: 健身房按次收费说 per session / a session。
w-session.en: According to your calendar, you had a session with Dan at seven on Tuesday.
w-session.szh: 你日历上写着，周二七点你跟 Dan 有节课。

w-squats.note: 单数 squat；做深蹲是 do squats。
w-squats.en: And you were in a very good mood for someone who'd just done fifty squats.
w-squats.szh: 一个刚做完五十个深蹲的人，心情未免也太好了。

make-an-excuse.note: to give a reason for something you did or did not do, which is often not the true reason
make-an-excuse.tip: 动词用 make，不用 find；为什么事找借口用 for：make excuses for being late。
make-an-excuse.example: He always makes an excuse when it's his turn to cook.

more.en: Before you two start making excuses, let me look into the meter readings.
more.szh: 你俩先别急着找借口，我来查查电表读数。

more.en: So I make an excuse, usually something about my chain, then get off and walk.
more.szh: 于是我就找个借口，一般是说链条有点毛病，然后下车推着走。

be-out-of-shape.note: to not be fit because you have not exercised enough
be-out-of-shape.tip: 说人，指体能差，不一定是胖；反义是 be in (good) shape。
be-out-of-shape.example: I was so out of shape that I couldn't run for the bus.

own-up.note: to admit that you did something wrong
own-up.tip: 承认什么用 to + 名词 / doing：own up to breaking it。比 admit 口语。
own-up.example: Nobody owned up to eating the last piece of cake.

w-skip.note: skip breakfast（不吃早饭）、skip a class（翘课）；过去式双写 p。
w-skip.en: I skipped both sessions and watched two hours of cooking videos instead.
w-skip.szh: 两节课我都翘了，在家看了两个小时的做饭视频。

get-back-into-sth.zh: 重新开始（做一件停了一阵的事）
get-back-into-sth.note: to start doing an activity again after a break
get-back-into-sth.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：get back into yoga / get back into reading。
get-back-into-sth.example: After the baby was born, it took me a year to get back into running.
get-back-into-sth.en: I'll get back into it slowly.

more.en: Since January, I've even got back into writing shopping lists on paper.
more.szh: 从一月起，我甚至又开始在纸上写购物清单了。

talk-sb-into-sth.note: to persuade someone to do something
talk-sb-into-sth.tip: 后面接名词或 doing；反过来「劝某人别做」是 talk sb out of doing。
talk-sb-into-sth.example: My friends talked me into joining the choir.
talk-sb-into-sth.en: And you can talk me into staying for the whole hour.
talk-sb-into-sth.szh: 到时候你负责劝我把一整个小时练完。

w-guest-pass.note: 会员可以带朋友进去一次的通行证。
w-guest-pass.en: I used your guest pass and introduced myself to Dan.
w-guest-pass.szh: 我用了你的访客卡，还跟 Dan 做了自我介绍。

w-marketing.note: 说在哪个行业工作用 work in：work in IT / work in marketing。
w-marketing.en: Nadia's twenty-nine, she works in marketing, and she drinks four cups a day.
w-marketing.szh: Nadia 二十九岁，做市场营销，一天喝四杯咖啡。

w-version.note: the short version 是「简短的说法」；软件的新版本是 the new version。
w-version.en: It's a long story, but here's the short version.
w-version.szh: 说来话长，我给你讲个简短版。

more.en: He set up our first test version in a weekend, and Arjun built the server from Bangalore.
more.szh: 他一个周末就搭好了第一个测试版，Arjun 在班加罗尔把服务器做了出来。

w-caffeine.note: 读 /ˈkæfiːn/，不可数。茶、可乐、巧克力里也有。
w-caffeine.en: Caffeine usually kicks in about twenty minutes after your first cup.
w-caffeine.szh: 第一杯咖啡下肚，大概二十分钟，咖啡因就开始起作用了。

kick-in.note: to start to have an effect
kick-in.tip: 常说药、咖啡、新规定等开始起效；不用被动。
kick-in.example: Take the medicine now — it takes about an hour to kick in.
kick-in.en: Caffeine usually kicks in about twenty minutes after your first cup.
kick-in.szh: 第一杯咖啡下肚，大概二十分钟，咖啡因就开始起作用了。

more.en: My room's like a fridge until the heating kicks in at six.
more.szh: 暖气六点才热起来，在那之前我房间跟冰箱似的。

more.en: As soon as I see it, the fear kicks in.
more.szh: 我一看到它，心里就开始发怵。

wear-off.note: to gradually stop having an effect
wear-off.tip: 和 kick in 正好相反；wear 的过去式 wore，过去分词 worn。
wear-off.example: The excitement wore off after the first week.
wear-off.en: The problem is, it takes five or six hours for just half of it to wear off.
wear-off.szh: 问题是，光是让一半的咖啡因消退，就得五六个小时。

more.en: And the excitement wears off so quickly that sometimes I forget what I've ordered.
more.szh: 而且那股兴奋劲儿过得飞快，有时候我连自己下单买了什么都忘了。

more.en: I couldn't stand the long meetings, and the excitement of every new case wore off by Wednesday.
more.szh: 我受不了那些没完没了的会，每接一个新案子，那股新鲜劲儿到星期三就没了。

keep-sb-awake.note: to stop someone from falling asleep
keep-sb-awake.tip: keep + 人 + 形容词，说让人保持某种状态：keep sb warm / keep sb busy。
keep-sb-awake.example: The noise from the party kept us awake all night.
keep-sb-awake.en: So a flat white at four is still keeping you awake at midnight.
keep-sb-awake.szh: 所以下午四点那杯馥芮白，到半夜还在让你睡不着。

more.en: "It kept me awake until three."
more.szh: 「一直到凌晨三点都没合眼。」

w-researcher.note: research（研究）加 -er；research 不可数，不说 a research。
w-researcher.en: Sleep researchers have been studying this for years, and one survey after another shows the same pattern.
w-researcher.szh: 睡眠研究人员研究这个问题已经很多年了，一次次调查都显示出同一个规律。

more.en: Sleep researchers say some people are becoming obsessed with their scores.
more.szh: 睡眠研究者说，有些人正变得对分数着了魔。

w-pattern.note: 也指图案：a shirt with a flower pattern。
w-pattern.en: Sleep researchers have been studying this for years, and one survey after another shows the same pattern.
w-pattern.szh: 睡眠研究人员研究这个问题已经很多年了，一次次调查都显示出同一个规律。

rely-on-sth.note: to need something or someone in order to do something
rely-on-sth.tip: 介词固定用 on；后面也可以接人：You can rely on me（你可以指望我）。
rely-on-sth.example: Many small shops rely on tourists in the summer.
rely-on-sth.en: Lots of people rely on coffee to get through the afternoon.
rely-on-sth.szh: 很多人下午全靠咖啡撑着。

get-a-good-night-s-sleep.note: to sleep well for the whole night
get-a-good-night-s-sleep.tip: night's 带撇号 s，表示「一晚的」；动词也可以用 have。
get-a-good-night-s-sleep.example: Try to get a good night's sleep before the interview.
get-a-good-night-s-sleep.en: And those people find it harder to get a good night's sleep.
get-a-good-night-s-sleep.szh: 而这些人晚上更难睡个好觉。

build-up.note: to slowly increase in amount or strength
build-up.tip: 也能带宾语：build up your strength（慢慢增强体力）；build 的过去式是 built。
build-up.example: If you don't reply to emails, they just build up.
build-up.en: The next morning they're tired, so they drink more, and the habit slowly builds up.
build-up.szh: 第二天早上一累，就喝得更多，这个习惯就这么一点点加重了。

w-cut-off.note: 动词词组是 cut off（切断）；名词带连字符。
w-cut-off.en: So, most experts say you should have a coffee cut-off at two o'clock.
w-cut-off.szh: 所以，大多数专家建议，下午两点以后就别再喝咖啡了。

w-latte.note: 来自意大利语，读 /ˈlɑːteɪ/ 或 /ˈlæteɪ/。
w-latte.en: Oh, and if you've been listening to this at eleven at night with a latte in your hand...
w-latte.szh: 对了，要是你正在晚上十一点、手里端着一杯拿铁听这期节目……

can-t-stand-sth.note: to dislike someone or something very much
can-t-stand-sth.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：can't stand waiting。过去用 couldn't stand；这里的 stand 是「忍受」，不是「站」。
can-t-stand-sth.example: I can't stand people who talk during films.
can-t-stand-sth.en: When Chen was a boy, he couldn't stand bitter melon.
can-t-stand-sth.szh: 小陈小时候，最受不了的就是苦瓜。

more.en: But I can't stand being told what to do by a clock.
more.szh: 可我就是受不了被一个钟指挥来指挥去。

more.en: I couldn't stand the long meetings, and the excitement of every new case wore off by Wednesday.
more.szh: 我受不了那些没完没了的会，每接一个新案子，那股新鲜劲儿到星期三就没了。

pull-a-face.zh: （因为不喜欢）皱起脸；露出嫌弃的表情
pull-a-face.note: to make an expression with your face to show that you do not like something
pull-a-face.tip: 这里是嫌弃、不情愿的表情，不是逗人笑的「做鬼脸」（那个常说 pull funny faces）。英式说法，美式多说 make a face；冲某人做是 pull a face at sb。
pull-a-face.example: My son pulled a face when he saw the broccoli.
pull-a-face.en: Every time, he'd pull a face as if she'd given him medicine.
pull-a-face.szh: 每回他都一脸嫌弃，好像奶奶喂他吃的是药。

more.en: Her boyfriend, Tom, pulls a face whenever she brings stamps to the dinner table.
more.szh: 她男朋友 Tom 一看到她把邮票带上饭桌，就一脸嫌弃。

more.en: I can see some of you pulling a face.
more.szh: 我看到有些人在皱眉头了。

w-squeeze.en: When he was eight, she showed him how to cook it himself: first salt it, then squeeze it.
w-squeeze.szh: 他八岁那年，奶奶教他自己做：先用盐腌，再把水挤掉。

w-bitter.note: bitter melon 就是苦瓜；也可以说人「心里不服、怨恨」：feel bitter about sth。
w-bitter.en: "Kids tend to hate bitter food," Lily said when he told her the story.
w-bitter.szh: 他跟 Lily 讲起这事，Lily 说：「小孩一般都讨厌苦的东西。」

an-acquired-taste.zh: （要慢慢才会喜欢的）独特口味
an-acquired-taste.note: something that you do not like at first but start to like after you try it more
an-acquired-taste.tip: 常说食物、饮料，也可以说音乐、人：His humour is an acquired taste。
an-acquired-taste.example: Strong black tea is an acquired taste.
an-acquired-taste.en: "It's an acquired taste, like coffee or beer."
an-acquired-taste.szh: 「这种味道得慢慢才吃得惯，跟咖啡、啤酒一样。」

w-slice.note: 一片面包是 a slice of bread；也能当动词「切片」。
w-slice.en: He left the slices in salt for twenty minutes, and in the meantime, he beat the eggs.
w-slice.szh: 苦瓜片用盐腌二十分钟，趁这工夫，他把鸡蛋打散。

w-beat.en: He left the slices in salt for twenty minutes, and in the meantime, he beat the eggs.
w-beat.szh: 苦瓜片用盐腌二十分钟，趁这工夫，他把鸡蛋打散。

clear-your-plate.note: to eat all the food on your plate
clear-your-plate.tip: your 要跟着主语换：he cleared his plate。clear the table 是「收拾餐桌」。
clear-your-plate.example: The kids cleared their plates in five minutes.
clear-your-plate.en: He cleared his plate, which his grandma would never believe.
clear-your-plate.szh: 他把盘子吃得干干净净——奶奶要是知道了，肯定不信。

grow-on-sb.note: if something grows on you, you start to like it more and more
grow-on-sb.tip: 主语是东西，宾语是人：It grew on me，不说 I grew on it。grow 的过去式 grew，过去分词 grown。
grow-on-sb.example: I didn't like the song at first, but it's grown on me.
grow-on-sb.en: He made it again on Thursday, and again on Sunday, and slowly it grew on him.
grow-on-sb.szh: 周四他又做了一次，周日又做了一次，慢慢地，他还真喜欢上这个味道了。

more.en: At first, I thought it was a bit boring, but it grew on me.
more.szh: 一开始我觉得它有点单调，可越看越顺眼。

take-a-bite.note: to put some food in your mouth and bite off a piece
take-a-bite.tip: 咬哪个用 of：take a bite of sth。喝一口是 take a sip。
take-a-bite.example: Can I take a bite of your sandwich?
take-a-bite.en: On Sunday, Chen made him take a bite.
take-a-bite.szh: 周日，小陈让他尝了一口。

w-chew.en: Tom chewed for a long time while Chen and Lily watched.
w-chew.szh: Tom 嚼了好半天，小陈和 Lily 就在旁边盯着。

w-cucumber.note: as cool as a cucumber 是「非常冷静」。
w-cucumber.en: "It tastes like a cucumber that's angry with you," he said at last.
w-cucumber.szh: 「吃起来像一根在生你气的黄瓜，」他终于开口了。

w-surgical.note: ward 是病房、病区；外科病房 surgical ward，儿科病房 children's ward。
w-surgical.en: I've been on a surgical ward in east London for three weeks now, so here's my first update.
w-surgical.szh: 我在伦敦东区一家医院的外科病房已经待了三个星期，先跟大家汇报一下。

be-short-staffed.tip: 常说医院、餐厅、商店；同义说法 be understaffed。
be-short-staffed.example: We're short-staffed this week because two people are ill.
be-short-staffed.en: So, the ward's often short-staffed and everyone's under pressure, just like at home.
be-short-staffed.szh: 病房经常缺人手，大家压力都很大，这点跟国内一样。

more.en: Six years ago, a charity shop near her flat was short-staffed.
more.szh: 六年前，她家附近一家慈善商店人手不够。

more.en: The school was short-staffed, so we had him for three years.
more.szh: 学校缺老师，所以他教了我们整整三年。

be-under-pressure.note: to feel worried because you have too much to do or people expect a lot from you
be-under-pressure.tip: 被谁逼着做某事：be under pressure to do sth；介词固定用 under。
be-under-pressure.example: I work better when I'm not under pressure.
be-under-pressure.en: So, the ward's often short-staffed and everyone's under pressure, just like at home.
be-under-pressure.szh: 病房经常缺人手，大家压力都很大，这点跟国内一样。

w-surgery.note: 说「做手术」常用 have surgery，不加 a；英式里 surgery 还指诊所。
w-surgery.en: Here, the nurses make patients get out of bed on the first day after surgery.
w-surgery.szh: 在这儿，护士会让病人手术后第一天就下床。

fill-in-a-form.note: to write the information that is asked for on a form
fill-in-a-form.tip: 英式多说 fill in，美式多说 fill out；代词放中间：fill it in。
fill-in-a-form.example: Please fill in this form and bring it to reception.
fill-in-a-form.en: And you have to fill in a form for almost everything.
fill-in-a-form.szh: 还有，几乎干什么都得填表。

more.en: Each time, I filled in the delivery form.
more.szh: 每次我都把收货信息填好了。

more.en: I'd even filled in a form to get it into today's kiln.
more.szh: 我还专门填了表，好赶上今天这一窑。
