w-senior.note: 反义 junior；senior citizens 是老年人。
w-senior.en: A senior nurse called Grace has been helping me find my feet.
w-senior.szh: 有位叫 Grace 的资深护士一直在帮我适应。

find-your-feet.zh: （在新环境里）站稳脚跟；适应过来
find-your-feet.note: to become confident in a new place or job
find-your-feet.tip: your 要跟着主语换：find my feet / find her feet；find 的过去式 found。
find-your-feet.example: It took me a few months to find my feet in London.
find-your-feet.en: A senior nurse called Grace has been helping me find my feet.
find-your-feet.szh: 有位叫 Grace 的资深护士一直在帮我适应。

take-sth-seriously.note: to think that something is important and give it attention
take-sth-seriously.tip: 东西放中间：take it seriously；反过来「别太当真」是 Don't take it too seriously。
take-sth-seriously.example: He doesn't take his health seriously.
take-sth-seriously.en: Handover takes thirty minutes, and people take their breaks seriously.
take-sth-seriously.szh: 交接班要半个小时，大家也很把休息当回事。

more.en: Please take this seriously, because a quick reply would make a difference.
more.szh: 请认真对待这件事，能尽快回复我就帮大忙了。

work-nights.note: to work during the night instead of the day
work-nights.tip: nights 不加介词也不加冠词；也说 be on nights / work night shifts。
work-nights.example: My dad worked nights for twenty years.
work-nights.en: The hardest part is working nights in English.
work-nights.szh: 最难的是用英语上夜班。

w-rota.note: 英式说法，美式多说 schedule。
w-rota.en: Anyway, I'd be grateful if someone could send me the new rota for June.
w-rota.szh: 好了，要是谁能把六月的新排班表发我一份，我就太感谢了。

w-wet.note: 说天气时 a wet day 就是下雨天，英国人很常用。
w-wet.en: Evening, everyone, and thanks for coming out on a wet Wednesday.
w-wet.szh: 大家晚上好，谢谢各位在这么个下雨的周三出门过来。

more.en: On the third one, I'd forgotten to wet my hands.
more.szh: 第三个，我忘了先把手沾湿。

w-familiar.note: a familiar face 是「熟面孔」；be familiar with sth 是「对…熟悉」。
w-familiar.en: I can see some familiar faces.

go-for-a-run.note: to go out and run, usually for exercise
go-for-a-run.tip: 同样的说法：go for a walk / a swim / a drink；不说 go to a run。
go-for-a-run.example: I go for a run before work when it's not raining.
go-for-a-run.en: They go for a run twice a week, and after three weeks the shoes are back in the box.
go-for-a-run.szh: 每周跑两次步，三个星期后，鞋又回盒子里去了。

a-waste-of-money.note: something that is not worth the money you pay for it
a-waste-of-money.tip: 同样可以说 a waste of time（第 35 课）；加强语气用 a complete / total waste of money。
a-waste-of-money.example: The extra warranty was a complete waste of money.
a-waste-of-money.en: That's a waste of money, and I've seen it a hundred times.
a-waste-of-money.szh: 这就是白花钱，这种事我见过上百回了。

more.en: Looking back, both the toaster and the coffee machine were a waste of money.
more.szh: 现在回头看，烤面包机和咖啡机都是白花钱。

warm-up.note: to do gentle exercises to get ready for sport
warm-up.tip: 名词连写：a warm-up；运动后放松是 cool down。
warm-up.example: Always warm up before you play football.
warm-up.en: You ought to warm up for five minutes first, even if you feel silly walking fast round the park.
warm-up.szh: 跑之前应该先热身五分钟，哪怕绕着公园快走会觉得自己有点傻。

w-replace.note: need replacing = need to be replaced，需要被换。
w-replace.en: Shoes only need replacing after about five hundred miles, not after one bad run.
w-replace.szh: 鞋大概跑满五百英里才需要换，而不是跑砸一次就换。

w-mile.note: 英国路牌和跑步距离常用英里。
w-mile.en: Shoes only need replacing after about five hundred miles, not after one bad run.
w-mile.szh: 鞋大概跑满五百英里才需要换，而不是跑砸一次就换。

get-your-money-s-worth.note: to get enough use or value from something you paid for
get-your-money-s-worth.tip: your 要跟着主语换：we got our money's worth；money's 带撇号 s。
get-your-money-s-worth.example: We stayed until the end to get our money's worth.
get-your-money-s-worth.en: Until then, you're still getting your money's worth.
get-your-money-s-worth.szh: 在那之前，这双鞋你都还没穿够本。

more.en: For £240, I wanted to be sure I'd get my money's worth.
more.szh: 花 240 英镑，我得确保这钱花得值。

more.en: And you still got your money's worth — it was a useful experiment.
more.szh: 而且你这钱也没白花——就当做了个有用的实验。

break-sth-in.note: to wear new shoes for short periods until they become comfortable
break-sth-in.tip: 代词放中间：break them in；break 的过去式 broke，过去分词 broken。
break-sth-in.example: Break your new boots in before the walking holiday.
break-sth-in.en: New ones need a few short runs to break them in.
break-sth-in.szh: 新鞋得先短跑几次，才能穿合脚。

more.en: My flatmate suggested wearing it for a week to break it in.
more.szh: 室友建议我先穿一个星期，把它穿服帖了。

more.en: "It's like breaking in new shoes," she said.
more.szh: 「就像穿新鞋，」她说。

pay-off.note: to bring good results after a lot of effort
pay-off.tip: 过去式写 paid，不写 payed；pay off a loan 是「还清贷款」。
pay-off.example: All those hours of practice finally paid off.
pay-off.en: What pays off isn't the shoes, it's turning up.
pay-off.szh: 真正有回报的不是鞋，而是每次都到场。

w-light.note: 英国夏天晚上九点多天还亮，the light evenings 指这段傍晚天长的日子；反义 dark evenings。
w-light.en: Make the most of the light evenings.
w-light.szh: 趁着傍晚天还亮，多出去跑跑。

w-worn.note: wear 的过去分词：wear–wore–worn；worn out 是穿破了。
w-worn.en: Oh, and if anyone wants a pair of size 10s, bright orange, worn once, see me after.
w-worn.szh: 对了，谁想要一双十码的鞋，亮橙色，只穿过一次——会后来找我。

w-fridge.note: refrigerator 的口语说法；冰箱贴是 fridge magnet。
w-fridge.en: Right, we stuck these lists on the fridge exactly thirty days ago.
w-fridge.szh: 好，这两张清单是咱们整整三十天前贴到冰箱上的。

keep-track-of-sth.note: to make sure you know what is happening or how much of something there is, often by writing it down
keep-track-of-sth.tip: 反义是 lose track of sth（第 31 课的 lose track of time）。keep 的过去式 kept。
keep-track-of-sth.example: I use an app to keep track of my spending.
keep-track-of-sth.en: You're the one who keeps track of everything in a notebook.
keep-track-of-sth.szh: 什么事都记在本子上的人是你。

w-notebook.note: 英式里不指笔记本电脑，那是 laptop。
w-notebook.en: You're the one who keeps track of everything in a notebook.
w-notebook.szh: 什么事都记在本子上的人是你。

stick-to-sth.note: to keep doing what you planned or promised, even when it is difficult
stick-to-sth.tip: stick 的过去式和过去分词都是 stuck；后面接名词：stick to a plan / a budget。
stick-to-sth.example: It's hard to stick to a diet when you eat out a lot.
stick-to-sth.en: I've stuck to my ten thousand steps every other day.
stick-to-sth.szh: 隔一天走一万步，我一直坚持着。

more.en: Normally, I stick to shops where I can try things on first.
more.szh: 我平时只在能先试穿的店里买衣服。

more.en: Now I stick to a simple plan: two hours every morning, after my shift and before bed."
more.szh: 现在我就守着一个简单的计划：每天早上学两个小时，下了夜班、睡觉之前。」

w-kilometre.note: 英式拼写，美式写 kilometer；英国人说距离其实更常用 mile。
w-kilometre.en: On average, I've walked six kilometres a day.
w-kilometre.szh: 平均下来，我每天走了六公里。

get-into-the-habit-of-doing.text: get into the habit of doing
get-into-the-habit-of-doing.note: to start doing something regularly so that it becomes a habit
get-into-the-habit-of-doing.tip: of 后面接 doing，不接 to do；英式过去分词 got，美式常用 gotten。
get-into-the-habit-of-doing.example: I've got into the habit of checking my phone first thing in the morning.
get-into-the-habit-of-doing.en: And I've got into the habit of cooking on Sundays.
get-into-the-habit-of-doing.szh: 还养成了周日做饭的习惯。

more.en: I got into the habit of checking the library first.
more.szh: 我养成了想要什么先去图书馆看看的习惯。

more.en: Get into the habit of saving a little every month.
more.szh: 养成每个月存一点钱的习惯。

w-sign-up.note: 报名参加什么用 for：sign up for a class。
w-sign-up.en: Oh, and Dan's Monday class is fully booked now, because I made half the hospital sign up.
w-sign-up.szh: 对了，Dan 周一那节课现在都约满了，因为我把半个医院的人都拉去报名了。

w-reach.note: reach for sth 是伸手去拿；reach 也有「到达」的意思：reach London。
w-reach.en: I'd lie in bed staring at the ceiling, and I kept reaching for my phone.
w-reach.szh: 我躺在床上盯着天花板，手老是往手机那儿伸。

slip-back-into-sth.note: to start doing something bad again, often without meaning to
slip-back-into-sth.tip: slip 是「滑」，过去式双写 p：slipped；后面接名词或 doing。
slip-back-into-sth.example: After the holiday, it's easy to slip back into old habits.
slip-back-into-sth.en: But I haven't slipped back into skipping the gym.
slip-back-into-sth.szh: 不过健身房我没再翘过。

so-far-so-good.note: used to say that things have gone well until now
so-far-so-good.tip: 带一点「还没结束，后面不好说」的意思；常单独成句。
so-far-so-good.example: "How's the new job?" "So far so good."

break-a-habit.note: to stop doing something that you have done regularly for a long time
break-a-habit.tip: 冠词可以换：break the habit / break that habit；反义是 get into the habit of doing。
break-a-habit.example: It took him two years to break the habit of biting his nails.
break-a-habit.en: Breaking that habit is the best thing I've done all year.
break-a-habit.szh: 改掉这个习惯，是我今年做过的最好的一件事。

more.en: Tom said it would help him break the habit of taking the bus for two stops.
more.szh: Tom 说，这能帮他改掉就两站路也要坐公交的毛病。

w-password.note: 改密码是 change a password；忘了密码是 forget your password。
w-password.en: Every night for a month, I've been changing the Wi-Fi password at a quarter to eleven.
w-password.szh: 这一个月，我每天晚上十点四十五都会改一次 Wi-Fi 密码。

more.en: He even signed in to every app for them, so as not to get calls about lost passwords.
more.szh: 他还替爸妈把每个 App 都登录好了，免得以后老接到「密码找不到了」的电话。

treat-yourself.zh: 犒劳自己；给自己买点好的
treat-yourself.note: to buy or do something special for yourself that you enjoy
treat-yourself.tip: yourself 要跟着主语变：I treat myself、she treats herself；犒劳的东西用 to：treat yourself to a new bag。
treat-yourself.example: I finished the project early, so I treated myself to a long lunch.
treat-yourself.en: So, back in March, I decided to treat myself.
treat-yourself.szh: 三月那会儿，我决定犒劳一下自己。

more.en: My friends said, "Go on, treat yourself, it's Christmas."
more.szh: 朋友们都说：「去吧，犒劳一下自己，过圣诞呢。」

more.en: But treat yourself to a second bowl of noodles sometimes — the ones in England aren't that good.
more.szh: 不过偶尔也犒劳一下自己，多吃一碗面——英国的面可没那么好吃。

try-sth-on.note: to put on clothes or shoes to see if they fit or look good
try-sth-on.tip: 宾语是名词时可放中间也可放后面：try the jacket on / try on the jacket；是代词时只能放中间：try it on。
try-sth-on.example: Can I try this jacket on, please?
try-sth-on.en: In a shop near Bond Street, I tried on a pair of white leather trainers.
try-sth-on.szh: 在邦德街附近的一家店里，我试穿了一双白色皮运动鞋。

more.en: But the shop on Regent Street let me try it on and take my time.
more.szh: 可摄政街那家店让我随便试戴，慢慢挑。

more.en: Normally, I stick to shops where I can try things on first.
more.szh: 我平时只在能先试穿的店里买衣服。

w-stylish.note: 比较级用 more stylish，不说 stylisher。
w-stylish.en: But they were a bit softer, and a lot more stylish.
w-stylish.szh: 不过穿着软一点，样子也时髦多了。

be-worth-the-money.note: to be good enough to justify the price you pay
be-worth-the-money.tip: worth 后面直接接名词，不加 of：worth the money，不说 worth of the money；也常说 worth every penny。
be-worth-the-money.example: The course wasn't cheap, but it was worth the money.

more.en: It had cost Mum ninety-eight yuan, and she kept saying it was worth the money.
more.szh: 那本词典花了妈妈九十八块钱，她一个劲儿地说买得值。

splash-out-on-sth.note: to spend a lot of money on something, usually something you do not really need
splash-out-on-sth.tip: 花多少钱可以放在中间：splash out £500 on a sofa；介词用 on，不用 for。
splash-out-on-sth.example: We splashed out on a nice hotel for our anniversary.
splash-out-on-sth.en: So I splashed out £180 on them, which is more than I usually spend on shoes in a year.
splash-out-on-sth.szh: 于是我一咬牙花了 180 英镑，比我平时一整年买鞋的钱还多。

more.en: "Don't splash out on something you'll only use at weekends," she said.
more.szh: 「别在周末才用得上的东西上大把花钱，」她说。

more.en: So in October, Chen splashed out £560 on two tablets, one for himself and one for them.
more.szh: 所以十月份，小陈一咬牙花了 560 英镑买了两台平板，一台自己用，一台给爸妈。

w-brush.note: 也能当动词：brush your teeth（刷牙）。
w-brush.en: I kept cleaning them with a special brush.
w-brush.szh: 我隔三岔五就拿专用刷子刷一遍。

w-wardrobe.note: 英式说法；美式常说 closet。
w-wardrobe.en: In April, Tom tried to throw my old pair away, but I hid them in my wardrobe.
w-wardrobe.szh: 四月份 Tom 想把我的旧鞋扔了，我把它们藏进了衣柜。

w-sole.en: Then, by June, the left sole was starting to come away.
w-sole.szh: 结果到了六月，左脚鞋底开始开胶了。

w-come-away.note: 也说 come off：The handle came off.
w-come-away.en: Then, by June, the left sole was starting to come away.
w-come-away.szh: 结果到了六月，左脚鞋底开始开胶了。

take-sth-back.note: to return something you bought to the shop because it is wrong or broken
take-sth-back.tip: 代词放中间：take it back；它还有「收回（说过的话）」的意思：I take it back — you're right。
take-sth-back.example: If the charger doesn't work, just take it back.
take-sth-back.en: On Saturday, I took them back to the shop.
take-sth-back.szh: 周六我把鞋拿回了店里。

wear-and-tear.note: the damage that happens to something when it is used for a long time
wear-and-tear.tip: 不可数名词，前面不加 a；常和 normal 连用。tear 在这里读 /teə/，和「眼泪」的 /tɪə/ 不同。
wear-and-tear.example: The landlord can't keep your deposit for normal wear and tear.
wear-and-tear.en: "I'm afraid that's normal wear and tear," she said.

w-customer-service.note: 前面一般不加冠词：call customer service。
w-customer-service.en: She told me to email customer service if anything else came up.
w-customer-service.szh: 她让我以后再有什么问题，就给客服发邮件。

w-parcel.note: 英式说法；美式多说 package。
w-parcel.en: The parcel has to go to China by Friday, or it won't get there in time.
w-parcel.szh: 包裹周五前必须寄去中国，不然就赶不上了。

more.en: Ten days later, the parcel arrived in Chengdu.
more.szh: 十天后，包裹到了成都。

have-sth-in-mind.note: to have an idea or plan about what you want
have-sth-in-mind.tip: 店员常问 Do you have anything in mind?（您有看中的吗？）；in 不能换成 on。
have-sth-in-mind.example: I'd like a new sofa, but I don't have a colour in mind yet.
have-sth-in-mind.en: Come on, you must have something in mind.
have-sth-in-mind.szh: 得了吧，你心里总该有点想法吧？

more.en: Tom already had something in mind: a red Golf, because his dad used to drive one.
more.szh: Tom 心里早有目标了：一辆红色高尔夫，因为他爸以前就开这款。

more.en: I know you've already got a plan in mind: football.
more.szh: 我知道你心里早有打算了：踢足球。

be-into-sth.note: to be very interested in an activity or subject and enjoy it
be-into-sth.tip: 口语说法；后面接名词或 doing：be into running。问别人喜好时 into 放在句末：What are you into?
be-into-sth.example: My brother is really into old cameras.

more.en: I'd never been into science, so I just decided secondary school was much harder.
more.szh: 我本来就对理科没兴趣，所以干脆认定中学就是难得多。

more.en: Chen's parents in Chengdu have never really been into technology.
more.szh: 小陈在成都的爸妈，对科技产品一直不怎么感冒。

on-a-budget.note: having only a limited amount of money to spend
on-a-budget.tip: 常说 be on a budget、travel on a budget；a tight budget 是「预算很紧」。
on-a-budget.example: If you're on a budget, the market is cheaper than the supermarket.
on-a-budget.en: Well, we're on a budget, so let's be clever about it.
on-a-budget.szh: 嗯，咱们预算有限，得动动脑子。

more.en: The school was on a budget, so she wrote her own listening tests from scratch.
more.szh: 学校经费紧张，她就自己从头编听力题。

more.en: We're on a budget, and I can't hire anyone else.
more.szh: 我们预算紧，我没法再招人了。

w-cookbook.en: The bookshop on Neal Street has the biggest cookbook section I know.
w-cookbook.szh: 尼尔街那家书店的菜谱区，是我知道的最大的。

you-can-t-go-wrong-with-sth.text: you can't go wrong with sth
you-can-t-go-wrong-with-sth.note: used to say that something is a safe choice and will not disappoint
you-can-t-go-wrong-with-sth.tip: you 在这里泛指「谁都」，不是专指对方；with 后面接名词。
you-can-t-go-wrong-with-sth.example: If you don't know what to cook, you can't go wrong with pasta.
you-can-t-go-wrong-with-sth.en: Listen, you can't go wrong with something she can eat.
you-can-t-go-wrong-with-sth.szh: 听我的，送吃的总不会错。

w-biscuit.note: 英式说法；美式的 biscuit 是一种松软的小面包。

wrap-sth-up.note: to cover something in paper, especially a present
wrap-sth-up.tip: 代词放中间：wrap it up；在会议里 Let's wrap up 是「收尾、结束」。
wrap-sth-up.example: I wrapped the present up in old newspaper.
wrap-sth-up.en: And food's the easiest thing to wrap up.

w-hang-on.note: 口语，比 wait 随意；打电话时 Hang on a sec 是「稍等」。

it-s-the-thought-that-counts.zh: 礼轻情意重；心意最重要
it-s-the-thought-that-counts.note: used to say that a present is nice because someone thought about you, even if it is small or not perfect
it-s-the-thought-that-counts.tip: 固定说法，count 在这里是「重要、算数」，不是「数数」；常带点安慰或打趣。
it-s-the-thought-that-counts.example: The cake looked terrible, but it's the thought that counts.
it-s-the-thought-that-counts.en: Well, it's the thought that counts.

w-figure.note: 也有「身材、人物」的意思，这里是「数字」。
w-figure.en: In 2020, the figure was only one in five.
w-figure.szh: 2020 年，这个数字还只有五分之一。

sell-sth-on.note: to sell something that you bought earlier to another person
sell-sth-on.tip: on 表示「往下传」；和 sell sth on an app（在 App 上卖）的 on 不是一回事。
sell-sth-on.example: He buys old bikes, fixes them and sells them on.
sell-sth-on.en: Others sell things on to make room for new ones, and earn a bit of money.
sell-sth-on.szh: 也有人把旧衣服转手卖掉，给新衣服腾地方，顺便赚点小钱。

more.en: He sold it on a month later.
more.szh: 一个月后就转手卖了。

make-room-for-sth.note: to move or remove things so that there is space for something else
make-room-for-sth.tip: room 在这里是不可数名词「空间」，不加 a；也可以说 make room for sb（给某人让个位子）。
make-room-for-sth.example: We sold the old sofa to make room for a desk.
make-room-for-sth.en: Others sell things on to make room for new ones, and earn a bit of money.
make-room-for-sth.szh: 也有人把旧衣服转手卖掉，给新衣服腾地方，顺便赚点小钱。

more.en: I'd also made room in my bag for a dictionary the size of a brick.
more.szh: 我还在书包里腾出地方，塞了一本砖头那么厚的词典。

more.en: We'll make room for it in the first update, so that the investors can see it before Christmas.
more.szh: 我们在第一次更新里给它腾出位置，好让投资人圣诞节前能看到。

w-mending.note: 动词 mend：mend a hole in a jumper。
w-mending.en: And a few have even taken up mending as a hobby.
w-mending.szh: 还有少数人干脆把缝缝补补当成了爱好。

w-wool.note: 形容词 woollen（英式两个 l）。
w-wool.en: Then, by chance, she spotted a wool coat for £8 while she was looking for boots.
w-wool.szh: 后来她找靴子的时候，碰巧看到一件羊毛大衣，只要 8 英镑。

snap-sth-up.note: to buy something quickly because it is cheap or there are not many left
snap-sth-up.tip: 常用被动：be snapped up（被抢光）；代词放中间：snap it up。
snap-sth-up.example: The cheap tickets were snapped up in an hour.
snap-sth-up.en: "I snapped it up for next to nothing," she told us.
snap-sth-up.szh: 「我几乎没花钱就抢到手了，」她跟我们说。

for-next-to-nothing.note: for a very small amount of money
for-next-to-nothing.tip: next to 在这里是「几乎」：next to nothing = almost nothing。
for-next-to-nothing.example: We bought the table at a car-boot sale for next to nothing.
for-next-to-nothing.en: "I snapped it up for next to nothing," she told us.
for-next-to-nothing.szh: 「我几乎没花钱就抢到手了，」她跟我们说。

cost-a-fortune.tip: cost 的过去式和过去分词都是 cost；口语夸张说法，类似的还有 cost an arm and a leg。
cost-a-fortune.example: Fixing the roof cost a fortune.
cost-a-fortune.en: "A coat like that would cost a fortune new, and it probably wouldn't be as warm."
cost-a-fortune.szh: 「这样的大衣买新的得花一大笔钱，还不一定有这么暖和。」

w-outfit.note: 指搭配好的一整套穿着。
w-outfit.en: Ella worked out that her whole winter outfit cost less than one new pair of jeans.
w-outfit.szh: Ella 算了算，她一整套冬装加起来，比一条新牛仔裤还便宜。

w-compete.note: 和谁竞争用 with；名词是 competition。
w-compete.en: Some small shop owners say they can't compete with prices that low.
w-compete.szh: 一些小服装店的店主说，价格这么低，他们根本没法竞争。

w-spokesperson.en: But a spokesperson for one app, Second Look, says the change is good for everyone.
w-spokesperson.szh: 可二手 App「Second Look」的一位发言人说，这个变化对大家都有好处。

go-out-of-fashion.note: to stop being popular or fashionable
go-out-of-fashion.tip: 反义是 come into fashion；「正流行」是 be in fashion。
go-out-of-fashion.example: White trainers never seem to go out of fashion.
go-out-of-fashion.en: "And older styles aren't as likely to go out of fashion as people think."
go-out-of-fashion.szh: 「而且老款式并不像大家想的那么容易过时。」

more.en: She carried it home in a brown bag that had gone out of fashion years before.
more.szh: 她就装进一个早就过时的棕色包里带回家。

more.en: Big ones went out of fashion for years, but noise-cancelling has brought them back.
more.szh: 大耳机有好些年不流行了，是降噪又把它们带了回来。

w-denim.note: a denim jacket 就是牛仔夹克。
w-denim.en: Actually, Ella's favourite find so far is a denim jacket for £6.
w-denim.szh: 说起来，Ella 到目前为止最得意的收获，是一件 6 英镑的牛仔夹克。

w-meter.note: 智能电表是 smart meter，英国家庭很常见。
w-meter.en: Before you two start making excuses, let me look into the meter readings.
w-meter.szh: 你俩先别急着找借口，我来查查电表读数。

w-accountant.note: accounts 是「账目」，accountant 是管账的人。
w-accountant.en: I'm an accountant — I love this stuff.

add-up.note: if numbers or facts do not add up, they do not make sense or seem wrong
add-up.tip: 多用否定：It doesn't add up.；本义是「加起来」：add up the numbers。
add-up.example: His story doesn't add up — he said he was at home, but his car was gone.
add-up.en: OK, the numbers don't add up.

more.en: It doesn't add up.
more.szh: 这说不通啊。

more.en: The numbers don't add up, though.
more.szh: 不过数字不对劲。

leave-sth-on.note: to not switch off a light or machine
leave-sth-on.tip: 反义是 switch / turn sth off；代词放中间：leave it on。
leave-sth-on.example: Did you leave the oven on again?
leave-sth-on.en: Someone's been leaving something on all day.
leave-sth-on.szh: 有人一直把什么东西整天开着。

more.en: Unfortunately, she'd left the microphone on, so eight hundred students heard that too.
more.szh: 可惜她忘了关话筒，这句话八百个学生也全听见了。

more.en: Some people leave them on all day without music, just for the quiet.
more.szh: 有人一整天戴着，不放音乐，就图个安静。

w-earn.en: I don't earn enough money to heat an empty flat.
w-earn.szh: 我挣的钱可不够给空房子供暖。

can-t-afford-sth.note: to not have enough money to pay for something
can-t-afford-sth.tip: 后面接名词或 to do：can't afford to buy a car；不说 can't afford buying。
can-t-afford-sth.example: We can't afford a holiday this year.
can-t-afford-sth.en: And I can't afford bills like this.
can-t-afford-sth.szh: 这样的账单我也付不起。

fair-enough.note: used to say that you accept what someone has said, even if you do not fully agree
fair-enough.tip: 英国口语里很常用，带一点「勉强同意」的意思；单独成句。
fair-enough.example: "I can't come — I'm working late." "Fair enough."

more.en: Fair enough.
more.szh: 也对。

keep-a-record-of-sth.note: to write down information regularly so that you can look at it later
keep-a-record-of-sth.tip: record 作名词重音在前 /ˈrekɔːd/，作动词重音在后。
keep-a-record-of-sth.example: Keep a record of everything you spend this month.
keep-a-record-of-sth.en: But let's keep a record of the smart meter readings for a week, three times a day.
keep-a-record-of-sth.szh: 不过咱们把智能电表的读数记一个星期，每天记三次。

w-reading.note: 这里不是「阅读」，是表上显示的数。
w-reading.en: But let's keep a record of the smart meter readings for a week, three times a day.
w-reading.szh: 不过咱们把智能电表的读数记一个星期，每天记三次。

pay-sb-back.note: to give someone back the money that you owe them
pay-sb-back.tip: 钱数可以放在后面：pay you back £30；也有「报复」的意思，看上下文。
pay-sb-back.example: Can I borrow a tenner? I'll pay you back tomorrow.
pay-sb-back.en: And Chen, I'll pay you back £30 for my extra hot showers.
pay-sb-back.szh: 还有小陈，我多洗的那些热水澡，补给你 30 英镑。

more.en: I'll pay you back, I promise.
more.szh: 我会还你的，保证。

w-dehumidifier.note: humid 是「潮湿的」，de- 表示「去掉」。
w-dehumidifier.en: It's the dehumidifier in the hall cupboard.
w-dehumidifier.szh: 是门厅柜子里那台除湿机。

w-non-stop.note: 也可以作形容词：a non-stop flight（直飞航班）。
w-non-stop.en: It's been running non-stop since January.

w-blender.note: 动词 blend 是「混合、搅拌」。
w-blender.en: So, last November, at 11:58 pm, I bought a blender I didn't need.
w-blender.szh: 去年十一月，晚上 11 点 58 分，我买了一台根本用不着的搅拌机。

w-brand-new.note: 比 new 语气强，强调「全新、没用过」。
w-brand-new.en: It was still £90 — with a brand-new clock.
w-brand-new.szh: 还是 90 英镑——配上了一个崭新的倒计时。

w-freelance.note: 做自由职业的人是 freelancer。
w-freelance.en: Now, I'm a freelance writer in Brighton, and I like to think I'm a careful shopper.
w-freelance.szh: 说起来，我是布莱顿的自由撰稿人，一直觉得自己买东西挺精明的。

w-discount.note: discount code 是网购用的折扣码。
w-discount.en: I'll happily spend twenty minutes tracking down a discount code for a £4 candle.
w-discount.szh: 为了一根 4 英镑的蜡烛，我能乐呵呵地花二十分钟去找折扣码。

w-countdown.note: 动词短语是 count down：count down the seconds。
w-countdown.en: But countdown clocks are such good tricks that even I keep falling for them.
w-countdown.szh: 可倒计时这一招实在太高明了，连我都一次次上当。

fall-for-sth.zh: 上（某种花招）的当；信以为真
fall-for-sth.note: to be tricked into believing something that is not true
fall-for-sth.tip: fall for sb 是「爱上某人」，看后面接的是人还是花招；fall 的过去式是 fell。
fall-for-sth.example: Don't fall for those emails that say you've won a prize.
fall-for-sth.en: But countdown clocks are such good tricks that even I keep falling for them.
fall-for-sth.szh: 可倒计时这一招实在太高明了，连我都一次次上当。

more.en: Every beginner falls for those videos.
more.szh: 新手都会被那些视频骗。

more.en: Did one of us fall for a fake email?
more.szh: 是不是我们谁上了假邮件的当？

w-excitement.note: 形容词 excited（人感到兴奋）、exciting（让人兴奋的）。
w-excitement.en: And the excitement wears off so quickly that sometimes I forget what I've ordered.
w-excitement.szh: 而且那股兴奋劲儿过得飞快，有时候我连自己下单买了什么都忘了。

sign-up-for-sth.zh: 报名参加；注册（某项服务）
sign-up-for-sth.note: to agree to take part in something or to start using a service, usually by giving your details
sign-up-for-sth.tip: 后面接名词用 for，接动词用 to do：sign up to do a course；名词 sign-up 带连字符。
sign-up-for-sth.example: I signed up for a free trial and forgot to cancel it.
sign-up-for-sth.en: I only sign up for an offer if I'd happily buy the thing at full price.
sign-up-for-sth.szh: 原价我也乐意买的东西，我才去抢它的优惠。

more.en: He keeps telling me to sign up for a cycling course for adults.
more.szh: 他老劝我去报个成人骑车课。

at-full-price.note: for the normal price, without any money taken off
at-full-price.tip: 介词用 at；同样的还有 at half price（半价）、at a discount（打折）。
at-full-price.example: I never buy books at full price.
at-full-price.en: I only sign up for an offer if I'd happily buy the thing at full price.
at-full-price.szh: 原价我也乐意买的东西，我才去抢它的优惠。

shop-around.note: to compare the prices of something in different shops before you buy it
shop-around.tip: 不及物，后面要说买什么用 for：shop around for a new phone。
shop-around.example: It's worth shopping around for car insurance.
shop-around.en: Before I spend more than £30, I shop around for a week.
shop-around.szh: 超过 30 英镑的东西，我先货比三家，看上一个星期再说。

in-stock.note: available in a shop and ready to buy
in-stock.tip: 反义是 out of stock（缺货）；stock 在这里不加冠词。
in-stock.example: Do you have this jacket in stock in a medium?
in-stock.en: And I pay no attention to "only 2 left in stock".
in-stock.szh: 还有，「库存仅剩 2 件」这种话，我一概不理。

more.en: I even started an email to the shop: "I'm writing to ask if the green band is still in stock."
more.szh: 我甚至给店里写了半封邮件：「我写信是想问一下，绿表带那款还有没有货。」

too-good-to-be-true.zh: 好得令人难以置信（多半有诈）
too-good-to-be-true.note: so good that you think there must be a problem with it
too-good-to-be-true.tip: 常跟在 look / sound / seem 后面；俗话说全了是 If it looks too good to be true, it probably is。
too-good-to-be-true.example: A two-bedroom flat in central London for £800 a month? It sounds too good to be true.
too-good-to-be-true.en: Honestly, if something looks too good to be true, it usually is.
too-good-to-be-true.szh: 说真的，一样东西要是好得不像真的，那它多半就不是真的。

more.en: A bowl cost three yuan, which seemed too good to be true even then.
more.szh: 一碗才三块钱，就算在那时候也便宜得不像真的。

more.en: And honestly, a watch that tells you how to sleep better sounds too good to be true.
more.szh: 说实话，一块能教你怎么睡得更好的手表，听着也太美了，不像真的。

hand-sth-down.note: to give something to a younger person in your family
hand-sth-down.tip: 常用被动：be handed down (from sb)；穿哥哥姐姐的旧衣服叫 hand-me-downs。
hand-sth-down.example: This watch was handed down from my great-grandfather.
hand-sth-down.en: That year, her grandfather handed down three old albums from Gujarat.
hand-sth-down.szh: 那年，爷爷把三本从古吉拉特带来的旧集邮册传给了她。

more.en: My cousin had handed it down to me, along with a helmet that was far too big.
more.szh: 那是表哥骑过传给我的，还附送一个大得离谱的头盔。

more.en: One was an old book my grandad had handed down to me.
more.szh: 其中一本是爷爷留给我的旧书。

w-album.note: stamp album 集邮册；也指音乐专辑。
w-album.en: That year, her grandfather handed down three old albums from Gujarat.
w-album.szh: 那年，爷爷把三本从古吉拉特带来的旧集邮册传给了她。

be-fascinated-by-sth.note: to be extremely interested in something
be-fascinated-by-sth.tip: 人「着迷」用 fascinated，让人着迷的东西用 fascinating：a fascinating book。
be-fascinated-by-sth.example: As a child, I was fascinated by trains.
be-fascinated-by-sth.en: She was fascinated by them at once, and she's hung on to every single one.
be-fascinated-by-sth.szh: 她一下子就被迷住了，每一本都留到了今天。

more.en: I was fascinated by the way that man pulled noodles by hand.
more.szh: 那个大叔手工拉面的样子，我当年看得入了迷。

more.en: At first, she was fascinated by the graphs.
more.szh: 一开始，那些图表让她着了迷。

hang-on-to-sth.note: to keep something and not give it away or throw it away
hang-on-to-sth.tip: hang 表示「挂」时过去式是 hung；英式也说 hang onto。
hang-on-to-sth.example: Hang on to your receipt in case you need to take it back.
hang-on-to-sth.en: She was fascinated by them at once, and she's hung on to every single one.
hang-on-to-sth.szh: 她一下子就被迷住了，每一本都留到了今天。

more.en: I used to draw on everything, and I've hung on to a folder of those drawings for forty-two years.
more.szh: 那时候我见什么画什么，那一夹子画，我留了整整四十二年。

look-through-sth.note: to look at a lot of things in a box, pile or document, usually quickly
look-through-sth.tip: through 表示从头翻到尾；look at 只是「看」一眼。
look-through-sth.example: I looked through my old photos last night.
look-through-sth.en: Every spring, she looks through the boxes at a few car-boot sales in Surrey.
look-through-sth.szh: 每年春天，她都会去萨里郡的几个后备箱集市翻箱子。

w-car-boot-sale.note: 英国特色：大家把旧东西放在汽车后备箱里卖。
w-car-boot-sale.en: Every spring, she looks through the boxes at a few car-boot sales in Surrey.
w-car-boot-sale.szh: 每年春天，她都会去萨里郡的几个后备箱集市翻箱子。

by-accident.note: without planning it or wanting it to happen
by-accident.tip: 反义是 on purpose（故意）；和 by chance 意思接近。
by-accident.example: I found the café by accident when I got lost.
by-accident.en: Actually, her best stamp turned up by accident.
by-accident.szh: 其实，她最好的一张邮票是碰巧得来的。

w-charity-shop.note: 卖捐来的旧物，收入给慈善机构，店员多是志愿者。
w-charity-shop.en: Six years ago, a charity shop near her flat was short-staffed.
w-charity-shop.szh: 六年前，她家附近一家慈善商店人手不够。

w-fake.note: 也能当形容词：a fake stamp。
w-fake.en: At fourteen, she paid £50 for a stamp that turned out to be a fake.
w-fake.szh: 十四岁那年，她花 50 英镑买了一张邮票，结果是假的。

w-dealer.note: stamp dealer 邮商，car dealer 车商。
w-dealer.en: These days, dealers in London know her by name.
w-dealer.szh: 如今，伦敦的邮商都叫得出她的名字。

take-pride-in-sth.note: to feel pleased about something you do or have and to do it carefully
take-pride-in-sth.tip: 后面接名词或 doing；pride 前面不加 a。
take-pride-in-sth.example: He takes pride in his cooking.
take-pride-in-sth.en: She takes pride in knowing where each stamp has been, and how much it cost to send a letter that year.
take-pride-in-sth.szh: 她最得意的，是知道每张邮票去过哪儿，那一年寄一封信要花多少钱。

w-plain.note: 说衣服、食物也常用：a plain T-shirt、plain rice。
w-plain.en: It was a £240 watch with a plain white face and a dark green leather band.
w-plain.szh: 一块 240 英镑的手表，白色素表盘，墨绿色皮表带。

take-your-time.note: to do something slowly and carefully without hurrying
take-your-time.tip: your 跟着主语变：I took my time；也常单独说 Take your time. 让对方别急。
take-your-time.example: Take your time — the train doesn't leave for an hour.
take-your-time.en: But the shop on Regent Street let me try it on and take my time.
take-your-time.szh: 可摄政街那家店让我随便试戴，慢慢挑。

more.en: Tom says I should take my time, but the drivers behind me don't agree.
more.szh: Tom 说我慢慢骑就行，可我后面的司机可不这么想。

more.en: Take your time.
more.szh: 不着急。

more.en: I started taking my time over dinner, and I could actually taste it.
more.szh: 吃晚饭我开始慢慢吃，真的尝出了味道。

go-back-and-forth.note: to keep changing your opinion or decision
go-back-and-forth.tip: 本义是「来来回回地走」；在什么事上犹豫用 on / about。
go-back-and-forth.example: We went back and forth about the holiday for weeks.
go-back-and-forth.en: So for two weeks, I went back and forth.
go-back-and-forth.szh: 于是整整两个星期，我一直拿不定主意。

more.en: For years I went back and forth: art or law, art or law.
more.szh: 好多年里我都在来回纠结：艺术还是法律，艺术还是法律。

more.en: He typed in an address and went back and forth between "Confirm" and "Cancel" for a whole minute.
more.szh: 他输了一个地址，在「确认」和「取消」之间来回犹豫了整整一分钟。

w-nervous.note: 比较级 more nervous；名词 nerves。
w-nervous.en: The closer I got to paying, the more nervous I felt.
w-nervous.szh: 离付款越近，我就越紧张。

have-second-thoughts.note: to start to have doubts about a decision you have made
have-second-thoughts.tip: thoughts 用复数；对什么犹豫用 about。
have-second-thoughts.example: I'm having second thoughts about the new job.

more.en: I had second thoughts about telling this story, because he still lives round the corner.
more.szh: 讲不讲这个故事，我犹豫过，因为他还住在附近。

check-out.note: to pay for the things you are buying online or in a shop, or to leave a hotel
check-out.tip: 名词写成 checkout：go to the checkout；check sth out 还有「看看、了解一下」的意思。
check-out.example: Your basket will be saved until you check out.
check-out.en: And I closed the page before I checked out.

change-your-mind.note: to change a decision or opinion
change-your-mind.tip: your 跟着主语变：she changed her mind；mind 用单数。
change-your-mind.example: If you change your mind, the offer is still there.
change-your-mind.en: Once, I even changed my mind at the bus stop.
change-your-mind.szh: 有一次在公交站，我又改了主意。

w-reviewer.note: review 是评价，-er 表示人。
w-reviewer.en: A few reviewers loved the band.
w-reviewer.szh: 有几个人很喜欢那条表带。

sell-out.note: if a product or event sells out, there are none left to buy
sell-out.tip: 说状态常用 be sold out；某店卖完了某物是 sell out of sth：They've sold out of bread。
sell-out.example: The concert sold out in ten minutes.
sell-out.en: "I'm afraid it's sold out," the assistant said.
sell-out.szh: 「不好意思，已经卖完了，」店员说。

w-tattoo.en: "The last one went yesterday — to a young man with a chef's tattoo."
w-tattoo.szh: 「最后一块昨天卖掉了，买的是个小伙子，胳膊上有个厨师的文身。」

make-a-complaint.note: to tell a company or person officially that you are not happy about something
make-a-complaint.tip: 投诉什么用 about，向谁投诉用 to：make a complaint to the manager；动词是 complain。
make-a-complaint.example: Several guests made a complaint about the noise.
make-a-complaint.en: Hi, my name's Chen, and I'm calling to make a complaint about order 48213.
make-a-complaint.szh: 你好，我叫小陈，打电话是想投诉一下 48213 号订单。

more.en: Most of my clients wanted to make a complaint about a neighbour's tree or wall.
more.szh: 我的客户大多是来投诉邻居家的树或者墙的。

more.en: Every winter, he makes a complaint to the bus company, and every winter nothing changes.
more.szh: 每年冬天他都向公交公司投诉，每年冬天都没有任何变化。

w-oversized.note: 服装网站常用词，oversized fit 是「宽松版型」。
w-oversized.szh: 你们网站上写的是「略微宽松」。

w-looser.note: loose 的比较级；反义是 tight（紧）。注意和 lose（丢失）区分。
w-looser.en: Well, I wanted something a little looser than my other jumpers — not a tent.
w-looser.szh: 嗯，我想要的是比我其他毛衣稍微宽松一点的，不是一顶帐篷。

w-tent.note: 搭帐篷是 put up a tent。
w-tent.en: Well, I wanted something a little looser than my other jumpers — not a tent.
w-tent.szh: 嗯，我想要的是比我其他毛衣稍微宽松一点的，不是一顶帐篷。

w-blanket.en: He said it was way warmer than his blanket.
w-blanket.szh: 他说这比他的毯子暖和多了。

as-described.note: the same as someone said or wrote it would be
as-described.tip: 网购和二手买卖里的常用语；not as described 就是「货不对板」。
as-described.example: The flat was exactly as described in the advert.
as-described.en: So I'm afraid it's not as described.
as-described.szh: 所以恐怕这件毛衣跟描述的不符。

more.en: It didn't go as described in the textbook, and we couldn't believe our eyes.
more.szh: 实验完全没按课本上写的来，我们都看傻了眼。

more.en: If the fix doesn't work as described, drop me a line, and I'll reply myself.
more.szh: 要是照着做了还是不行，给我写两句就好，我亲自回。

send-sth-back.note: to return something by post because it is wrong or you do not want it
send-sth-back.tip: 代词放中间：send it back；当面拿回店里是 take sth back。
send-sth-back.example: The shoes didn't fit, so I sent them back.
send-sth-back.en: So I'd like to send it back.

more.en: If this were a shop mug, I'd just send it back.
more.szh: 要是店里买的杯子，我直接退回去就完了。

get-a-refund.note: to get your money back for something you have returned
get-a-refund.tip: refund 作名词重音在前；作动词（refund the money）重音在后。
get-a-refund.example: If the train is more than an hour late, you can get a refund.

i-d-appreciate-it-if.note: a polite way to ask someone to do something
i-d-appreciate-it-if.tip: it 不能省：不说 I'd appreciate if …；if 后面常用 you could / you would。
i-d-appreciate-it-if.example: I'd appreciate it if you could reply by Friday.
i-d-appreciate-it-if.en: I'd appreciate it if someone could call me back.
i-d-appreciate-it-if.szh: 麻烦哪位尽快给我回个电话。

put-sth-right.note: to correct a mistake or deal with a problem so that things are as they should be
put-sth-right.tip: put 的过去式、过去分词都是 put；也常说 put things right。
put-sth-right.example: The bank made a mistake, but they put it right the same day.
put-sth-right.en: I need a jumper for a party on Saturday, so I hope you can put this right before then.
put-sth-right.szh: 我周六要去参加聚会，得有件毛衣穿，所以希望你们能在那之前把这事处理好。

w-delighted.note: 比 happy 更正式，客服和商务邮件里很常见。
w-delighted.en: We're delighted you love your new jumper.
w-delighted.szh: 很高兴您喜欢您的新毛衣。

w-podcast.note: 做播客的人叫 podcaster；听播客是 listen to a podcast。
w-podcast.en: Hello, and welcome to Spend Less, the podcast about keeping your money.
w-podcast.szh: 大家好，欢迎收听《少花点》，一档教你把钱留住的播客。

w-payday.note: 英国很多公司按月发工资，月底那天就是 payday。
w-payday.en: I should say, I used to buy a new top every payday.
w-payday.szh: 先交代一句，我以前每到发工资那天都要买件新上衣。

trade-sth-for-sth.note: to give something to someone and get something else from them in return
trade-sth-for-sth.tip: for 后面是换来的东西；跟谁换用 with：trade seats with sb。trade 也是「贸易」，这里是口语里的「换」。
trade-sth-for-sth.example: I traded my old guitar for a bike.
trade-sth-for-sth.en: Once a month, I'd trade my old tops for my older sister's jumpers.
trade-sth-for-sth.szh: 每个月我会拿自己的旧上衣去换姐姐的毛衣。

learn-to-live-with-sth.zh: 学会接受（不理想的情况）
learn-to-live-with-sth.note: to accept something that is not perfect because you cannot change it
learn-to-live-with-sth.tip: learn 的过去式英式常写 learnt，learned 也对；with 后面接名词。
learn-to-live-with-sth.example: The flat is small, but we've learned to live with it.
learn-to-live-with-sth.en: I also learned to live with one pair of jeans.
learn-to-live-with-sth.szh: 我也学会了一条牛仔裤穿到底。

more.en: Apparently, the school just learned to live with the black mark on the bench.
more.szh: 听说实验台上那块黑印，学校也就一直将就着没管。

more.en: But we did have to learn to live with the coffee stains.
more.szh: 不过，上面的咖啡渍我们也只好忍了。

w-colleague.en: And none of my colleagues noticed.
w-colleague.szh: 结果同事一个都没发现。

do-without-sth.zh: 没有（某物）也行；将就着不用
do-without-sth.tip: 常和 can 连用：I can't do without coffee（离不开咖啡）。
do-without-sth.example: We can do without a car — the bus stops outside our house.
do-without-sth.en: I did without most of the electric stuff in my kitchen.
do-without-sth.szh: 厨房里的大部分小电器，我都不用了。

more.en: He'll have to do without a mug this year.
more.szh: 今年只好委屈他，没有杯子了。

more.en: And it's worth remembering that most people can do without another app.
more.szh: 还有一点得记住：大多数人不多装一个 App，日子也照样过。

get-by.note: to manage to live or do something with the money or things you have
get-by.tip: 靠什么过活用 on：get by on £20 a week；也说语言：get by in French（法语能凑合用）。
get-by.example: I don't earn much, but I get by.
get-by.en: I gave myself £20 a month for fun stuff, and I got by.
get-by.szh: 我每个月给自己留 20 英镑玩，也就这么过来了。

more.en: For forty years, she got by with a calculator and a good memory.
more.szh: 四十年来，她就靠一个计算器和一副好记性对付过来。

w-board-game.note: Monopoly（大富翁）、chess（国际象棋）都算 board games。
w-board-game.en: And I got into board games.

be-tempted-to-do.note: to want to do something, especially something you know you should not do
be-tempted-to-do.tip: 后面接 to do；名词 temptation（诱惑）。
be-tempted-to-do.example: I was tempted to leave early, but I stayed until the end.
be-tempted-to-do.en: There was a huge sale, and I was really tempted to break the rule.
be-tempted-to-do.szh: 那时候有个大促销，我是真想破一次戒。

save-up-for-sth.note: to keep money for a period of time so that you can buy something
save-up-for-sth.tip: up 强调「一点点攒起来」；也可以接 to do：save up to buy a car。
save-up-for-sth.example: She's saving up for a trip to Japan.
save-up-for-sth.en: Instead, I saved up for a second-hand bike.
save-up-for-sth.szh: 结果我没买，而是攒钱买了一辆二手自行车。

w-advert.note: 英式口语说法，也说 ad；正式一点是 advertisement。
w-advert.en: I stayed up late three nights in a row, reading adverts.
w-advert.szh: 我一连三个晚上熬夜看卖车广告。

w-spreadsheet.note: Excel 做的那种表格就是 spreadsheet。
w-spreadsheet.en: Her spreadsheet was so detailed that it had a page for car washes.
w-spreadsheet.szh: 她做的对比表细到连洗车都单独列了一页。

w-reliable.note: 说人也行：a reliable friend（靠得住的朋友）。
w-reliable.en: A 2015 Fiesta for £3,200 was the cheapest, and nearly as reliable as the Golf.
w-reliable.szh: 一辆 2015 年的嘉年华要 3200 英镑，是最便宜的，可靠程度也跟高尔夫差不多。

take-sth-for-a-test-drive.text: take sth for a test drive
take-sth-for-a-test-drive.note: to drive a car before you buy it to see if you like it
take-sth-for-a-test-drive.tip: 代词放中间：take it for a test drive；也可以说 test-drive a car（动词带连字符）。
take-sth-for-a-test-drive.example: Can I take it for a test drive before I decide?
take-sth-for-a-test-drive.en: So we took the Fiesta for a test drive in Lewisham.
take-sth-for-a-test-drive.szh: 于是我们去刘易舍姆试驾了那辆嘉年华。

more.en: First, she took the course for a test drive at a free taster evening.
more.szh: 她先去参加了一个免费的体验晚课，试了试这门课。

more.en: And a woman living with five flatmates took it for a test drive for a week.
more.szh: 还有，有个跟五个室友合租的女生拿它试用了一个星期。

w-horn.note: 按喇叭是 sound / use the horn，口语也说 beep the horn。
w-horn.en: The seller kept an eye on Tom, who was trying the horn for fun.
w-horn.szh: 卖家一直盯着 Tom，因为他在那儿按喇叭玩。

w-petrol.en: She added up insurance, road tax, parking and petrol, and it came to £2,400 a year.
w-petrol.szh: 她把保险、路税、停车费和油钱加起来，一年要 2400 英镑。

come-to-amount.note: to be a particular total when everything is added together
come-to-amount.tip: 主语常是 bill、total、cost；不用被动，也不说 come up to。
come-to-amount.example: The bill came to £86 for four of us.
come-to-amount.en: She added up insurance, road tax, parking and petrol, and it came to £2,400 a year.
come-to-amount.szh: 她把保险、路税、停车费和油钱加起来，一年要 2400 英镑。

keep-costs-down.note: to stop the amount of money you spend from getting higher
keep-costs-down.tip: costs 用复数；同类说法 keep prices down、keep the noise down。
keep-costs-down.example: We cook at home to keep costs down.
keep-costs-down.en: I looked for ways to keep costs down.

more.en: One day you'll share a flat in England with a man called Tom to keep costs down.
more.szh: 将来有一天，为了省钱，你会在英国跟一个叫 Tom 的人合租。

get-a-good-deal.note: to buy something at a good price
get-a-good-deal.tip: 在什么上划算用 on：get a good deal on sth；最划算是 the best deal。
get-a-good-deal.example: We got a good deal on the flights because we booked early.
get-a-good-deal.en: But even if we got a good deal on insurance, the car would still cost us £200 a month.
get-a-good-deal.szh: 可就算保险谈到个好价钱，这辆车每个月还是要花掉我们 200 英镑。

more.en: I'll give him socks instead — I got a good deal on a pack of five last week.
more.szh: 我改送他袜子吧——上周刚好买到一包五双的，挺划算。

more.en: By the way, we got a good deal on this room, so please eat all the sandwiches.
more.szh: 顺便说一句，这个场地我们租得很便宜，所以请把三明治都吃完。

be-out-of-the-question.note: to be impossible or not allowed
be-out-of-the-question.tip: the 不能省：out of question 是错的；without question 才是「毫无疑问」。
be-out-of-the-question.example: A holiday this summer is out of the question.
be-out-of-the-question.en: So a car was out of the question.

think-twice.note: to think very carefully before you decide to do something
think-twice.tip: 常说 think twice before doing / about sth；过去式 thought。
think-twice.example: I'd think twice before lending him money.
think-twice.en: We both thought twice, and the next weekend, we bought two bikes instead.
think-twice.szh: 我们俩都重新掂量了一下，第二个周末改买了两辆自行车。

w-receipt.en: Then Priya read out the receipt.
w-receipt.szh: 然后 Priya 把收据念了一遍。

w-helmet.note: 自行车头盔是 bike helmet。
w-helmet.en: Two bikes, helmets, locks, lights and rain jackets — £3,310.
w-helmet.szh: 两辆自行车、头盔、车锁、车灯和雨衣——3310 英镑。

more.en: My cousin had handed it down to me, along with a helmet that was far too big.
more.szh: 那是表哥骑过传给我的，还附送一个大得离谱的头盔。

w-secondary-school.note: 英国 11 到 16、18 岁上的学校；小学是 primary school。
w-secondary-school.en: It was September 2008, my first day at secondary school.
w-secondary-school.szh: 那是 2008 年 9 月，我上中学的第一天。

w-brick.note: the size of a brick 形容又厚又重，和中文「砖头那么厚」正好一样。
w-brick.en: I'd also made room in my bag for a dictionary the size of a brick.
w-brick.szh: 我还在书包里腾出地方，塞了一本砖头那么厚的词典。

w-confidently.en: At ten to eight, I walked confidently into Room 304 and sat at the back.
w-confidently.szh: 七点五十，我信心满满地走进 304 教室，在最后一排坐下。

w-physics.note: 虽然以 s 结尾，却是不可数名词，动词用单数：Physics is hard.
w-physics.en: The first lesson was physics, and for forty minutes I tried to take in every word.
w-physics.szh: 第一节是物理课，整整四十分钟，我拼命想把每个字都听进去。

take-sth-in.zh: 理解并记住（听到、读到的东西）
take-sth-in.note: to understand and remember something that you hear or read
take-sth-in.tip: 宾语是代词时必须放中间：take it in；名词可以放后面：take in every word。
take-sth-in.example: There was so much information on my first day that I couldn't take it all in.
take-sth-in.en: The first lesson was physics, and for forty minutes I tried to take in every word.
take-sth-in.szh: 第一节是物理课，整整四十分钟，我拼命想把每个字都听进去。

more.en: Try to take in everything she says, even the jokes.
more.szh: 她说的每句话都尽量听进去，连笑话也是。

feel-out-of-place.zh: 觉得格格不入；觉得自己不该在这儿
feel-out-of-place.note: to feel uncomfortable because you are different from the people around you
feel-out-of-place.tip: 可以加 a bit、completely 调程度；东西放得不合适说 look out of place。
feel-out-of-place.example: I felt out of place at the party because everyone else knew each other.
feel-out-of-place.en: I felt a bit out of place, but I told myself it was no big deal.
feel-out-of-place.szh: 我觉得自己有点格格不入，但我跟自己说，没什么大不了的。

at-first.note: at the beginning, before something changes
at-first.tip: 后面通常跟着转折（but、then、later）；first of all 是列举时的「首先」，别混。
at-first.example: At first I hated the new office, but now I quite like it.
at-first.szh: 一开始谁也没注意到我。

w-assume.note: 没有证据就这么认为，常常是错的；名词 assumption。
w-assume.en: I found out later that the other students had assumed I was someone's little brother.
w-assume.szh: 后来我才知道，班上同学都以为我是谁家的弟弟。

put-your-hand-up.note: to raise your arm in a class or meeting because you want to answer or ask something
put-your-hand-up.tip: your 要跟着人称变：put my hand up、put their hands up；也可以说 raise your hand。Hands up! 是「举手」的口令。
put-your-hand-up.example: If you have a question, just put your hand up.
put-your-hand-up.en: So I put my hand up.

more.en: At the bottom, he added, "If you get lost, just put your hand up and wait."
more.szh: 最下面他又加了一句：「要是不知道怎么弄了，举个手，等着就行。」

get-sth-wrong.note: to make a mistake about something, for example a time, a place or a fact
get-sth-wrong.tip: sth 放在 get 和 wrong 中间：get the time wrong；全弄错了说 get it all wrong。英式英语的过去分词是 got。
get-sth-wrong.example: Sorry, I got the date wrong — the party is next Friday.
get-sth-wrong.en: That was when I realised I'd got the building wrong.
get-sth-wrong.szh: 就在那一刻，我才反应过来自己走错了楼。

more.en: I still get half the homework wrong, but at least now I know why."
more.szh: 作业我还是错一半，不过至少现在我知道错在哪儿了。」

more.en: That's fair, we got that part wrong.
more.szh: 说得对，那一块我们没做好。

w-absent.note: mark sb absent 记某人缺勤；反义词是 present（出席的）。
w-absent.en: My class was in Room 304 of Building B, where I'd already been marked absent on the register.
w-absent.szh: 我的班在 B 栋的 304，那边的点名册上已经把我记成缺课了。

make-friends-with.note: to start a friendship with someone
make-friends-with.tip: friends 一定用复数，哪怕只交了一个朋友：make friends with Tom，不说 make a friend with Tom。
make-friends-with.example: My son made friends with the boy next door in his first week.
make-friends-with.en: Anyway, that afternoon I made friends with Liu Yang, who thought it was the coolest thing ever.
make-friends-with.szh: 反正那天下午，我和刘洋交上了朋友，他觉得这事简直酷毙了。

w-dictation.note: give a dictation 是老师「报听写」；动词 dictate（口述、让人记下）。
w-dictation.en: For most of those years, she'd been giving a dictation at twenty to eight every morning.
w-dictation.szh: 这些年里的大部分时间，她每天早上七点四十都要听写，雷打不动。

be-strict-with.note: to make someone follow rules and behave well, and not allow them to break the rules
be-strict-with.tip: 对人用 with，对某件事用 about：strict about homework。strict 本身是形容词，前面要有 be。
be-strict-with.example: My dad was very strict with us about bedtime.
be-strict-with.en: Mrs Zhou was strict with everyone, even the physics teacher's son.
be-strict-with.szh: 周老师对谁都严，连物理老师的儿子也不例外。

more.en: About Mrs Zhou: she's strict with you because she believes in you.
more.szh: 关于周老师：她对你严，是因为她相信你行。

more.en: One man says the app is too strict with him, because it reminds him about the bins every hour.
more.szh: 有个男的说这个 App 对他太严了，每小时都提醒他倒垃圾。

tell-sb-off.note: to speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong
tell-sb-off.tip: 为什么挨训用 for + doing；「挨训」常说 get told off：I got told off by my mum.
tell-sb-off.example: The manager told me off for being late again.
tell-sb-off.en: If you spoke Chinese in her lessons, she told you off.
tell-sb-off.szh: 谁在她课上说中文，她就训谁。

more.en: When Chen was nine, he'd broken the family computer, and his dad hadn't even told him off.
more.szh: 小陈九岁那年把家里的电脑弄坏了，爸爸连一句都没骂他。

go-easy-on-sb.note: to treat someone more gently than usual and not criticise them too much
go-easy-on-sb.tip: 常用在祈使句里替别人求情：Go easy on her。go easy on sth 还可以是「少吃点、少用点」：go easy on the salt。
go-easy-on-sb.example: Go easy on him — it's only his second week.
go-easy-on-sb.en: And she never went easy on anyone who forgot their homework.
go-easy-on-sb.szh: 忘带作业的人，她也从不手下留情。

more.en: Go easy on me, Chen.
more.szh: 手下留情啊，小陈。

w-marking.note: 英式说法，不可数；动词 mark 是「批改、打分」，美式多说 grade。
w-marking.en: Every night the marking piled up.
w-marking.szh: 每天晚上，要批的作业都堆成山。

have-a-sense-of-humour.note: to be able to see what is funny and to make people laugh
have-a-sense-of-humour.tip: 英式拼写 humour，美式 humor；可以加形容词：a great / dry sense of humour。
have-a-sense-of-humour.example: You need a good sense of humour if you work with teenagers.
have-a-sense-of-humour.en: She had a great sense of humour, actually.

be-scared-of.note: to be afraid of someone or something
be-scared-of.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：be scared of flying；突然被吓一跳是 get scared。
be-scared-of.example: My daughter is scared of dogs, even small ones.
be-scared-of.en: Chen was scared of her for most of his first year at secondary school.
be-scared-of.szh: 上中学第一年，小陈大半时间都很怕她。

w-aloud.note: read aloud 是「念出声」，和 loudly（音量大）不完全一样。
w-aloud.en: He'd been hiding at the back for months when she chose him to read a story aloud in front of the whole school.
w-aloud.szh: 他在最后一排躲了好几个月，结果她偏偏挑中他，让他在全校面前朗读一篇故事。

w-shed.note: bike shed 车棚；花园里放工具的小屋叫 garden shed。
w-shed.en: For two weeks he'd been practising in the bike shed at lunchtime, while his friends killed time playing cards.
w-shed.szh: 那两个星期，他每天中午都躲在车棚里练，朋友们就在一旁打牌打发时间。

w-whisper.note: 也能当名词：in a whisper（小声地）。
w-whisper.en: On the day, his hands were shaking, and she whispered, "Read at your own pace. Nobody's going anywhere."
w-whisper.szh: 到了那天，他的手一直在抖，她小声跟他说：「按你自己的节奏读，没人会走的。」

w-microphone.en: Unfortunately, she'd left the microphone on, so eight hundred students heard that too.
w-microphone.szh: 可惜她忘了关话筒，这句话八百个学生也全听见了。

more.en: Tiny microphones on the outside pick up the noise around you thousands of times a second.
more.szh: 耳机外面的小麦克风，每秒钟要把你周围的噪音收进来几千次。

look-up-to.note: to admire and respect someone, often someone older or more experienced
look-up-to.tip: 反义是 look down on（瞧不起）；说的是长期的态度，不说 I'm looking up to her。
look-up-to.example: I've always looked up to my older sister.
look-up-to.en: From then on, Chen stopped hiding from her and started looking up to her.
look-up-to.szh: 从那以后，小陈不再躲着她，而是打心底里敬重她。

get-a-feel-for-sth.zh: 摸到……的门道；找到……的感觉
get-a-feel-for-sth.note: to start to understand how to do something or how something works
get-a-feel-for-sth.tip: feel 在这里是名词，前面要有 a；也可以说 have a feel for sth（已经有感觉了，说状态）。
get-a-feel-for-sth.example: It took me a few weeks to get a feel for the new city.
get-a-feel-for-sth.en: So I assumed I'd get a feel for the wheel in an hour.
get-a-feel-for-sth.szh: 所以我以为一个小时就能摸到拉坯机的门道。

more.en: It would take them weeks to get a feel for it, but Dad was already pressing buttons that weren't in the guide.
more.szh: 他们得花好几个星期才能摸到门道，可爸爸已经在按说明上没写的按钮了。

w-collapse.note: 楼、桥、人都能 collapse；名词也是 collapse。
w-collapse.en: But the first one collapsed before I'd even noticed I was pressing too hard.
w-collapse.szh: 结果我还没发现自己用力太猛，第一个就塌了。

w-centre.note: 做陶的专门说法：把泥在转盘正中压稳。英式拼写 centre，美式 center。
w-centre.en: I hadn't centred the clay properly, so it wobbled and fell over.
w-centre.szh: 我没把泥摆正，它晃来晃去就倒了。

w-clay.note: 不可数：a piece of clay、a lump of clay。
w-clay.en: I hadn't centred the clay properly, so it wobbled and fell over.
w-clay.szh: 我没把泥摆正，它晃来晃去就倒了。

w-wobble.note: 桌子腿不平也会 wobble；形容词 wobbly。
w-wobble.en: I hadn't centred the clay properly, so it wobbled and fell over.
w-wobble.szh: 我没把泥摆正，它晃来晃去就倒了。

slow-down.note: to do something less quickly, or to become less busy
slow-down.tip: 可以不带宾语：You need to slow down；也可以带：slow the car down。反义 speed up。
slow-down.example: Slow down — I can't understand you when you talk so fast.
slow-down.en: Look, you need to slow down.

start-from-scratch.note: to begin something again from the very beginning, without using anything from before
start-from-scratch.tip: from scratch（第 39 课）也能跟别的动词：build sth from scratch、cook from scratch。
start-from-scratch.example: The file was lost, so we had to start from scratch.
start-from-scratch.en: Just leave it behind and start from scratch.

practice-makes-perfect.note: if you do something again and again, you will become very good at it
practice-makes-perfect.tip: 英式拼写里 practice 是名词，practise 是动词，这句谚语里用名词 practice。
practice-makes-perfect.example: My piano playing is still terrible, but practice makes perfect.

more.en: My little brother's learning the trumpet, and Mum keeps saying practice makes perfect.
more.szh: 我弟弟在学小号，我妈老说熟能生巧。

be-good-with-your-hands.note: to be skilful at making or repairing things
be-good-with-your-hands.tip: your 跟着人称变：good with his hands；good with people 是「会跟人打交道」，good with numbers 是「对数字在行」。
be-good-with-your-hands.example: My grandad was very good with his hands — he built our kitchen table.
be-good-with-your-hands.en: Anyway, are you good with your hands?

w-count.note: 这里不是「数数」，而是「被算进去」：That doesn't count.（那不算。）

have-a-go.note: to try to do something, often for the first time
have-a-go.tip: 英式口语；go 是名词，可以说 one more go、one last go；试着做某事用 have a go at doing sth。
have-a-go.example: I've never played golf, but I'd love to have a go.
have-a-go.en: It's ten to twelve, so have one last go.
have-a-go.szh: 现在十一点五十，最后再试一次吧。

more.en: Could you have a go at it this week?
more.szh: 你这周能试着做一下吗？

w-invitation.note: 动词 invite；接受邀请是 accept an invitation。
w-invitation.en: Hi Liu Yang, thanks for the invitation!

w-rent.note: 也能当动词：rent a flat（租房）。
w-rent.en: I'd love to come on 19 December, but I've worked out the flight would cost more than two months' rent.
w-rent.szh: 我很想 12 月 19 号回去，可我算了一下，机票比我两个月的房租还贵。

grow-up.note: to change from a child into an adult
grow-up.tip: 说在哪儿长大用 grow up in / on；名词 grown-up 是「大人」。别说 grow up a child，「养大孩子」是 bring up。
grow-up.example: I grew up in a small town by the sea.
grow-up.en: We grew up together, but to be honest, I lost touch with most of Class 3 after university.
grow-up.szh: 我们是一起长大的，可说实话，上了大学以后，我和三班大部分人都断了联系。

more.en: When I was growing up, headphones were cheap and light, and mine kept falling off on the bus.
more.szh: 我小时候，耳机又便宜又轻，我那副在公交车上老往下掉。

lose-touch-with.note: to stop talking to or writing to someone, so that you no longer know what they are doing
lose-touch-with.tip: touch 前面不加 the；反义是 keep in touch with / stay in touch with。
lose-touch-with.example: I lost touch with my university friends when I moved abroad.
lose-touch-with.en: We grew up together, but to be honest, I lost touch with most of Class 3 after university.
lose-touch-with.szh: 我们是一起长大的，可说实话，上了大学以后，我和三班大部分人都断了联系。

more.en: Maybe I've lost touch with what users actually want.
more.szh: 说不定我已经不太清楚用户真正想要什么了。

settle-down.note: to start living a quiet life in one place, often with a partner, a home and a steady job
settle-down.tip: 常带「结婚、买房、不再到处跑」的意思；对孩子说 settle down 是「安静下来」。
settle-down.example: After years of travelling, she settled down in Edinburgh.
settle-down.en: By the time I moved to the UK last year, half of you had settled down in Shanghai or Shenzhen.
settle-down.szh: 等我去年搬到英国的时候，你们一半人都已经在上海或深圳安家了。

more.en: Everyone, settle down.
more.szh: 大家都冷静点。

hear-from.note: to get a message, letter, email or call from someone
hear-from.tip: hear from sb 是对方联系了你；hear about sth 是听说某事；hear of sb 是听说过有这么个人。
hear-from.example: Have you heard from the bank about your loan yet?
hear-from.en: Still, I've heard from a few people on WeChat, and some of the news is amazing.
hear-from.szh: 不过，微信上倒是有几个人跟我联系过，有些消息真让人想不到。

w-twins.note: 单数 twin：my twin sister（我的双胞胎姐妹）。
w-twins.en: And Zhang Min had had twins before most of us had even found a job.
w-twins.szh: 张敏呢，我们大多数人还没找到工作，她就已经生了一对双胞胎。

remind-sb-of.note: to make someone remember or think about something or someone
remind-sb-of.tip: remind sb of sth 是「让人想起」；remind sb to do 是「提醒某人去做」，别混。
remind-sb-of.example: This song always reminds me of my first car.
remind-sb-of.en: Your old photos reminded me of so many things I hadn't thought about for years.
remind-sb-of.szh: 你发的老照片，让我想起了好多很多年都没想起过的事。

w-fascinated.note: 比 interested 强得多，说人；fascinating 是「让人着迷的」，说事物。
w-fascinated.en: I was fascinated by the way that man pulled noodles by hand.
w-fascinated.szh: 那个大叔手工拉面的样子，我当年看得入了迷。

w-owe.note: owe sb sth：I owe you one.（我欠你一个人情。）
w-owe.en: Oh, by the way, I still owe you ten yuan for noodles.
w-owe.szh: 哦对了，我还欠你十块钱面钱。

w-torn.note: tear（撕）的过去分词：tear – tore – torn。
w-torn.en: And do you remember my Harry Potter book, the one with the torn cover?
w-torn.szh: 还有，你记得我那本《哈利·波特》吗？封面破了的那本。

w-lend.note: 过去式、过去分词 lent。借出是 lend，借入是 borrow。
w-lend.en: It went missing in our final year, just after I'd lent it to someone in the class.
w-lend.szh: 毕业那年它不见了，就在我把它借给班上某个人之后。

get-together.note: to meet in order to spend time together or do something together
get-together.tip: 和谁聚用 with：get together with old friends；名词 get-together 是「小聚会」。
get-together.example: We should get together for a drink after the holidays.
get-together.en: Anyway, here's my idea: next time, why don't we get together online, so I can join too?
get-together.szh: 总之，我有个主意：下次我们在网上聚一聚吧，这样我也能参加。

w-roundabout.note: 英国路口很常见；美式说 traffic circle。
w-roundabout.en: Now I cycle to Ruth's studio every Saturday, and I love it, apart from one thing: the big roundabout near the station.
w-roundabout.szh: 现在我每个星期六都骑车去 Ruth 的工作室，骑得很开心，只有一件事除外：车站附近那个大环岛。

w-fear.note: the fear 加 the，指的是「那种熟悉的害怕」；fear of sth 对……的恐惧。
w-fear.en: As soon as I see it, the fear kicks in.
w-fear.szh: 我一看到它，心里就开始发怵。

w-chain.note: 也是「链子」：a gold chain；连锁店是 a chain of shops。
w-chain.en: So I make an excuse, usually something about my chain, then get off and walk.
w-chain.szh: 于是我就找个借口，一般是说链条有点毛病，然后下车推着走。

w-cousin.note: 英语不分堂、表、男女、长幼，都叫 cousin。
w-cousin.en: My cousin had handed it down to me, along with a helmet that was far too big.
w-cousin.szh: 那是表哥骑过传给我的，还附送一个大得离谱的头盔。

keep-going.note: to continue doing something, especially when it is difficult
keep-going.tip: 鼓励别人时常用；后面也能接 doing：keep going straight on。
keep-going.example: You're nearly at the top — keep going!
keep-going.en: Every evening after dinner, Dad ran behind me in the car park, holding the seat and shouting, "Keep going!"
keep-going.szh: 每天晚饭后，爸爸都在停车场里跟在我后面跑，扶着车座喊：「继续骑！」

fall-off.note: to fall from something such as a bike, a horse or a wall
fall-off.tip: 从什么上掉下来就直接加宾语：fall off a bike；原地摔倒是 fall over。
fall-off.example: My phone fell off the table and landed in my coffee.
fall-off.en: I fell off eleven times — I counted.
fall-off.szh: 我摔下来十一次——我数过。

more.en: When I was growing up, headphones were cheap and light, and mine kept falling off on the bus.
more.szh: 我小时候，耳机又便宜又轻，我那副在公交车上老往下掉。

lose-your-balance.note: to become unable to stay standing or sitting steadily, so that you start to fall
lose-your-balance.tip: your 跟着人称变：lose my / his balance；反过来「保持平衡」是 keep your balance。
lose-your-balance.example: She lost her balance on the ice and sat down hard.
lose-your-balance.en: I lost my balance on every corner, and I learned the hard way that you can't stop a bike with your feet.
lose-your-balance.szh: 每到拐弯我就失去平衡，吃了不少苦头才明白：用脚是刹不住自行车的。

more.en: Some watches can even tell when you lose your balance and fall over.
more.szh: 有些手表甚至能发现你没站稳、摔倒了。

learn-the-hard-way.zh: 吃了苦头才学会；从教训中学到
learn-the-hard-way.note: to learn something by making mistakes or having a bad experience
learn-the-hard-way.tip: 后面常跟 that + 句子，说学到了什么；英式过去式也可以写 learnt。
learn-the-hard-way.example: I learned the hard way that you should always save your work.
learn-the-hard-way.en: I lost my balance on every corner, and I learned the hard way that you can't stop a bike with your feet.
learn-the-hard-way.szh: 每到拐弯我就失去平衡，吃了不少苦头才明白：用脚是刹不住自行车的。

pluck-up-the-courage.note: to make yourself brave enough to do something that frightens you
pluck-up-the-courage.tip: 后面接 to do；也可以省掉 the：pluck up courage。
pluck-up-the-courage.example: It took me a week to pluck up the courage to ask for a pay rise.
pluck-up-the-courage.en: Then one evening, I finally plucked up the courage to look back.
pluck-up-the-courage.szh: 后来有一天晚上，我终于鼓起勇气回头看了一眼。

w-metre.note: 英式拼写 metre，美式 meter；ten metres away 是「十米开外」。
w-metre.en: Dad was standing in the middle of the car park, ten metres away.
w-metre.szh: 爸爸站在停车场中间，离我有十米远。

let-go-of.note: to stop holding something or someone
let-go-of.tip: 后面有宾语时用 let go of sth；没有宾语只说 let go：Let go! let 的过去式、过去分词都是 let。
let-go-of.example: Don't let go of my hand in the crowd.
let-go-of.en: He'd let go of the seat long before.

more.en: Let go of the mouse, Hannah.
more.szh: Hannah，把鼠标放下。

w-folder.note: 电脑里的文件夹也叫 folder。
w-folder.en: I used to draw on everything, and I've hung on to a folder of those drawings for forty-two years.
w-folder.szh: 那时候我见什么画什么，那一夹子画，我留了整整四十二年。

w-solicitor.note: 英国律师分两种：solicitor 多做咨询、文书，barrister 出庭辩护；美式统称 lawyer。
w-solicitor.en: But my father was a solicitor, and his father had been one too, so I followed in their footsteps and did law.
w-solicitor.szh: 可我父亲是律师，祖父也是，于是我就走了他们的老路，学了法律。

follow-in-sb-s-footsteps.note: to do the same job or the same things as someone, often a parent, did before you
follow-in-sb-s-footsteps.tip: sb's 跟着人称变：follow in my father's footsteps / in their footsteps；footsteps 一定用复数。
follow-in-sb-s-footsteps.example: Her mum is a doctor, and she wants to follow in her footsteps.
follow-in-sb-s-footsteps.en: But my father was a solicitor, and his father had been one too, so I followed in their footsteps and did law.
follow-in-sb-s-footsteps.szh: 可我父亲是律师，祖父也是，于是我就走了他们的老路，学了法律。

more.en: My dad was a night-shift engineer, and now I'm following in his footsteps.
more.szh: 我爸以前是上夜班的工程师，现在我也算接了他的班。

at-the-time.note: at a particular moment in the past, especially when things seemed different from how they seem now
at-the-time.tip: 常暗示「现在看法变了」；别和 at a time（一次、每次）混：one at a time。
at-the-time.example: At the time I thought it was a good idea, but now I'm not so sure.
at-the-time.en: At the time, it seemed like the sensible choice.
at-the-time.szh: 在当时，这看起来是最稳妥的选择。

more.en: "Buying it seemed like a good idea at the time," she said.
more.szh: 「当时觉得买它是个好主意。」她说。

w-sensible.en: At the time, it seemed like the sensible choice.
w-sensible.szh: 在当时，这看起来是最稳妥的选择。

have-doubts-about-sth.note: to feel not sure whether something is right or true
have-doubts-about-sth.tip: doubts 常用复数；程度可以加 serious：have serious doubts about sth。
have-doubts-about-sth.example: I'm starting to have doubts about this plan.
have-doubts-about-sth.en: I didn't hate the job, but I had doubts about it every Monday morning.
have-doubts-about-sth.szh: 我并不讨厌这份工作，可一到星期一早上，我就怀疑自己是不是选错了。

more.en: To be honest, I had serious doubts about the whole idea.
more.szh: 说实话，我很怀疑这么做到底有没有用。

make-a-career-change.note: to leave one kind of work and start doing a completely different kind
make-a-career-change.tip: 从什么转到什么用 from … to …；career 是长期的职业道路，不是某一份工作（job）。
make-a-career-change.example: At thirty-eight, he made a career change from banking to teaching.
make-a-career-change.en: At forty-five, I finally made a career change.
make-a-career-change.szh: 四十五岁那年，我终于转了行。

w-arch.note: 英国很多老铁路桥下的拱洞被改成了酒吧、车行、工作室，火车一过，屋里就晃。
w-arch.en: This arch dates back to 1870, and the rent was a bargain.
w-arch.szh: 这间桥洞工作室是 1870 年建的，房租便宜得很。

w-salary.note: 白领按月或按年拿的固定工资；按小时、按周拿的叫 wages。
w-salary.en: But in my first year, I earned less than my old monthly salary.
w-salary.szh: 可第一年我挣的钱，还不如以前一个月的工资。

dream-of-doing.note: to think a lot about something you would like to do
dream-of-doing.tip: of 后面接 doing 或名词，不接 to do；英式过去式也常写 dreamt。
dream-of-doing.example: When I was a kid, I dreamed of becoming a pilot.
dream-of-doing.en: And I wish I hadn't spent all those years dreaming of making things instead of making them.
dream-of-doing.szh: 我还后悔，这么多年光想着做东西，却一直没动手去做。

make-every-minute-count.note: to use all the time you have in a useful or enjoyable way
make-every-minute-count.tip: count 在这里是「有价值、算数」；也说 make every second / day count。
make-every-minute-count.example: We only have two days in Rome, so let's make every minute count.
make-every-minute-count.en: So now I try to make every minute at the wheel count.
make-every-minute-count.szh: 所以现在，我坐在拉坯机前的每一分钟都不想浪费。

w-lease.note: 租约是 the lease on 某处房子；签租约 sign a lease。
w-lease.en: It's the only reason I read the lease on this place properly.
w-lease.szh: 要不是学过法律，我也不会把这里的租约读得那么仔细。

w-psychology.note: p 不发音，读作 /saɪˈkɒlədʒi/；心理学家 psychologist。
w-psychology.en: I'm Alan Price, and I teach psychology here.
w-psychology.szh: 我是 Alan Price，在这儿教心理学。

come-to-mind.note: if something comes to mind, you suddenly think of it or remember it
come-to-mind.tip: 主语是被想起的东西，不是人：Nothing comes to mind，不说 I come to mind。
come-to-mind.example: When I think of summer, long evenings in the garden come to mind.
come-to-mind.en: Think of one lesson from school — the first one that comes to mind — and shout it out.
come-to-mind.szh: 想一节上学时的课，脑子里冒出来的第一节就行，大声说出来。

more.en: "But now, when I think about sleep, the first thing that comes to mind is a number."
more.szh: 「可现在一想到睡觉，我脑子里冒出来的第一个东西就是一个数字。」

stick-in-your-mind.zh: 让人一直记得；印在脑子里
stick-in-your-mind.note: if something sticks in your mind, you remember it for a long time
stick-in-your-mind.tip: 主语是被记住的事；stick 的过去式、过去分词是 stuck。
stick-in-your-mind.example: One thing he said in that meeting has stuck in my mind.
stick-in-your-mind.en: Well, a lesson sticks in your mind when it makes you feel something: surprise, fear, even embarrassment.
stick-in-your-mind.szh: 其实，一节课要是能让你有点感觉——惊讶、害怕，甚至是难堪——你就会一直记得它。

more.en: But what's stuck in my mind most is the bus.
more.szh: 不过我印象最深的，还是公交车。

w-embarrassment.note: 形容词 embarrassed（人觉得尴尬）、embarrassing（事情让人尴尬）。拼写注意双 r、双 s。
w-embarrassment.en: Well, a lesson sticks in your mind when it makes you feel something: surprise, fear, even embarrassment.
w-embarrassment.szh: 其实，一节课要是能让你有点感觉——惊讶、害怕，甚至是难堪——你就会一直记得它。

take-notes.note: to write down information while you are listening to someone or reading something
take-notes.tip: notes 用复数；动词用 take，不用 write：take notes，也说 make notes。
take-notes.example: Can someone take notes during the meeting?
take-notes.en: Students who take notes by hand remember more than students who type.
take-notes.szh: 手写笔记的学生，比打字的记得多。

more.en: Dad took notes on the back of an envelope lying on the table.
more.szh: 爸爸拿起桌上的一个信封，在背面记笔记。

go-over.note: to look at or study something again carefully
go-over.tip: 后面接要检查、复习的东西：go over your notes / the figures；go over to 是「走过去」。
go-over.example: Let's go over the plan one more time before the client arrives.
go-over.en: And going over your notes the night before an exam doesn't actually help much.
go-over.szh: 考试前一晚把笔记过一遍，其实没多大用。

w-chemistry.note: ch 读 /k/；化学家 chemist，英式里 chemist 还是「药店」。
w-chemistry.en: Which brings me to Mr Jenkins, my Year 9 chemistry teacher.
w-chemistry.szh: 这就说到 Jenkins 老师了，他是我初三的化学老师。

w-experiment.note: 做实验是 do / carry out an experiment。
w-experiment.en: In 1994, he was showing us an experiment when he accidentally set fire to a bench.
w-experiment.szh: 1994 年，他给我们做一个实验，结果不小心把实验台点着了。

w-accidentally.note: = by accident；反义 on purpose（故意）。
w-accidentally.en: In 1994, he was showing us an experiment when he accidentally set fire to a bench.
w-accidentally.szh: 1994 年，他给我们做一个实验，结果不小心把实验台点着了。

make-an-impression-on.note: to make someone notice and remember you
make-an-impression-on.tip: 可以加形容词：make a good / bad / big impression on sb；第一印象是 first impression。
make-an-impression-on.example: She made a great impression on the interview panel.
make-an-impression-on.en: He made an impression on the whole class, and after that, he held our attention with every topic.
make-an-impression-on.szh: 全班都对他印象深刻，从那以后，他讲什么我们都听得聚精会神。

hold-sb-s-attention.note: to keep someone interested so that they keep listening or watching
hold-sb-s-attention.tip: sb's 跟着人称变：hold our / their attention；「引起注意」是 get / catch sb's attention。
hold-sb-s-attention.example: It's hard to hold children's attention for more than ten minutes.
hold-sb-s-attention.en: He made an impression on the whole class, and after that, he held our attention with every topic.
hold-sb-s-attention.szh: 全班都对他印象深刻，从那以后，他讲什么我们都听得聚精会神。

w-memorable.note: 来自 memory；a memorable day 难忘的一天。
w-memorable.en: And if only I could make my own lectures that memorable.
w-memorable.szh: 要是我自己的讲座也能让人记得这么牢就好了。

w-kiln.note: 读 /kɪln/，n 要发出来；陶器要放进 kiln 里高温烧（fire）。
w-kiln.en: Bad news from the kiln, I'm afraid: your mug for Tom has cracked.
w-kiln.szh: 恐怕是个坏消息：你给 Tom 做的杯子在窑里裂了。

be-gutted.note: to feel very disappointed and sad about something
be-gutted.tip: 英式口语，非常常用；比 disappointed 语气重得多，正式场合别用。
be-gutted.example: He was gutted when his team lost in the last minute.

more.en: I was gutted.
more.szh: 我难受死了。

go-wrong.note: to stop happening or working in the way you planned
go-wrong.tip: 某东西出了毛病用 with：go wrong with sth；Everything went wrong（诸事不顺）。
go-wrong.example: Something went wrong with the printer, so I couldn't print the tickets.
go-wrong.en: Do you want to know what went wrong?
go-wrong.szh: 想知道哪儿出问题了吗？

more.en: Well, what could go wrong?
more.szh: 嗯，还能出什么岔子呢？

w-evenly.note: 形容词 even（平的、均匀的）。
w-evenly.en: And if the handle hadn't been so thick, the clay would have dried evenly.
w-evenly.szh: 还有，把手要是没那么厚，泥也会干得均匀些。

that-explains-it.note: something you say when you suddenly understand why something happened
that-explains-it.tip: 口语里也常说 That explains a lot.（这就全明白了），带一点调侃。
that-explains-it.example: "I left the window open all night." "That explains it — the room's freezing."

more.en: And if your flatmates suddenly stopped doing their chores, well, that explains it.
more.szh: 要是你的室友突然不做家务了，嗯，原因就在这儿。

w-glue.en: Can I just glue the crack, or will it fall apart?
w-glue.szh: 我拿胶把裂缝粘上行吗？还是会散架？

it-s-not-the-end-of-the-world.text: it's not the end of the world
it-s-not-the-end-of-the-world.zh: 又不是天塌下来了；没那么严重
it-s-not-the-end-of-the-world.note: something you say to tell someone that a problem is not very serious
it-s-not-the-end-of-the-world.tip: 用来安慰别人或自己；也说 It won't be the end of the world if …
it-s-not-the-end-of-the-world.example: You failed one test — it's not the end of the world.
it-s-not-the-end-of-the-world.en: Honestly, it's not the end of the world.
it-s-not-the-end-of-the-world.szh: 说真的，又不是天塌下来了。

what-a-shame.note: something you say when you are disappointed or sorry about something
what-a-shame.tip: 这里的 shame 是「可惜」，不是「羞耻」；也说 What a pity。
what-a-shame.example: You can't come to the party? What a shame!

never-mind.note: something you say to show that something is not important, or that you will stop worrying about it
never-mind.tip: 对别人的道歉说「没关系」用 That's OK / No problem 更自然；Never mind 多是自己放下、叫对方别在意。
never-mind.example: Never mind — we can take the next train.

w-wrap.note: 包礼物 wrap a present；包装纸 wrapping paper。
w-wrap.en: Quick update — I wrapped the cracked mug anyway and gave it to Tom.
w-wrap.szh: 汇报一下——我最后还是把那个裂了的杯子包好送给了 Tom。

go-back-to-college.note: to start studying again at a college after a long time away from education
go-back-to-college.tip: 英国的 college 常指继续教育学院（成人、职业和 A-level 课程），和 university 不同；college 前面不加 the。
go-back-to-college.example: After ten years in sales, she decided to go back to college and study nursing.
go-back-to-college.en: Now, some good news for anyone thinking of going back to college.
go-back-to-college.szh: 下面这条好消息，送给正在考虑回学校读书的各位。

more.en: "It's like going back to college at sixty-four," he said.
more.szh: 「这就跟 64 岁又回学校念书一样。」他说。

w-figures.note: figure 在报道里常是「数字」，复数 figures；sales figures 销售数据。
w-figures.en: The number of students over thirty at Northfield College has gone up by eighteen per cent in two years, according to new figures.
w-figures.szh: 最新数据显示，北田学院三十岁以上的学生人数两年里涨了百分之十八。

enrol-on-sth.note: to officially join a course so that you can study on it
enrol-on-sth.tip: 英式拼写 enrol（一个 l），但 enrolled、enrolling 双写 l；英式用 on，美式说 enroll in。
enrol-on-sth.example: I've enrolled on an evening course in photography.
enrol-on-sth.en: She enrolled on an A-level maths course last September, a few months after her husband had died.
enrol-on-sth.szh: 去年九月，丈夫去世几个月后，她报了 A-level 数学课。

more.en: If you enrolled on our beta programme in October, the fix is already there.
more.szh: 如果你十月报名参加了我们的测试计划，修复已经自动完成了。

w-taster.note: 英式说法：a taster session / class，先免费体验一次。
w-taster.en: First, she took the course for a test drive at a free taster evening.
w-taster.szh: 她先去参加了一个免费的体验晚课，试了试这门课。

drop-out-of.note: to leave a school, university or course before you have finished it
drop-out-of.tip: 名词 dropout 是「退学的人」；不说 drop out from。
drop-out-of.example: He dropped out of his law course after six months.
drop-out-of.en: Dev Mistry, who's thirty-four, dropped out of university in 2012 after a year of computer science.
drop-out-of.szh: Dev Mistry 今年三十四岁，2012 年读了一年计算机专业后就退了学。

more.en: I nearly dropped out of the whole project twice.
more.szh: 我两次差点就不干了。

w-warehouse.note: ware 是「货物」，house 是「房子」，合起来就是放货的地方。
w-warehouse.en: These days he works night shifts at a warehouse to pay the rent.
w-warehouse.szh: 现在他在一家仓库上夜班，挣钱交房租。

fit-sth-in.note: to find time to do something or see someone
fit-sth-in.tip: 围着什么安排用 around：fit sth in around work；英式过去式常用 fitted。
fit-sth-in.example: The doctor is busy, but she can fit you in at four.
fit-sth-in.en: He fits his coding course in around them.
fit-sth-in.szh: 编程课就挤在夜班的空当里上。

a-second-chance.zh: 第二次机会；重来的机会
a-second-chance.note: an opportunity to try something again after you failed or missed it the first time
a-second-chance.tip: 常和 give、get、deserve 连用：give sb a second chance。
a-second-chance.en: "Most of our adult students want a second chance, not a certificate," said the college director, Sunita Rao.
a-second-chance.szh: 「我们大多数成年学生想要的是第二次机会，而不是一张证书，」学院院长 Sunita Rao 说。

it-s-never-too-late-to.note: used to say that you can still do something, even if you are older or it seems late
it-s-never-too-late-to.tip: 后面接动词原形；也可以单说一句：It's never too late!
it-s-never-too-late-to.example: It's never too late to learn to swim.
it-s-never-too-late-to.en: It's never too late to start, and I think the numbers will keep rising."
it-s-never-too-late-to.szh: 什么时候开始都不晚，我觉得人数还会继续涨。」

w-revise.note: 英式意思是「复习」，美式多说 review / study；revise 也有「修改」的意思。

be-hard-on-yourself.note: to criticise yourself too much or expect too much from yourself
be-hard-on-yourself.tip: 对别人苛刻是 be hard on sb：Don't be so hard on him。常和 so、too 连用。
be-hard-on-yourself.example: You made one small mistake — stop being so hard on yourself.
be-hard-on-yourself.en: Don't be so hard on yourself.

more.en: So if you thought you'd pressed the wrong button, please don't be hard on yourself.
more.szh: 所以要是你以为自己按错了键，千万别自责。

move-on.note: to stop thinking about something bad that happened and start thinking about other things
move-on.tip: 也可以是「（换个话题）接着往下说」：Let's move on to the next point。从什么里走出来用 from。
move-on.example: It's been a year since they broke up — it's time to move on.
move-on.en: Cry for one evening, then move on.
move-on.szh: 哭一个晚上，然后就翻篇。

more.en: Let's move on to the one-star reviews.
more.szh: 我们接着看一星差评。

w-survive.note: survive worse 是「比这更糟的都熬过来了」；名词 survival。
w-survive.szh: 更糟的你都熬过来了，记得吧？

be-for-the-best.zh: （结果）是最好的安排；塞翁失马
be-for-the-best.note: if something is for the best, it seems bad now but will have a good result later
be-for-the-best.tip: 常加 all：It's all for the best；多用来安慰别人或自己。
be-for-the-best.example: I didn't get the job, but maybe it's for the best.
be-for-the-best.en: Believe it or not, it'll all be for the best.
be-for-the-best.szh: 信不信由你，这一切到头来都是好事。

more.en: But it was all for the best, because the second time, I met Chen.
more.szh: 不过结果反倒是好事，因为第二次想放弃的时候，我认识了小陈。

w-computer-science.note: 大学专业名称，不加 the；读这个专业：study computer science。
w-computer-science.en: If you hadn't failed that exam, you'd never have chosen computer science.
w-computer-science.szh: 要不是那次考砸了，你根本不会去选计算机。

a-turning-point.note: a time when an important change happens, especially one that makes things better
a-turning-point.tip: 在什么中的转折点用 in：a turning point in my life；常和 be、become、mark 连用。
a-turning-point.example: Moving to London was a turning point in her career.
a-turning-point.en: And that was a real turning point.
a-turning-point.szh: 那可是一个真正的转折点。

w-believe-in.note: believe sb 是相信某人说的话；believe in sb 是相信这个人行。
w-believe-in.en: About Mrs Zhou: she's strict with you because she believes in you.
w-believe-in.szh: 关于周老师：她对你严，是因为她相信你行。

w-properly.note: 英式口语很常用：Do it properly!（好好做！）
w-properly.en: I should have thanked her properly before I left.
w-properly.szh: 我毕业前本该好好谢谢她的。

more.en: She checks her score as soon as she wakes up, before she's even opened her eyes properly.
more.szh: 她一醒就看分数，眼睛都还没完全睁开。

stand-up-for-yourself.note: to defend yourself when someone treats you badly or unfairly
stand-up-for-yourself.tip: yourself 跟着人称变：stand up for myself；为别人出头是 stand up for sb。
stand-up-for-yourself.example: You need to stand up for yourself in meetings, or people will ignore you.
stand-up-for-yourself.en: I also wish I'd stood up for myself more, so please start now.
stand-up-for-yourself.szh: 我还后悔自己当年没多为自己说句话，所以请你从现在就开始。

w-noodles.note: 通常用复数；一碗面 a bowl of noodles。
w-noodles.en: But treat yourself to a second bowl of noodles sometimes — the ones in England aren't that good.
w-noodles.szh: 不过偶尔也犒劳一下自己，多吃一碗面——英国的面可没那么好吃。

make-time-for-sb.zh: 抽出时间陪（某人）；为……留出时间
make-time-for-sb.note: to find time to spend with someone or to do something, even when you are busy
make-time-for-sb.tip: 后面也能接事情：make time for exercise；比 have time for 更主动，是「挤出来的时间」。
make-time-for-sb.example: However busy you are, make time for your kids.
make-time-for-sb.en: And make time for Mum and Dad's Sunday phone calls.
make-time-for-sb.szh: 还有，爸妈每个星期天打来的电话，一定要抽时间好好接。

w-realise.note: 英式拼写 realise，美式 realize。
w-realise.en: If only I'd realised that sooner.
w-realise.szh: 要是我早点明白这一点就好了。

w-cactus.en: But Tom says a cactus counts as a pet.
w-cactus.szh: 不过 Tom 说，仙人掌也算宠物。

w-technology.note: 重音在第二个音节 /tekˈnɒlədʒi/；形容词 technical。
w-technology.en: Chen's parents in Chengdu have never really been into technology.
w-technology.szh: 小陈在成都的爸妈，对科技产品一直不怎么感冒。

struggle-with.note: to find something very difficult to do, use or deal with
struggle-with.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：struggle with maths / struggle with getting up early；想努力做到某事用 struggle to do。
struggle-with.example: I always struggle with the self-service machines at the supermarket.
struggle-with.en: His dad has struggled with his smartphone for years, and his mum only uses hers to check the weather.
struggle-with.szh: 他爸爸跟智能手机较劲了好几年，他妈妈的手机只拿来看天气。

w-tablet.note: 原意是「药片」，看上下文分辨。
w-tablet.en: So in October, Chen splashed out £560 on two tablets, one for himself and one for them.
w-tablet.szh: 所以十月份，小陈一咬牙花了 560 英镑买了两台平板，一台自己用，一台给爸妈。

set-up.note: to get a machine or a piece of equipment ready so that it can be used
set-up.tip: 宾语是代词时放中间：set it up；也可以说「创办」：set up a company。过去式、过去分词都是 set。
set-up.example: It took me an hour to set up the new printer.
set-up.en: He spent the whole of Saturday afternoon setting up the one for his parents.
set-up.szh: 星期六整个下午，他都在给爸妈那台做设置。

more.en: He set up our first test version in a weekend, and Arjun built the server from Bangalore.
more.szh: 他一个周末就搭好了第一个测试版，Arjun 在班加罗尔把服务器做了出来。

w-icon.en: In order to make it as simple as possible, he made all the icons bigger.
w-icon.szh: 为了让它用起来越简单越好，他把所有图标都调大了。
